docs.title: ☀️ SAOS
docs.text:
Solar Adaptive Optics Simulator — a Python-first, free-threaded simulation framework for wide-field solar AO.

📚 Documentation 🚀 Get Started 💻 GitHub

docs.title: Free-Threaded Python
docs.text: Built for Python 3.13t. Scales across CPU cores with no GIL bottleneck — essential for solar AO's wide-field computations.

docs.title: LightPath Abstraction
docs.text: Each line of sight is an independent LightPath — a transparent pipeline connecting atmosphere, DM, and WFS.

docs.title: Solar & Night-Time AO
docs.text: Supports extended sources (Sun) via CorrelatingShackHartmann and point sources via classical ShackHartmann.

docs.title: PyTorch Accelerated
docs.text: Heavy image and FFT operations run on PyTorch — CPU today, GPU-ready tomorrow.

docs.title: Where to go next?
docs.text:
Installation Set up your Python 3.13t environment and install SAOS. Introduction tutorial Step-by-step notebook: build your first SCAO simulation. API Reference Full documentation of every class and method.

SAOS is based on OOPAO by Cédric Taïssir Héritier. The LightPath architecture and solar AO extensions are the main new contributions of SAOS.

docs.title: Installation Guideline
docs.text:
This guide covers the recommended installation procedure for SAOS, targeting a Linux environment (e.g., Ubuntu 24). SAOS requires Python >= 3.10. Since it propagates the light paths in threads, a free-threaded Python (no GIL) is highly recommended: with the GIL enabled the results are the same but the light paths do not run in parallel (SAOS logs a notice at import). Tested configuration: Python 3.13.9t, torch 2.11 (CUDA 13.0), h5py 3.16, pyzmq 27.1, pvlib 0.15.

Note on free-threading: torch support for 3.13t is experimental and PyTorch is moving its free-threaded wheels to 3.14t. PYTHON_GIL=0 also forces extensions that do not declare free-threading support (OpenCV, astropy, pyzmq) to run without the GIL.

docs.title: 1. Prerequisites (Ubuntu)
docs.text:
Install the necessary system dependencies required to build Python and other scientific packages:

sudo apt update
sudo apt install -y build-essential curl git libssl-dev zlib1g-dev \
libbz2-dev libreadline-dev libsqlite3-dev wget llvm \
libncursesw5-dev xz-utils tk-dev libxml2-dev libxmlsec1-dev libffi-dev liblzma-dev

docs.title: 2. Python Environment Setup
docs.text: We recommend using pyenv to manage your Python versions and virtual environments.

docs.title: Install pyenv and pyenv-virtualenv
docs.text:
Follow the official pyenv installation instructions or run the installer:

curl https://pyenv.run | bash
Make sure to add pyenv to your ~/.bashrc or ~/.profile as instructed by the installer.

docs.title: Install Python 3.13 (Free-Threaded)
docs.text:
Install the free-threaded version of Python 3.13 (or newer) and create a virtual environment:

pyenv install 3.13.9t
pyenv virtualenv 3.13.9t venv_saos
pyenv activate venv_saos

To optimize the Python execution, ensure you upgrade pip and disable the limited API for CMake packages:

pip install --upgrade pip
export CMAKE_ARGS="-DPYTHON3_LIMITED_API=OFF"

Note: You can add export PYTHON_GIL=0 to your ~/.bashrc to ensure the Global Interpreter Lock is disabled when running the free-threaded version.

docs.title: 3. Clone and Install SAOS
docs.text:
Clone the SAOS repository and install it in editable mode (-e) so you can modify the source code easily.

mkdir -p ~/projects
cd ~/projects

# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/nrodlin/SAOS.git
cd SAOS

# Checkout to the development branch (if required)
git checkout develop

# Install SAOS (editable) with its runtime dependencies
pip install --prefer-binary -e .

# Optional: documentation (mkdocs) and validation-suite tools (pytest, pytest-timeout, pyyaml, psutil, ruff, jupyter)
pip install --prefer-binary -r requirements.txt

The validation suite is described in ci/README.md (ci/run_ci.sh fast, or python -m pytest tests -m fast). torch runs on the CPU by default; a CUDA build of torch is optional and is used automatically when torch.cuda.is_available().

Free-threaded builds and wheels: use --prefer-binary. On a free-threaded Python the newest release of several dependencies is often published only as source (e.g. scipy 1.18, matplotlib 3.11.2, pyzmq 27.2 at the time of writing), and pip would try to compile it (scipy then fails without a Fortran compiler). --prefer-binary picks the newest version with a free-threaded wheel instead (checked for 3.13t: numpy 2.4, scipy 1.17.1, matplotlib 3.11.1, pyzmq 27.1.0, torch 2.12).

Packages built from source: opencv-contrib-python and h5py have no free-threaded wheels, so pip compiles them. OpenCV is the long one (of the order of one hour on a 12-core laptop); it needs the build tools of section 1, cmake, and the CMAKE_ARGS="-DPYTHON3_LIMITED_API=OFF" exported in section 2. For h5py, see the optional HDF5 build below. The compiled wheels stay in pip's cache, so later environments install them in seconds.

The runtime dependencies (h5py, joblib, matplotlib, numpy, opencv-contrib-python, pvlib, pyzmq, scipy, torch) are declared in setup.cfg and installed by pip. A non-editable install (pip install . or a wheel built with pip wheel . --no-deps) contains every subpackage, so SAOS also works outside the repository.

docs.title: Solar images
docs.text:
ExtendedSource uses solar continuum images at 500 nm and 680 nm (370 MB in total). They are not part of the package: they are published in Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23821204 (CC BY 4.0), and SAOS keeps them in a local data directory:

  • $SAOS_DATA_DIR when the variable is set;
  • otherwise ~/.cache/SAOS ($XDG_CACHE_HOME/SAOS).

Download them once after installing SAOS:

saos-download-data            # or: python -m SAOS.data
saos-download-data --verify   # also check the MD5 checksum of the files already present

If a file is missing, ExtendedSource downloads it the first time it is needed (the MD5 checksum is always verified). On a cluster, download them once into a shared directory and export SAOS_DATA_DIR on every node. Images passed with img_path are read directly and need no download.

docs.title: 4. Additional Dependencies
docs.text: h5py (data files, M7 discrete models) and pyzmq (telemetry streaming) are installed with SAOS.

docs.title: Compiling HDF5 and h5py from source (Optional)
docs.text:
If you encounter issues with pre-compiled h5py binaries, you can compile HDF5 and h5py from source:

# 1. Compile HDF5
git clone https://github.com/HDFGroup/hdf5.git
cd hdf5
git checkout hdf5-1_14_3
mkdir build && cd build
cmake .. -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=$HOME/hdf5-install -DHDF5_ENABLE_THREADSAFE=ON -DHDF5_BUILD_CPP_LIB=OFF -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON
make -j$(nproc)
make install
cd ../..

# 2. Compile h5py against the custom HDF5
git clone https://github.com/h5py/h5py.git
cd h5py
export HDF5_DIR=$HOME/hdf5-install
pip install .

You are now ready to run your first simulation! Head over to the Tutorials section to learn the basics of SAOS.

docs.title: Model
docs.text:
The atmosphere is a stack of \(N_L\) thin turbulent layers with von Kármán statistics (see Layer for the statistics of one layer). Layers are independent, horizontally stationary and move rigidly ("frozen flow", Taylor hypothesis) at a constant velocity. Propagation is geometric: the phase seen along a line of sight is the sum of the layer phases sampled at the point where the line crosses each layer (near-field approximation, no Fresnel propagation, no scintillation).

Conventions. The reference wavelength of the screens is \(\lambda_0 = 500\) nm. Layer screens are stored as phase in rad at 500 nm; the value returned by getOPD is an OPD in m. Sky coordinates of a source are \([\rho, \theta]\) with \(\rho\) in arcsec and \(\theta\) in degrees, giving \(x = \rho\cos\theta\) along the columns and \(y = \rho\sin\theta\) along the rows of the screens (the same frame is used for wind directions, DM misregistration and the chromatic shift). The wind direction is the direction towards which the turbulence moves in that frame.

docs.title: Layer scaling
docs.text:
With the zenith angle \(z\) and fractional weights \(w_i\) (\(\sum_i w_i = 1\), fractionalR0), layer \(i\) is built with

\[ r_{0,i} = r_0\,\cos^{3/5}(z)\; w_i^{-3/5}, \qquad h_i' = \frac{h_i}{\cos z}, \]

so that \(\sum_i r_{0,i}^{-5/3} = r_0^{-5/3}\cos^{-1}(z)\), i.e. the total Fried parameter is the zenith \(r_0\) scaled to the airmass \(1/\cos z\) (plane-parallel atmosphere). A layer with \(w_i = 0\) gets \(r_{0,i}=\infty\) and a null screen. The slant altitude \(h_i'\) is used for the footprint geometry. The pupil is not foreshortened, and neither the wind speed nor \(L_0\) are scaled with \(z\). The attribute layer.fractionalR0 stores the resulting \(r_{0,i}\) in metres (not the fraction).

docs.title: Metapupil and sampling
docs.text:
The layer pixel is the pupil pixel, \(\delta = D/N\), where \(N\) is the telescope resolution. The part of the layer seen by the field of view (FoV, diameter in arcsec taken from the telescope) is

\[ D_{fov,i} = D + 2\,h_i'\tan(\mathrm{FoV}/2), \qquad n_{pix,i} = N + 2\left\lceil \frac{D_{fov,i}-D}{2\delta} - 10^{-9} \right\rceil , \]

i.e. a square screen of \(n_{pix}\times n_{pix}\) pixels whose margin around the pupil is rounded up to whole pixels and symmetric (\(n_{pix}-N\) even), so that the on-axis footprint is centred on the screen. Each screen is a PhaseScreenVonKarman with n_columns=2 and the default options (subharmonics, 4x oversized initial grid, far rows). Layer \(i\) is seeded with randomState + 1000 i; if no seed is given a random one is drawn, logged and stored in atm.randomState. Layers are built (and updated) in a thread pool.

docs.title: Footprint of a line of sight
docs.text:
The direction of a source is the vector \(\mathbf{v} = (\rho\cos\theta,\ \rho\sin\theta) + \mathbf{c}_i\) in arcsec, where \(\mathbf{c}_i\) is the optional chromatic shift of layer \(i\) (one \((dx, dy)\) per layer, common to all the sources of that wavelength, see Source). The footprint centre on layer \(i\), in layer pixels from the screen centre, is

\[ \mathbf{p}_i = \frac{h_i'\,\tan(|\mathbf{v}|/206265)}{\delta}\;\frac{\mathbf{v}}{|\mathbf{v}|}, \qquad \text{col}_0 = \mathrm{round}(p_{x}) + \lfloor n_{pix}/2\rfloor,\quad \text{row}_0 = \mathrm{round}(p_{y}) + \lfloor n_{pix}/2\rfloor . \]

The pupil is the \(N\times N\) window of the screen starting at \((\text{row}_0 - \lfloor N/2\rfloor,\ \text{col}_0 - \lfloor N/2\rfloor)\). All sources are at infinity, so the footprint has the same size on every layer (no cone effect).

Integer-pixel model (by design). The footprint position is rounded to the nearest layer pixel (np.round), with no sub-pixel interpolation. The position error is at most \(\delta/2\) per axis and is unbiased, but the angular separation between two sources is quantised to \(\delta/h_i'\) on each layer. Interpolating would smooth the screens and alter their spectrum, which is why it is not done. There is no bounds check: a source outside the circle of the telescope FoV makes the window leave the screen and the extraction fails.

docs.title: Frozen flow with whole-pixel steps
docs.text:
Each AO step of duration \(T_s\) (telescope.samplingTime) adds to two per-layer buffers

\[ s_x \mathrel{+}= \frac{v\cos\phi\; T_s}{\delta}, \qquad s_y \mathrel{+}= \frac{v\sin\phi\; T_s}{\delta}, \]

with \(v\) the wind speed and \(\phi\) the wind direction. The integer part \(n = \mathrm{trunc}(s)\) is applied to the screen as \(|n|\) successive extrusions (several per step for a fast layer, none if the displacement is below one pixel) and the fractional remainder stays in the buffer. Hence the mean velocity is exact, but the screen moves in whole-pixel jumps: within a step the instantaneous displacement can differ from the ideal one by up to \(\delta\) (temporal jitter of the order of \(\delta/v\)). Sign conventions:

  • \(s_x>0\): add_col(+1) adds a new column at the left (index 0) and the pattern moves towards \(+\)column (\(+x\)).
  • \(s_y>0\): add_row(-1) adds a new row at the top (index 0) and the pattern moves towards \(+\)row (\(+y\)). The row sign is inverted with respect to the method (add_row(+1) appends at the bottom, i.e. moves the pattern towards \(-\)row).

The buffers and the random generator of the extrusion are the evolution state of a layer.

docs.title: OPD of a line of sight (getOPD)
docs.text:
For each line of sight, the phase at 500 nm of every layer is cut at its footprint, rescaled to the observing wavelength \(\lambda_s\) under the non-dispersive assumption, and summed:

\[ \varphi_s = \sum_i \varphi_{500,i}\;\frac{\lambda_0}{\lambda_s}, \qquad \mathrm{OPD} = \varphi_s\,\frac{\lambda_s}{2\pi} = \frac{\lambda_0}{2\pi}\sum_i \varphi_{500,i}\ [\mathrm{m}] . \]

The OPD is therefore wavelength independent (refractive index of air constant with \(\lambda\)); only the phase in rad (computed later as \(2\pi\,\mathrm{OPD}/\lambda_s\)) depends on the band. The pupil mask is not applied here. For an extended source (tag == 'sun') the OPD is computed for each sub-direction star and returned with an extra leading axis. The chromatic shift only displaces the footprint, i.e. it models differential atmospheric refraction between wavelengths as a per-layer shift of the line of sight.

docs.title: Save and load
docs.text: save writes an H5 file with, per layer, the attributes (seed, D_fov, spatial_res, npix, fractionalR0, windSpeed, windDirection, altitude, n_columns), the extrusion matrices A_vert, B_vert, A_horz, B_horz, the current phase screen, the serialised state of the random generator and the two displacement buffers. load rebuilds the screens from these data without recomputing the covariance matrices or the initial screen, so a loaded atmosphere continues exactly as the saved one would have (files without the generator state restart it from the seed). Atmosphere parameters not stored in the file (\(L_0\), sampling time) come from the object being loaded into.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Integer-pixel footprints and whole-pixel motion (above); the pixel is \(D/N\), so the resolution sets the position accuracy.
  • Near-field, non-dispersive, plane-parallel layers; no scintillation, no cone effect, no \(L_0\) or wind scaling with zenith angle.
  • Extrusion statistics are approximate (stencil truncation, see Layer).

docs.title: References
docs.text:
• Roddier, F. (1981), The effects of atmospheric turbulence in optical astronomy, Progress in Optics 19, 281.
  • Assémat, F., Wilson, R. W., Gendron, E. (2006), Method for simulating infinitely long and non stationary phase screens with optimized memory storage, Opt. Express 14, 988.
  • Sasiela, R. J. (2007), Electromagnetic Wave Propagation in Turbulence, SPIE Press.

The Atmosphere class represents a multi-layer atmosphere with Von Kármán statistics.

Each layer is defined with altitude, wind speed/direction, and Cn2 contribution. Layers can be updated, saved to disk, and used to compute the OPD (Optical Path Difference) for various line-of-sight sources.

Attributes: r0 (float): Fried parameter at 500 nm. L0 (float): Outer scale of turbulence. windSpeed (List[float]): Wind speeds per layer. windDirection (List[float]): Wind directions per layer. altitude (List[float]): Altitudes of each layer. fractionalR0 (List[float]): Relative contribution of each layer to turbulence.

Initialize an Atmosphere object representing layered atmospheric turbulence.

None Source code in SAOS/Atmosphere.py 
def __init__(self,
             r0:float,
             L0:float,
             windSpeed:list,
             fractionalR0:list,
             windDirection:list,
             altitude:list,
             telescope,
             zenith:float=0.0,
             logger=None,
             n_jobs=None):
    """
    Initialize an Atmosphere object representing layered atmospheric turbulence.

    Parameters
    ----------
    r0 : float
        Fried parameter at 500 nm [m] and pointing to zenith.
    L0 : float
        Outer scale of turbulence [m].
    windSpeed : list of float
        Wind speed for each layer [m/s].
    fractionalR0 : list of float
        Cn2 profile; fractional contribution to turbulence per layer.
    windDirection : list of float
        Wind direction for each layer [degrees]: direction towards which the turbulence moves, in the frame of the source
        azimuths (0 deg -> +x = +column, 90 deg -> +y = +row of the phase screens).
    altitude : list of float
        Altitude of each layer [m].
    telescope : Telescope object
        Telescope class instantiation to take certain parameters required for the atmosphere.
    zenith : float, optional, by default 0.0
        Zenith angle [degrees] of the telescope during the simulation, to automatically convert the r0 given to the specific conditions.
    logger : logging.Logger, optional
        Logger instance for this object, by default None.
    n_jobs : int, optional
        Threads used to compute the OPD of the sub-directions of an extended source and to update the layers. Default (None):
        the CPUs available to the process (os.sched_getaffinity, which honours Slurm, cgroups and taskset) when called from the
        main thread, and 1 when called from another thread (e.g. LightPaths propagated in parallel), so that thread pools are
        never nested.
    """
    self.logger = logger if logger is not None else get_logger()

    self.hasNotBeenInitialized  = True
    self.r0                     = r0                     # Fried Parameter in m, at 500 nm and pointing to the zenith
    self.fractionalR0           = fractionalR0           # Fractional Cn2 profile of the turbulence
    self.L0                     = L0                     # Outer Scale in m
    self.altitude               = altitude               # altitude of the layers
    self.nLayer                 = len(fractionalR0)      # number of layer
    self.windSpeed              = windSpeed              # wind speed of the layers in m/s
    self.windDirection          = windDirection          # wind direction in degrees
    self.zenith                 = zenith * (np.pi/180)   # Zenith angle of the telescope during simulation
    self.n_jobs                 = n_jobs                 # threads of the internal pools (None: automatic, see _n_jobs)
    self.tag                    = 'atmosphere'           # Tag of the object

    self.wavelength             = 500*1e-9               # Wavelength used to define the properties of the atmosphere

    self.logger.debug('Atmosphere::initializeAtmosphere - Taking key parameters from the telescope.')
    self.resolution = telescope.resolution
    self.D = telescope.D
    self.samplingTime = telescope.samplingTime

    self.fov      = telescope.fov
    self.fov_rad  = telescope.fov_rad

    # Sanity check
    if len(self.windSpeed) < self.nLayer:
        self.logger.error('Atmosphere::__init - Wind speed list size is smaller than the number of layers')
        raise ValueError('Wind speed list size is smaller than the number of layers')
    elif len(self.windSpeed) > self.nLayer:
        self.logger.warning('Atmosphere::__init - Wind speed list size is larger than the number of layers. Only the first layers are considered.')

    if len(self.windDirection) < self.nLayer:
        self.logger.error('Atmosphere::__init - Wind direction list size is smaller than the number of layers')
        raise ValueError('Wind direction list size is smaller than the number of layers')
    elif len(self.windDirection) > self.nLayer:
        self.logger.warning('Atmosphere::__init - Wind direction list size is larger than the number of layers. Only the first layers are considered.')

    if len(self.altitude) < self.nLayer:
        self.logger.error('Atmosphere::__init - Altitude list size is smaller than the number of layers')
        raise ValueError('Altitude list size is smaller than the number of layers')
    elif len(self.altitude) > self.nLayer:
        self.logger.warning('Atmosphere::__init - Altitude list size is larger than the number of layers. Only the first layers are considered.')

def initializeAtmosphere(self, randomState=None):
    """
    Initialize the atmosphere layers using the telescope linked at construction time.

    Parameters
    ----------
    randomState : int or None, optional
        Seed for reproducible random number generation (layer i uses randomState + 1000 i). None: a random seed, logged
        and stored in self.randomState so that the atmosphere can be reproduced.

    Returns
    -------
    bool
        True if initialization succeeded, False otherwise.
    """
    self.logger.debug('Atmosphere::initializeAtmosphere')

    if self.hasNotBeenInitialized:
        self.initial_r0 = self.r0
        self.logger.debug('Atmosphere::initializeAtmosphere - Creating layers...')
        if randomState is None:
            # Random base seed (not the time of day), logged so that the atmosphere can be reproduced
            randomState = int(np.random.default_rng().integers(0, 2**31 - 1000*self.nLayer))
            self.logger.info(f'Atmosphere::initializeAtmosphere - randomState not given: using {randomState}.')
        self.randomState = randomState
        results_layers = Parallel(n_jobs=self._n_jobs(self.nLayer), prefer="threads")(delayed(self.buildLayer)(i_layer, randomState) for i_layer in range(self.nLayer))
        for i_layer in range(self.nLayer):
            setattr(self,'layer_'+str(i_layer+1),results_layers[i_layer])
    else:
        self.logger.warning('Atmosphere::initializeAtmosphere - The atmosphere has already been initialized.')
        return True

    self.hasNotBeenInitialized  = False 
    return True

def buildLayer(self, i_layer, seed = None):
    """
    Build and initialize a single atmospheric layer.

    Parameters
    ----------
    i_layer : int
        Index of the layer to build.
    seed : int, optional
        Seed for the random number generator.

    Returns
    -------
    LayerClass
        The initialized atmospheric layer.
    """
    self.logger.debug('Atmosphere::buildLayer - layer '+str(i_layer+1))

    # initialize layer object
    layer               = LayerClass()
    layer.id            = i_layer
    # Seed for the random phase generation  
    if seed is None:
        seed = int(np.random.default_rng().integers(0, 2**31 - 1000*self.nLayer))
    layer.seed          = seed + i_layer*1000

    # gather properties of the atmosphere
    layer.altitude      = self.altitude[i_layer] / np.cos(self.zenith)       
    layer.windSpeed     = self.windSpeed[i_layer]
    layer.windDirection = self.windDirection[i_layer]

    # Diameter of the layer seen by the Field Of View (metapupil). The layer pixel is the pupil pixel D / resolution, so the
    # resolution pixels cut for a footprint span exactly D; the margin around the pupil is rounded up to whole pixels and kept
    # symmetric (npix - resolution even), so the on-axis footprint is centred on the layer
    layer.D_fov        = self.D+2*np.tan(self.fov_rad/2)*layer.altitude
    layer.spatial_res  = self.D/self.resolution
    layer.npix         = self.resolution + 2*int(np.ceil((layer.D_fov - self.D)/(2*layer.spatial_res) - 1e-9))

    self.logger.debug('Atmosphere::buildLayer - Creating layer '+str(i_layer+1))    

    # Fried parameter of the layer (a layer with zero Cn2 fraction has r0 = infinity: no turbulence)
    frac = float(self.fractionalR0[i_layer])
    layer.fractionalR0 = self.r0*(np.cos(self.zenith)**0.6)*(frac**(-3/5)) if frac > 0 else np.inf

    layer.screen = PhaseScreenVonKarman(nx_size=layer.npix, pixel_scale=layer.spatial_res, r0 = layer.fractionalR0, 
                                        L0 = self.L0, random_seed = layer.seed, n_columns=2, logger=self.logger)

    self.logger.debug('Atmosphere::buildLayer - Layer '+str(i_layer+1)+' created.')      

    return layer

def save(self, filename):
    """
    Save the state of the atmosphere to a H5 file.

    Parameters
    ----------
    filename : str
        Path and base filename (with extension) to save the H5.

    Returns
    -------
    bool
        True if saved successfully, False otherwise.
    """
    self.logger.debug('Atmosphere::save')

    if self.hasNotBeenInitialized:
        self.logger.error('Atmosphere::save - The atmosphere has not been initialized yet.')
        return False

    # Create folder if it does not exist
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(filename), exist_ok=True)

    if not filename.endswith(".h5"):
        filename += ".h5"

    self.logger.info('Atmosphere::save - Creating the H5 file tree')

    with h5py.File(filename, 'a') as f:
        for i_layer in range(self.nLayer):
            group = f.create_group('layer_' + str(i_layer+1))
            # Atmosphere layer params
            group.attrs['id'] = getattr(self,'layer_'+str(i_layer+1)).id
            group.attrs['seed'] = getattr(self,'layer_'+str(i_layer+1)).seed
            group.attrs['D_fov'] = getattr(self,'layer_'+str(i_layer+1)).D_fov
            group.attrs['spatial_res'] = getattr(self,'layer_'+str(i_layer+1)).spatial_res
            group.attrs['npix'] = getattr(self,'layer_'+str(i_layer+1)).npix
            group.attrs['fractionalR0'] = getattr(self,'layer_'+str(i_layer+1)).fractionalR0
            group.attrs['windSpeed'] = getattr(self,'layer_'+str(i_layer+1)).windSpeed
            group.attrs['windDirection'] = getattr(self,'layer_'+str(i_layer+1)).windDirection
            group.attrs['altitude'] = getattr(self,'layer_'+str(i_layer+1)).altitude
            # Von Karman infinite layer params:
            # Vertical movement matrices
            group.create_dataset('A_vert', data=getattr(self,'layer_'+str(i_layer+1)).screen.A_vert)
            group.create_dataset('B_vert', data=getattr(self,'layer_'+str(i_layer+1)).screen.B_vert)
            # Horizontal movement matrices
            group.create_dataset('A_horz', data=getattr(self,'layer_'+str(i_layer+1)).screen.A_horz)
            group.create_dataset('B_horz', data=getattr(self,'layer_'+str(i_layer+1)).screen.B_horz)
            # Common variables
            group.create_dataset('phase', data=getattr(self,'layer_'+str(i_layer+1)).screen.scrn)
            group.attrs['n_columns'] = getattr(self,'layer_'+str(i_layer+1)).screen.n_columns
            # Evolution state: random generator of the extrusion and sub-pixel displacement buffers, so that a loaded
            # atmosphere continues exactly as the saved one would have
            group.attrs['rng_state'] = json.dumps(getattr(self,'layer_'+str(i_layer+1)).screen._R.bit_generator.state)
            group.attrs['displ_buffer_x'] = getattr(self,'layer_'+str(i_layer+1)).displ_buffer_x
            group.attrs['displ_buffer_y'] = getattr(self,'layer_'+str(i_layer+1)).displ_buffer_y

    self.logger.info('Atmosphere::save - Saved.')

def load(self, filename): 
    """
    Load an atmosphere configuration from a H5 file.

    Parameters
    ----------
    filename : str
        Path and base filename (with extension) of the H5 file to load.

    Returns
    -------
    bool
        True if loaded successfully, False otherwise.
    """
    self.logger.debug('Atmosphere::load')


    if not filename.endswith(".h5"):
        filename += ".h5"        

    with h5py.File(filename, 'r') as f:
        # Layers in their numeric order (the h5 groups are listed alphabetically: layer_10 before layer_2)
        layer_names = sorted([k for k in f.keys() if k.startswith('layer_')], key=lambda k: int(k.split('_')[1]))
        for i_layer, grp_name in enumerate(layer_names):
            layer = LayerClass()
            layer.id = f[grp_name].attrs['id']
            layer.seed = f[grp_name].attrs['seed']
            layer.D_fov = f[grp_name].attrs['D_fov']
            layer.spatial_res = f[grp_name].attrs['spatial_res']
            layer.npix = f[grp_name].attrs['npix']
            layer.fractionalR0 = f[grp_name].attrs['fractionalR0']
            layer.windSpeed = f[grp_name].attrs['windSpeed']
            layer.windDirection = f[grp_name].attrs['windDirection']
            layer.altitude = f[grp_name].attrs['altitude']

            screen_dict = {'A_vert': np.array(f[grp_name]['A_vert']),
                           'B_vert': np.array(f[grp_name]['B_vert']),
                           'A_horz': np.array(f[grp_name]['A_horz']),
                           'B_horz': np.array(f[grp_name]['B_horz']),
                           'phase': np.array(f[grp_name]['phase'])}
            layer.screen = PhaseScreenVonKarman(nx_size=layer.npix, pixel_scale=layer.spatial_res, r0=layer.fractionalR0, L0=self.L0, 
                                                random_seed=layer.seed, n_columns=f[grp_name].attrs['n_columns'], from_file=True, screen_file=screen_dict, logger=self.logger)
            # Evolution state (optional in the file: if absent, the generator restarts from the seed)
            if 'rng_state' in f[grp_name].attrs:
                layer.screen._R.bit_generator.state = json.loads(f[grp_name].attrs['rng_state'])
            layer.displ_buffer_x = float(f[grp_name].attrs.get('displ_buffer_x', 0.0))
            layer.displ_buffer_y = float(f[grp_name].attrs.get('displ_buffer_y', 0.0))

            setattr(self, 'layer_'+str(i_layer+1), layer)

        self.hasNotBeenInitialized = False


        self.logger.info(f"Atmosphere::load - All layers finished.")     


        return True

def update(self):
    """
    Update all atmospheric layers based on wind and time step.

    Returns
    -------
    bool
        True if update was successful.
    """
    self.logger.debug('Atmosphere::update')
    # Update each layer at a different process to speed up the computation.
    # Threads are faster than multiprocessing due to the overheads of making the copies. 
    results = Parallel(n_jobs=self._n_jobs(self.nLayer), prefer="threads")(
        delayed(self.updateLayer)(getattr(self,'layer_'+str(i_layer+1))) for i_layer in range(self.nLayer))
    for i_layer in range(self.nLayer):
        setattr(self,'layer_'+str(i_layer+1),results[i_layer])

    # Serialize layers into shared memory before the getOPD method call

    self.logger.debug('Atmosphere::update - Updated.')
    return True

Update a single atmospheric layer, shifting the phase screen. ^ +Vy (adds row --> + to the bottom, - to the top) | | |----> +Vx (adds col --> + to the left, - to the right)

def updateLayer(self,updatedLayer):
    """
    Update a single atmospheric layer, shifting the phase screen.
    ^ +Vy (adds row --> + to the bottom, - to the top)
    |
    |
    |----> +Vx (adds col --> + to the left, - to the right)

    Parameters
    ----------
    updatedLayer : LayerClass
        The layer to update.

    Returns
    -------
    LayerClass
        The updated layer.
    """
    self.logger.debug('Atmosphere::updateLayer')

    # Compute speed per axis

    vx = updatedLayer.windSpeed * np.cos(np.deg2rad(updatedLayer.windDirection))
    vy = updatedLayer.windSpeed * np.sin(np.deg2rad(updatedLayer.windDirection))

    # Compute displacement in px
    updatedLayer.displ_buffer_x += (vx*self.samplingTime) / updatedLayer.spatial_res
    updatedLayer.displ_buffer_y += (vy*self.samplingTime) / updatedLayer.spatial_res

    # Move the screen by every whole pixel accumulated in the buffers (several per step for fast layers); the fraction stays
    # in the buffer. Same frame as the source azimuths (getOPD): x = +column, y = +row. add_col(+1) shifts the content
    # towards +column; add_row(+1) appends at the bottom, so the content moves towards -row: the row sign is inverted
    n_y = int(np.trunc(updatedLayer.displ_buffer_y))
    for _ in range(abs(n_y)):
        updatedLayer.screen.add_row(-np.sign(n_y))
    updatedLayer.displ_buffer_y -= n_y
    n_x = int(np.trunc(updatedLayer.displ_buffer_x))
    for _ in range(abs(n_x)):
        updatedLayer.screen.add_col(np.sign(n_x))
    updatedLayer.displ_buffer_x -= n_x

    return updatedLayer

def _n_jobs(self, n_tasks):
    """
    Threads for an internal pool of n_tasks tasks: n_jobs if given; otherwise 1 when called from a thread other than the main one
    (the caller already runs in parallel: no nested pools), else the CPUs available to the process (not os.cpu_count, which
    ignores the Slurm allocation).
    """
    if self.n_jobs is not None:
        n = int(self.n_jobs)
    elif threading.current_thread() is not threading.main_thread():
        n = 1
    else:
        n = len(os.sched_getaffinity(0)) if hasattr(os, 'sched_getaffinity') else (os.cpu_count() or 1)
    return max(1, min(n, n_tasks))

def getOPD(self, src):
    """
    Compute the Optical Path Difference (OPD) for a given source.

    Parameters
    ----------
    src : Source or ExtendedSource
        The light source for which to compute the OPD.

    Returns
    -------
    np.ndarray
        OPD values in meters (or list of OPDs if multiple sources).
    """
    self.logger.debug('Atmosphere::getOPD - Getting the OPD for each source.')

    # First, we need to check the source tbecause the sun is made of an asterism, 
    # it will be more efficient to run in parallel the process for each individual star and then combine it.

    list_src = []

    if src.tag == 'sun':
        for subDir in src.subDirs_stars:
            list_src.append(subDir)
    else:
        list_src.append(src)

    # One task per line of sight: footprint per layer, phase per layer [rad], sum of the layers -> OPD without pupil [m].
    # A single pool (sequential when called from a parallel LightPath, see _n_jobs)
    def opd_of(s):
        return self.get_opd_per_src(s, self.project_phase(s, self.get_pupil_footprint(s)))
    n_jobs = self._n_jobs(len(list_src))
    t0 = time.time()
    if n_jobs == 1:
        result_opd_no_pupil = [opd_of(s) for s in list_src]
    else:
        result_opd_no_pupil = Parallel(n_jobs=n_jobs, prefer="threads")(delayed(opd_of)(s) for s in list_src)
    self.logger.debug(f'getOPD: {time.time()-t0} s for {len(list_src)} lines of sight, {n_jobs} threads')
    return np.squeeze(result_opd_no_pupil)

def get_pupil_footprint(self, src):
    """
    Determine the pupil footprint of a source on every layer. The footprint centre is h tan(theta) rounded to the nearest
    layer pixel (integer-pixel model, like the screen motion): position error <= 0.5 px per axis, unbiased.

    Parameters
    ----------
    src : Source
        Light source object.

    Returns
    -------
    list
        Pupil footprint (mask of the layer) per layer.
    """
    self.logger.debug('Atmosphere::set_pupil_footprint')
    footprint_per_layer = []

    for i_layer in range(self.nLayer):
        layer = getattr(self,'layer_'+str(i_layer+1))

        # Chromatic shift: one on-sky vector (dx, dy) [arcsec] per layer, x = +column, y = +row, common to every source of
        # this wavelength (atmospheric dispersion moves all the lines of sight alike); added to the source direction
        if src.chromatic_shift is None:
            chromatic_shift = np.zeros(2)
        else:
            chromatic_shift = np.asarray(src.chromatic_shift, dtype=float)
            if chromatic_shift.shape != (self.nLayer, 2):
                raise ValueError(f'Atmosphere::get_pupil_footprint - chromatic_shift must be one (dx, dy) [arcsec] per layer, '
                                 f'shape ({self.nLayer}, 2); got {chromatic_shift.shape}.')
            chromatic_shift = chromatic_shift[i_layer]

        # The source coordinates are defined as: [elevation, azimuth] taking as reference the Zenith, i.e. [0,x] has the telescope pointing to the sky vertically.
        # Elevation is measured in arcsec, azimuth in degrees.
        # We need to compute the location of the source w.r.t zenith to define the pupil centered at the source
        # The polar coordinates, at an altiudue z_i are: r = z_i*tan(elevation), theta = azimuth. Then, we convert to cartesian coordinates.
        # Note that before changing coordinates, the radius in meters is converted to px using the layer diameter (layer.D) and phase screen size (layer.resolution)
        D = layer.npix * (self.D/ self.resolution)
        # On-sky direction vector [arcsec] of the line of sight (source + chromatic shift), then its footprint h tan(|v|) along v
        v = np.array(pol2cart(src.coordinates[0], np.deg2rad(src.coordinates[1]))) + chromatic_shift
        ang = np.hypot(v[0], v[1])
        r_px = layer.altitude*np.tan(ang/206265) * layer.npix / D
        [x_z, y_z] = (r_px * v / ang) if ang > 0 else (0.0, 0.0)
        # [x_z, y_z] are the cartesian coordinates in px w.r.t zenith. 
        # Rounded to the nearest layer pixel (integer-pixel model)
        center_x = int(np.round(y_z))+layer.npix//2
        center_y = int(np.round(x_z))+layer.npix//2

        # Finally, create the pupil and set the points inside the pupil to 1
        pupil_footprint = np.zeros([layer.npix,layer.npix])
        row0, col0 = center_x - self.resolution//2, center_y - self.resolution//2      # resolution pixels, odd or even
        pupil_footprint[row0:row0 + self.resolution, col0:col0 + self.resolution] = 1

        footprint_per_layer.append(pupil_footprint)
    return footprint_per_layer

def project_phase(self, src, pupil_footprint):

def get_opd_per_src(self, src, phase):
    """
    Sum up the phases from all layers to compute the OPD for a source.

    Parameters

    src : Source
        Light source.
    phase : list of np.ndarray

docs.title: Theory and implementation
docs.text: The controller converts the slopes of the WFS light paths into commands of the DMs, in the modal basis of the IM (see Interaction Matrix Helper). At every iteration computeControlAction returns the absolute command of each DM, \(u_i = B_i\,c_i\), where \(B_i\) are the columns of the modal basis of DM \(i\) that match the IM (the first discarded_modes columns are skipped) and \(c_i\) the modal coefficients [m].

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Slopes \(s\) are those of the WFS after the loop delay (LightPath.get_wavefront_error), in the units of the IM (px, or rad). The linear model is \(s = s_{turb} + H\,c\), with \(H\) the IM.
  • The controller works with the negative slopes, \(e_{res} = -s\) (error_res in the code, "\(-1\) for the feedback"), so that a positive gain drives the slopes to zero: \(c \leftarrow c + g\,R\,e_{res}\).
  • \(d_i\) is the delay of DM \(i\) in samples (delay, int or list, default 1). command_history keeps the last commands: \(c_i(k-d_i)\) is the command computed \(d_i\) calls ago.
  • Per-DM parameters (rcond, beta, gain, decay, ki, nModes) accept a scalar (copied to all DMs) or a list of length \(n_{DM}\).

docs.title: Reconstructors
docs.text:
Let \(H\) be the IM (stacked over the WFS that are used), of shape \(n_s\times n\), and \(H = U\Sigma V^T\) its SVD with singular values \(\sigma_1\ge\sigma_2\ge\dots\).

Inversion. \(R = H^{+}\), the pseudo-inverse with rcond \(\rho\) (torch.linalg.pinv): singular values \(\sigma_j<\rho\,\sigma_1\) are set to zero, i.e. \(R=V\,\mathrm{diag}(\sigma_j^{-1}\,[\sigma_j\ge\rho\sigma_1])\,U^T\). It is a fraction (not a percentage) of the largest singular value. The discarded combinations of modes are not controlled (zero gain), which limits the noise propagation of poorly sensed modes.

Tikhonov. \(R=(H^TH+\alpha I)^{-1}H^T = V\,\mathrm{diag}\!\left(\frac{\sigma_j}{\sigma_j^2+\alpha}\right)U^T\) with \(\alpha=\beta\,\sigma_1^2\) (beta, dimensionless, default \(10^{-4}\)): the regularisation is relative to the largest singular value, so \(\beta\) does not depend on the units of the slopes.

Joint block reconstructor (joint_reconstruction=True, default, for inversion and tikhonov). One matrix is built over all the active WFS (rows) and all the DMs (columns)

\[ H_{glob}=\begin{pmatrix} H_{1,1} & \cdots & H_{1,n_{DM}}\\ \vdots & & \vdots\\ H_{n_{WFS},1} & \cdots & H_{n_{WFS},n_{DM}}\end{pmatrix} \]

where \(H_{w,i}\) is the IM of DM \(i\) on WFS \(w\), or zeros when the link is not in the target mask, and its pseudo-inverse \(R_{glob}\) is split in row blocks \(R_i\) (one per DM). The DMs then share the work: the slopes of a WFS that sees several DMs are explained by all of them at once. For inversion, a single \(\rho\) is used for the whole matrix (the minimum of the list). For tikhonov, \(\Gamma=\mathrm{diag}(\alpha_i I_{n_i})\) with \(\alpha_i=\beta_i\,\sigma_{1}(H_{:,i})^2\), the largest singular value of the columns of DM \(i\), and \(R_{glob}=(H_{glob}^TH_{glob}+\Gamma)^{-1}H_{glob}^T\). The input of each \(R_i\) is the concatenation of \(-s\) of all the active WFS in light-path order, whatever the masks.

Per-DM reconstructors (joint_reconstruction=False, and always for the tomography method). Each DM is inverted independently with the IMs of the WFS of its row of the target mask. The input of \(R_i\) is the concatenation of \(-s\) of the WFS of the row of the control mask. A DM without WFS in its row gets a zero reconstructor (warning).

Masks. control_mask (\(n_{DM}\times n_{LP}\)) selects the (DM, WFS) pairs whose slopes the controller uses; target_mask (default control_mask) selects the pairs whose IM enters the reconstructor. Pairs without a measured IM are ignored (warning).

Modes. The number of controlled modes of DM \(i\) is \(\min(n_{basis}-n_{discarded},\ nModes_i,\ n_{IM\,columns})\). discarded_modes (2 for altitude DMs with zernike/dh/kl) are the leading modes removed at the measurement of the IM; the command uses the basis columns shifted by that offset.

docs.title: Control laws
docs.text:
With \(e(k)=R\,e_{res}(k)\) the modal error (for the tomography method see below), per DM:

Law Recursion Transfer function \(C(z)\) (\(c = C\,e\)) leaky \(c(k)=g\,e(k)+a\,c(k-1)\), \(a=\)decay \(\dfrac{g}{1-a z^{-1}}\) forwardPI \(c(k)=c(k-1)+g\,[e(k)-e(k-1)]+k_i\,e(k-1)\) \(g+\dfrac{k_i z^{-1}}{1-z^{-1}}\) backwardPI \(c(k)=c(k-1)+g\,[e(k)-e(k-1)]+k_i\,e(k)\) \(g+\dfrac{k_i}{1-z^{-1}}\) stateSpace \(y(k)=C x(k)+D\,u(k),\quad x(k+1)=A x(k)+B\,u(k)\), \(u=e\), \(c=y\) \(C(zI-A)^{-1}B+D\)

decay is the leak factor applied to the previous command (\(a=1\) is a pure integrator, \(a<1\) leaks). For the PI laws the proportional action is applied on the variation of the error, as a velocity-form PI. The state-space matrices are given per DM, \(A\): \(n_x\times n_x\), \(B\): \(n_x\times n_{modes}\), \(C\): \(n_{modes}\times n_x\), \(D\) optional (zeros); the state starts at zero. The loop delay is not part of \(C(z)\): it comes from the light path buffer (the slopes are \(d\) samples old).

docs.title: Operation modes
docs.text:
• closed: \(e_{res}=-s\) with the residual slopes seen by the WFS (the DM correction is included in \(s\)).
  • open: the command is zero (flat DM) at all iterations; the slopes are not used. It is meant to record open-loop telemetry or the atmosphere-only performance.
  • polc (pseudo-open-loop control, Ellerbroek and Vogel 2003): the reconstructor acts on the estimate of the open-loop slopes
\[ s_{pol}(k)=s(k)-\sum_j H_j\,c_j(k-d_j), \]

with the code's sign \(-s_{pol}=e_{res}+\sum_j H_j c_j(k-d_j)\), where \(H_j\) is the IM of DM \(j\) on the slopes of the vector and \(c_j(k-d_j)\) the command that the WFS is seeing now. For inversion/tikhonov with the leaky or PI laws the law is

\[ c(k)=(1-g)\,c(k-1)+g\,\big(-R\,s_{pol}(k)\big), \]

whose DC gain is 1 for any \(0<g\le1\) (the integrator of the closed-loop is replaced by a first-order filter, because an integrator fed with open-loop slopes has no feedback and winds up). decay and ki are not used (a warning is logged for the PI laws). A stateSpace law receives \(-R\,s_{pol}\) as its input \(u\).

The slopes whose commands are added back depend on the reconstructor. With a joint reconstructor, the global vector gets \(\sum_j H_j c_j(k-d_j)\) with \(H_j\) the IM of DM \(j\) on all the active WFS, which requires all the DMs to have their IM on the global vector (otherwise ValueError). With per-DM reconstructors, the slope vector of DM \(i\) (the WFS of its row of the control mask) gets the commands of every DM seen by those WFS, not only DM \(i\). If a DM is in the optical path of one of those WFS and its IM on that WFS was not measured, the pseudo-open-loop slopes would be incomplete and a ValueError is raised at the first call.

Limitation. POLC uses the commanded \(c(k-d_j)\), not the DM shape filtered by the DM dynamic model (response, hysteresis, coupling dynamics) that the WFS actually sees; the IM is also measured with the dynamics off. Using the filtered shape is left as a future development.

docs.title: Tomography
docs.text:
With reconstructionMethod='tomography', R_tomo (HDF5 dataset R_tomo or Rtomo in R_tomo_path, see Learn Estimator) maps the measured slopes to the slopes of the target (virtual) WFS, \(s_{tgt}=R_{tomo}\,s_{pol}\). It is kept on the CPU. set_tomography_targets(D_list, joint=True) takes the IMs \(D_i\) of every DM on the target slopes, builds a reconstructor \(R_i\) of them (joint: Tikhonov of \(D_{all}=[D_1\dots D_n]\) with the per-DM \(\alpha_i\) as above, so the DMs share the fit; per-DM otherwise) and precomputes

\[ M_1^{(i)}=R_i\,R_{tomo},\qquad M_2^{(i)}=R_i\,D_{all}. \]

The modal error of DM \(i\) is the reconstruction of the target residual, \(R_i\,(R_{tomo}\,s_{pol}-D_{all}\,c(k-1))\), evaluated online as

\[ e_i(k)=M_1^{(i)}\,(-s_{pol}(k))-M_2^{(i)}\,c(k-1), \]

with \(c(k-1)\) the stacked last commands, in the code's sign. It is then filtered by the control law (leaky or PI; stateSpace is not applied in this branch). release_R_tomo=True frees \(R_{tomo}\) after the products are formed, so the online cost is two small matrix-vector products. Without set_tomography_targets the open-loop target slopes are integrated (warning). The formula assumes pseudo-open-loop slopes: it is the polc operation that provides them.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Linear model: \(H\) measured with one push per mode and without dynamics.
  • No explicit noise model in inversion/tikhonov: \(\rho\) and \(\beta\) are tuned by hand.
  • POLC with commanded, not filtered, DM shape (see above).

def __init__(self,
             telescope,
             interactionMatrix,
             controllerType,
             reconstructionMethod,  
             operationType='closed',               
             logger = None,
             **kwargs):
    """
    Initialize the Controller module.

    Parameters
    ----------
    telescope : Telescope instance
        Telescope instance, provides the sampling time of the simulation.
    interactionMatrix : InteractionMatrixHandler instance
        Contains the interaction matrices and modal basis for the simulation configuration.
    controllerType : String
        The type of controller that will be used, supported types are: {leaky, forwardPI, backwardPI, stateSpace}. 
    reconstructionMethod : String
        Type of reconstructor used, supported types are: {inversion, tikhonov, tomography}.        
    operationType : String
        The type of operation that will be used, supported types are: {open, closed, polc}. By default, closed.
        polc: the reconstructor acts on the pseudo-open-loop slopes s_pol = s + IM c(k - delay). With inversion/tikhonov and the
        leaky or PI controllers the law is c(k) = (1 - gain) c(k-1) + gain (-R s_pol) (decay and ki are not used); a stateSpace
        controller receives -R s_pol as its input. With tomography, see the tomographic law.
        The IM term adds back every DM in the optical path of the WFS: with a joint reconstructor on the global slope
        vector, sum_j IM_j c_j(k - d_j); with per-DM reconstructors (joint_reconstruction=False), the slope vector of DM i
        (WFS of its mask row) also gets the commands of the other DMs seen by those WFS. A DM in the optical path of one
        of those WFS whose IM was not measured raises ValueError at the first call.
    **kwargs
        rcond : list of length equal to nDMs or float
            Percentage of the maximum singular value below witch the SV are discarded.
        beta : list of length equal to nDMs or float
            Regularisation coefficient beta for the Tikhonov Regularisation: alfa = beta * (Smax**2)
        gain : list of length equal to nDMs or float
            Proportional gain of the Leaky and PI controllers
        decay : list of length equal to nDMs or float
            Decay rate for the Leaky integrator
        ki : list of length equal to nDMs or float
            Integral gain for the PI controllers            
        A : list of 2D arrays or single 2D array
            State-transition matrix/matrices for the stateSpace controller. Shape (N_states, N_states).
        B : list of 2D arrays or single 2D array
            Input-to-state matrix/matrices for the stateSpace controller. Shape (N_states, N_inputs).
        C : list of 2D arrays or single 2D array
            State-to-output matrix/matrices for the stateSpace controller. Shape (N_outputs, N_states).
        D : list of 2D arrays or single 2D array, optional
            Feedforward matrix/matrices for the stateSpace controller. Shape (N_outputs, N_inputs).
    """        
    # Setup the logger to handle the queue of info, warning and errors msgs in the simulator
    self.logger = logger if logger is not None else get_logger()

    # Define class attributes
    self.tag = 'controller'
    self.delay_input = kwargs.get('delay', 1)

    self.device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")

    self.samplingTime = telescope.samplingTime

    if reconstructionMethod in {'inversion', 'tikhonov', 'tomography'}:
        self.reconstructionMethod = reconstructionMethod
    else:
        self.logger.error('Controller - Unknown reconstructor.')
        raise ValueError('Unknown controller')

    # Default will change to list of size nDMs once the IM is scanned
    self.rcond = kwargs.get('rcond', 0.025)
    self.beta = kwargs.get('beta', 1e-4) # adim, adjusted through trial-error

    # Mask provided by the user to select specific WFS-DM links
    self.control_mask = kwargs.get('control_mask', None)
    self.target_mask = kwargs.get('target_mask', self.control_mask)
    self.R_tomo_path = kwargs.get('R_tomo_path', None)

    self.nModes = kwargs.get('nModes', None)
    self.joint_reconstruction = kwargs.get('joint_reconstruction', True)

    # Run the initialization of the reconstructor
    self.reconstructor, self.modal_basis, self.mask, self.t_mask, self.discarded_modes = self.initializeReconstructor(self.reconstructionMethod, interactionMatrix)                

    # Setup the controller

    if controllerType in {'leaky', 'forwardPI', 'backwardPI', 'stateSpace'}:
        self.controllerType = controllerType
    else:
        self.logger.error('Controller - Unknown controller.')
        raise ValueError('Unknown controller')

    if operationType in {'open', 'closed', 'polc'}:
        self.operationType = operationType
    else:
        raise ValueError('Unknown operation type')

    # POLC with per-DM slope vectors: IMs of every DM on the WFS of each DM's mask
    self.im_polc_cross, self.polc_cross_missing = None, []
    if self.operationType == 'polc':
        self.im_polc_cross, self.polc_cross_missing = self._init_polc_cross_ims(interactionMatrix)

    if self.controllerType == 'stateSpace':
        self.A = kwargs.get('A', None)
        self.B = kwargs.get('B', None)
        self.C = kwargs.get('C', None)
        self.D = kwargs.get('D', None)

        if self.A is None or self.B is None or self.C is None:
            raise ValueError("State-space controller requires matrices A, B, and C to be specified.")

        if not isinstance(self.A, list):
            self.A = [self.A]
        if not isinstance(self.B, list):
            self.B = [self.B]
        if not isinstance(self.C, list):
            self.C = [self.C]
        if self.D is not None and not isinstance(self.D, list):
            self.D = [self.D]

        if len(self.A) != len(self.reconstructor) or len(self.B) != len(self.reconstructor) or len(self.C) != len(self.reconstructor):
            raise ValueError("State-space matrices A, B, C lists must have length equal to the number of DMs.")
        if self.D is not None and len(self.D) != len(self.reconstructor):
            raise ValueError("State-space matrix D list must have length equal to the number of DMs.")
    else:
        self.gain = kwargs.get('gain', [0.0 for _ in range(len(self.reconstructor))])
        self.decay = kwargs.get('decay', [0.0 for _ in range(len(self.reconstructor))])
        self.ki = kwargs.get('ki', [0.0 for _ in range(len(self.reconstructor))])

        if not isinstance(self.gain, list):
            temp_gain = self.gain
            self.gain = [temp_gain for _ in range(len(self.reconstructor))]
        if not isinstance(self.decay, list):
            temp_decay = self.decay
            self.decay = [temp_decay for _ in range(len(self.reconstructor))]
        if not isinstance(self.ki, list):
            temp_ki = self.ki
            self.ki = [temp_ki for _ in range(len(self.reconstructor))]                        

        if len(self.gain) != len(self.reconstructor):
            raise ValueError('The gain should be a float or a a list of size nDMs.')
        if len(self.decay) != len(self.reconstructor):
            raise ValueError('The decay should be a float or a a list of size nDMs.')
        if len(self.ki) != len(self.reconstructor):
            raise ValueError('The ki should be a float or a a list of size nDMs.')                

    # Run the initialization of the controller
    self.initializeController(self.controllerType, self.reconstructor)

def initializeReconstructor(self, reconstructionMethod, interactionMatrix):
    """
    Initialize the reconstructor matrix from the measured interaction matrices.

    Parameters
    ----------
    reconstructionMethod : str
        Type of reconstructor ('inversion' or 'tikhonov').
    interactionMatrix : InteractionMatrixHandler
        Object containing the measured interaction matrices and modal basis.

    Returns
    -------
    reconstructor : list
        List of reconstructor matrices per DM.
    modal_basis : list
        List of modal basis per DM.
    mask : np.ndarray
        Boolean mask indicating interactions between DMs and measured light paths.
    t_mask : np.ndarray
        Boolean mask indicating interactions between DMs and targeted light paths.
    discarded_modes : list
        List of number of discarded modes per DM.
    """
    self.logger.info('Controller::initializeReconstructor - Computing the reconstructor.')
    t0 = time.time()

    # Define the mask that relates the DMs with the LPs

    nDMs = len(interactionMatrix.interaction_matrix_warehouse) # IM warehouse has: nDms x nLPs

    if nDMs < 1:
        raise ValueError('Number of DMs detected are less than 1.')

    nLPs = len(interactionMatrix.interaction_matrix_warehouse[0])

    if nLPs < 1:
        raise ValueError('Number of LPs detected are less than 1.')

    # Setup delay array
    if isinstance(self.delay_input, list):
        if len(self.delay_input) != nDMs:
            raise ValueError('Delay parameter must be an integer or a list of size nDMs.')
        self.delay = self.delay_input
    else:
        self.delay = [self.delay_input for _ in range(nDMs)]

    mask = np.zeros((nDMs, nLPs),dtype=bool)
    t_mask = np.zeros((nDMs, nLPs),dtype=bool)

    # Scan for interactions: if None, then there is not interaction.

    for i in range(nDMs):
        for j in range(nLPs):
            if interactionMatrix.interaction_matrix_warehouse[i][j]['IM'] is not None:
                mask[i, j] = True
                t_mask[i, j] = True

    if hasattr(self, 'control_mask') and self.control_mask is not None:
        # Check dimensions
        control_mask_arr = np.array(self.control_mask, dtype=bool)
        if control_mask_arr.shape != (nDMs, nLPs):
            self.logger.error(f'Controller - control_mask shape must be ({nDMs}, {nLPs})')
            raise ValueError(f'control_mask shape mismatch. Expected ({nDMs}, {nLPs}), got {control_mask_arr.shape}')

        # Warn if user requests control where no IM exists
        invalid_requests = control_mask_arr & (~mask)
        if np.any(invalid_requests):
            self.logger.warning('Controller - control_mask requests control for DM/LP pairs without an interaction matrix. These will be ignored.')

        mask = mask & control_mask_arr

    if hasattr(self, 'target_mask') and self.target_mask is not None:
        target_mask_arr = np.array(self.target_mask, dtype=bool)
        if target_mask_arr.shape != (nDMs, nLPs):
            self.logger.error(f'Controller - target_mask shape must be ({nDMs}, {nLPs})')
            raise ValueError(f'target_mask shape mismatch. Expected ({nDMs}, {nLPs}), got {target_mask_arr.shape}')

        invalid_requests = target_mask_arr & (~t_mask)
        if np.any(invalid_requests):
            self.logger.warning('Controller - target_mask requests control for DM/LP pairs without an interaction matrix. These will be ignored.')
        t_mask = t_mask & target_mask_arr
    else:
        t_mask = t_mask & mask


    # Check the reconstructor parameters
    if isinstance(self.rcond, list):
        if len(self.rcond) != nDMs:
            raise ValueError('Rcond parameter is expected to be a list of size equal to the number of DMs.')
    else:
        # Make the list copying the values
        temp_rcond = self.rcond
        self.rcond = [temp_rcond for _ in range(nDMs)]

    if isinstance(self.beta, list):
        if len(self.beta) != nDMs:
            raise ValueError('Beta parameter is expected to be a list of size equal to the number of DMs.')
    else:
        # Make the list copying the values
        temp_beta = self.beta
        self.beta = [temp_beta for _ in range(nDMs)]   

    # Get modal basis
    modal_basis = []
    for i in range(nDMs):
        for j in range(nLPs):
            if interactionMatrix.interaction_matrix_warehouse[i][j]['IM'] is not None:
                # The modal basis is common for each DM
                modal_basis_type = interactionMatrix.interaction_matrix_warehouse[i][j]['modalBasis']
                modal_basis.append(torch.as_tensor(interactionMatrix.modal_basis[i][modal_basis_type], dtype=torch.float64, device=self.device))
                break
    # Get discarded modes metadata:
    discarded_modes = []
    for i in range(nDMs):
        found_discarded_modes = 0
        for j in range(nLPs):
            if interactionMatrix.interaction_matrix_warehouse[i][j]['IM'] is not None:
                found_discarded_modes = interactionMatrix.interaction_matrix_warehouse[i][j].get('discarded_modes', 0)
                break
        discarded_modes.append(found_discarded_modes)

    if reconstructionMethod == 'tomography':
        import h5py
        if hasattr(self, 'R_tomo_path') and self.R_tomo_path is not None:
            try:
                with h5py.File(self.R_tomo_path, 'r') as f:
                    if 'R_tomo' in f:
                        R_tomo_np = np.array(f['R_tomo'])
                    elif 'Rtomo' in f:
                        R_tomo_np = np.array(f['Rtomo'])
                    else:
                        raise KeyError("Neither 'R_tomo' nor 'Rtomo' dataset found in the HDF5 file.")
                # Keep R_tomo on CPU to avoid CUDA OOM (for M19_T19 it occupies 12 GB, which exceeds RTX 2080 VRAM)
                self.R_tomo = torch.as_tensor(R_tomo_np, dtype=torch.float64, device='cpu')
                self.logger.info(f"Loaded tomographic reconstructor from {self.R_tomo_path}")
            except Exception as e:
                self.logger.error(f"Failed to load R_tomo from {self.R_tomo_path}: {e}")
                raise
        else:
            self.logger.error("R_tomo_path must be provided for tomography reconstruction method.")
            raise ValueError("R_tomo_path must be provided for tomography reconstruction method.")

    # Check if joint reconstruction across multiple DMs should be performed
    joint_reconstruction = getattr(self, 'joint_reconstruction', True)

    # Define the reconstruction matrices for each DM
    reconstructor = []
    self.im_per_dm = []
    im_target_tensors = []
    n_modes_target = []
    all_dms_have_target = True

    for i in range(nDMs):
        # 1. Measured IM for POLC
        interaction_matrix_per_DM = []
        for j in range(nLPs):
            if mask[i,j]:
                # Append the IMs to shape one large matrix of size nValidAct x nSignals
                im = interactionMatrix.interaction_matrix_warehouse[i][j]['IM']
                if self.nModes is not None:
                    n_m = self.nModes[i] if isinstance(self.nModes, list) else self.nModes
                    if n_m is not None:
                        im = im[:, :n_m]
                interaction_matrix_per_DM.append(im)

        if len(interaction_matrix_per_DM) == 0:
            nModes_i = modal_basis[i].shape[1] - discarded_modes[i]
            if self.nModes is not None:
                n_m = self.nModes[i] if isinstance(self.nModes, list) else self.nModes
                if n_m is not None:
                    nModes_i = min(nModes_i, n_m)
            self.im_per_dm.append(torch.zeros((0, nModes_i), dtype=torch.float64, device=self.device))
        else:
            # (n_slopes, n_modes) also for a single mode: squeezing a (n, 1) IM would transpose it
            im_measured_tensor = torch.as_tensor(np.vstack([np.atleast_2d(np.asarray(im).T).T for im in interaction_matrix_per_DM]),
                                                 dtype=torch.float64, device=self.device)
            self.im_per_dm.append(im_measured_tensor)

    # Identify active WFS LightPaths (excluding science cameras with no sensor)
    self.active_wfs_lps = []
    for j in range(nLPs):
        if any(interactionMatrix.interaction_matrix_warehouse[i][j]['IM'] is not None for i in range(nDMs)):
            self.active_wfs_lps.append(j)

    # Mode dimensions per DM
    n_modes_target = []
    for i in range(nDMs):
        n_m = modal_basis[i].shape[1] - discarded_modes[i]
        if self.nModes is not None:
            user_n_m = self.nModes[i] if isinstance(self.nModes, list) else self.nModes
            if user_n_m is not None:
                n_m = min(n_m, user_n_m)
        # Never more modes than the measured IM has (an IM measured with fewer modes than the basis)
        if self.im_per_dm[i].shape[0] > 0:
            n_m = min(n_m, self.im_per_dm[i].shape[1])
        n_modes_target.append(n_m)

    # Slope dimensions per active WFS
    n_slopes_per_wfs = {}
    for j in self.active_wfs_lps:
        first_im = next(interactionMatrix.interaction_matrix_warehouse[i][j]['IM']
                        for i in range(nDMs)
                        if interactionMatrix.interaction_matrix_warehouse[i][j]['IM'] is not None)
        n_slopes_per_wfs[j] = first_im.shape[0]

    # Compute Reconstructors: 2D Block Matrix (default) or Independent DM-by-DM
    if joint_reconstruction and len(self.active_wfs_lps) > 0 and reconstructionMethod in {'inversion', 'tikhonov'}:
        # Build 2D block matrix of shape (sum(N_slopes_wfs), sum(N_modes_dms))
        blocks_2d = []
        for j in self.active_wfs_lps:
            row_blocks = []
            n_s = n_slopes_per_wfs[j]
            for i in range(nDMs):
                n_m = n_modes_target[i]
                im = interactionMatrix.interaction_matrix_warehouse[i][j]['IM']
                if t_mask[i, j] and (im is not None):
                    block_im = im[:, :n_m]
                    row_blocks.append(torch.as_tensor(block_im, dtype=torch.float64, device=self.device))
                else:
                    row_blocks.append(torch.zeros((n_s, n_m), dtype=torch.float64, device=self.device))
            blocks_2d.append(row_blocks)

        row_tensors = [torch.cat(row, dim=1) for row in blocks_2d]
        H_global = torch.cat(row_tensors, dim=0)

        if reconstructionMethod == 'inversion':
            rcond_val = min(self.rcond) if isinstance(self.rcond, (list, tuple)) else self.rcond
            R_global = torch.linalg.pinv(H_global, rcond=rcond_val)
        elif reconstructionMethod == 'tikhonov':
            gamma_parts = []
            for i in range(nDMs):
                offset_i = sum(n_modes_target[:i])
                n_m = n_modes_target[i]
                dm_cols = H_global[:, offset_i : offset_i + n_m]
                s_vals = torch.linalg.svdvals(dm_cols)
                s_max = s_vals[0] if len(s_vals) > 0 and s_vals[0] > 0 else torch.tensor(1.0, dtype=torch.float64, device=self.device)
                beta_val = self.beta[i] if isinstance(self.beta, (list, tuple)) else self.beta
                alfa_i = beta_val * (s_max ** 2)
                gamma_parts.append(alfa_i * torch.ones(n_m, dtype=torch.float64, device=self.device))

            Gamma = torch.cat(gamma_parts)
            reg_matrix = H_global.T @ H_global + torch.diag(Gamma)
            R_global = torch.linalg.solve(reg_matrix, H_global.T)

        # Slice reconstructor blocks for each DM
        offset = 0
        for i in range(nDMs):
            n_m = n_modes_target[i]
            reconstructor.append(R_global[offset : offset + n_m, :])
            offset += n_m
    else:
        # Independent DM-by-DM reconstruction
        for i in range(nDMs):
            im_target_list = []
            for j in range(nLPs):
                if t_mask[i, j]:
                    im = interactionMatrix.interaction_matrix_warehouse[i][j]['IM']
                    if self.nModes is not None:
                        n_m = self.nModes[i] if isinstance(self.nModes, list) else self.nModes
                        if n_m is not None:
                            im = im[:, :n_m]
                    im_target_list.append(im)

            if len(im_target_list) == 0:
                self.logger.warning(f'Controller - DM {i} has no associated WFS in the target mask. Setting reconstructor to zero.')
                reconstructor.append(torch.zeros((n_modes_target[i], 0), dtype=torch.float64, device=self.device))
            else:
                im_target_tensor = torch.as_tensor(np.vstack([np.atleast_2d(np.asarray(im).T).T for im in im_target_list]),
                                                   dtype=torch.float64, device=self.device)
                if reconstructionMethod == 'inversion':
                    temp_reconstructor = torch.linalg.pinv(im_target_tensor, self.rcond[i])
                elif reconstructionMethod == 'tikhonov' or reconstructionMethod == 'tomography':
                    H = im_target_tensor
                    U, S, Vh = torch.linalg.svd(H, full_matrices=False)
                    alfa = self.beta[i] * torch.max(S)**2
                    S_reg = S / (S**2 + alfa)
                    temp_reconstructor = Vh.T @ torch.diag(S_reg) @ U.T
                else:
                    self.logger.error('Controller::initializeReconstructor - Unknown reconstructor')
                    raise ValueError('Unknown reconstructor method.')
                reconstructor.append(temp_reconstructor)

    self.logger.info(f'Controller::initializeReconstructor - Reconstruction took {time.time()-t0}[s]')

    return reconstructor, modal_basis, mask, t_mask, discarded_modes

def _init_polc_cross_ims(self, interactionMatrix):
    """
    IMs needed by the pseudo-open-loop slopes of each DM's own slope vector (the WFS of mask row i, in the order
    computeControlAction concatenates them): s_pol_i = s_i + sum_j IM_{j -> WFS(mask i)} c_j(k - d_j). Every DM j that
    is in the optical path of one of those WFS contributes, not only DM i.

    Returns
    -------
    cross : list of list of torch.Tensor or None
        ``cross[i][j]``: IM of DM j on the slopes of mask row i, (n_slopes_i, n_modes_j); None when DM j is in none of
        those light paths.
    missing : list of tuple
        (i, j, lp): DM j is in the optical path of light path lp (in mask row i) but its IM on lp was not measured.
    """
    warehouse = interactionMatrix.interaction_matrix_warehouse
    lps = getattr(interactionMatrix, 'light_path_list', None) or []
    dms = getattr(interactionMatrix, 'dm_scanned_list', None) or []
    nDMs, nLPs = len(warehouse), len(warehouse[0])
    cross, missing = [], []
    for i in range(nDMs):
        row = []
        lp_idx = [k for k in range(nLPs) if self.mask[i, k]]
        for j in range(nDMs):
            n_modes_j = self.reconstructor[j].shape[0]
            blocks, used = [], False
            for k in lp_idx:
                im = warehouse[j][k]['IM']
                n_slopes_k = next((warehouse[m][k]['IM'].shape[0] for m in range(nDMs) if warehouse[m][k]['IM'] is not None), 0)
                if im is not None:
                    blocks.append(np.atleast_2d(np.asarray(im).T).T[:, :n_modes_j]); used = True
                else:
                    in_path = k < len(lps) and j < len(dms) and getattr(lps[k], 'dm', None) is not None and \
                              any(d is dms[j] for d in lps[k].dm)
                    if in_path:
                        missing.append((i, j, k))
                    blocks.append(np.zeros((n_slopes_k, n_modes_j)))
            row.append(torch.as_tensor(np.vstack(blocks), dtype=torch.float64, device=self.device) if used else None)
        cross.append(row)
    return cross, missing

def set_tomography_targets(self, im_target_per_dm, joint=True, release_R_tomo=True):
    """
    Reconstructor of the tomographic (L&A) control law from the interaction matrices of the DMs seen by the target
    (virtual) WFSs, and precomputation of the matrices used online.

    Parameters
    ----------
    im_target_per_dm : list
        One array per DM, [N_target_slopes, n_modes_i], rows in the order of the target slopes of R_tomo.
    joint : bool, optional
        True: one Tikhonov reconstructor of the stacked matrix [D_1 ... D_n], so that the DMs share the fit of the
        target slopes (L&A control matrix C_z = (D_z^T D_z + alpha)^-1 D_z^T, regularisation beta_i * s_max(D_i)^2 per
        DM as in the joint tikhonov reconstructor). False: one reconstructor per DM (every DM fits the whole target).
    release_R_tomo : bool, optional
        Free R_tomo once the products are computed (it is not used online any more).

    Notes
    -----
    The tomography control law of computeControlAction() needs modal_error_i = R_i (R_tomo s_pol - sum_j D_j c_j),
    which is evaluated as M1_i s_pol - M2_i c with M1_i = R_i R_tomo [n_modes_i x N_meas_slopes] and
    M2_i = R_i [D_1 ... D_n]: two small products per iteration instead of R_tomo [N_target x N_meas] on the CPU.
    """
    if not hasattr(self, 'R_tomo') or self.R_tomo is None:
        raise ValueError('Controller::set_tomography_targets - R_tomo is not loaded.')
    nDMs = len(im_target_per_dm)
    D = [torch.as_tensor(np.asarray(im), dtype=torch.float64, device='cpu') for im in im_target_per_dm]
    n_modes = [d.shape[1] for d in D]
    D_all = torch.cat(D, dim=1)
    if joint:
        gamma = []
        for i in range(nDMs):
            s_max = torch.linalg.svdvals(D[i])[0]
            gamma.append(self.beta[i] * s_max ** 2 * torch.ones(n_modes[i], dtype=torch.float64))
        R_all = torch.linalg.solve(D_all.T @ D_all + torch.diag(torch.cat(gamma)), D_all.T)
        R = list(torch.split(R_all, n_modes, dim=0))
    else:
        R = []
        for i in range(nDMs):
            U, S, Vh = torch.linalg.svd(D[i], full_matrices=False)
            alfa = self.beta[i] * torch.max(S) ** 2
            R.append(Vh.T @ torch.diag(S / (S ** 2 + alfa)) @ U.T)
    self.reconstructor = [r.to(self.device) for r in R]
    self.im_target_per_dm = [d.to(self.device) for d in D]
    self.tomo_M1 = [(r @ self.R_tomo).to(self.device) for r in R]
    self.tomo_M2 = [(r @ D_all).to(self.device) for r in R]
    if release_R_tomo:
        self.R_tomo = None
    self.logger.info(f"Controller::set_tomography_targets - {'joint' if joint else 'per-DM'} target reconstructor, "
                     f"online matrices {[tuple(m.shape) for m in self.tomo_M1]}")

def initializeController(self, controllerType, reconstructor):
    """
    Initialize the control state (history buffers) based on the controller type.

    Parameters
    ----------
    controllerType : str
        Type of controller ('leaky', 'forwardPI', 'backwardPI', 'stateSpace').
    reconstructor : list
        List of reconstructor matrices per DM.

    Returns
    -------
    bool
        True if initialization succeeds.
    """
    buffer_size = max(max(self.delay), 1)
    self.command_history = [
        [torch.zeros((reconstructor[i].shape[0], 1), dtype=torch.float64, device=self.device) for i in range(len(reconstructor))]
        for _ in range(buffer_size)
    ]
    self.slopes_res = None
    self.slopes_polc = None

    if controllerType == 'leaky':
        self.command_previous = [torch.zeros((reconstructor[i].shape[0],1), dtype=torch.float64, device=self.device) for i in range(len(reconstructor))]
    elif controllerType == 'forwardPI' or controllerType == 'backwardPI':
        self.command_previous = [torch.zeros((reconstructor[i].shape[0],1), dtype=torch.float64, device=self.device) for i in range(len(reconstructor))]
        self.error_previous = [torch.zeros((reconstructor[i].shape[0],1), dtype=torch.float64, device=self.device) for i in range(len(reconstructor))]
    elif controllerType == 'stateSpace':
        self.state_previous = []
        self.A_tensor = []
        self.B_tensor = []
        self.C_tensor = []
        self.D_tensor = []

        for i in range(len(reconstructor)):
            n_inputs = reconstructor[i].shape[0]
            n_outputs = n_inputs

            A_i = torch.as_tensor(self.A[i], dtype=torch.float64, device=self.device)
            B_i = torch.as_tensor(self.B[i], dtype=torch.float64, device=self.device)
            C_i = torch.as_tensor(self.C[i], dtype=torch.float64, device=self.device)

            if A_i.ndim != 2 or A_i.shape[0] != A_i.shape[1]:
                raise ValueError(f"Matrix A for DM {i} must be a square 2D matrix.")

            n_states = A_i.shape[0]

            if B_i.ndim != 2 or B_i.shape[0] != n_states or B_i.shape[1] != n_inputs:
                raise ValueError(f"Matrix B for DM {i} must have shape ({n_states}, {n_inputs}).")

            if C_i.ndim != 2 or C_i.shape[0] != n_outputs or C_i.shape[1] != n_states:
                raise ValueError(f"Matrix C for DM {i} must have shape ({n_outputs}, {n_states}).")

            if self.D is not None and self.D[i] is not None:
                D_i = torch.as_tensor(self.D[i], dtype=torch.float64, device=self.device)
                if D_i.ndim != 2 or D_i.shape[0] != n_outputs or D_i.shape[1] != n_inputs:
                    raise ValueError(f"Matrix D for DM {i} must have shape ({n_outputs}, {n_inputs}).")
            else:
                D_i = torch.zeros((n_outputs, n_inputs), dtype=torch.float64, device=self.device)

            self.A_tensor.append(A_i)
            self.B_tensor.append(B_i)
            self.C_tensor.append(C_i)
            self.D_tensor.append(D_i)

            self.state_previous.append(torch.zeros((n_states, 1), dtype=torch.float64, device=self.device))
    else:
        self.logger.error('Controller::initializeController - Unknown controller')
        raise ValueError('Unknown controller.')
    return True
