    source_file : str
        Vibration filename, the data is expected in arcsec on sky.
    """        
    # Setup the logger to handle the queue of info, warning and errors msgs in the simulator
    self.logger = logger if logger is not None else get_logger()

    # Define class attributes
    self.tag = 'vibrations'

    # Load vibrations sequence

    self.x_vibrations_arcsec, self.y_vibrations_arcsec, self.Ts = self.load(source_file)

    # Sampling time sanity check
    if self.Ts != telescope.samplingTime:
        self.logger.error(f'Vibrations sampling time ({self.Ts}s) does not match the Telescope\'s sampling time ({telescope.samplingTime}s)')
        raise ValueError('Vibrations sampling time does not match the telescope\'s.')

    # Generate base phase

    # Pixel centres of the pupil grid (i - (N-1)/2) D/N, normalised by D/2: the mode is x / (D/2) exactly (a linspace(-1, 1, N)
    # would put the edge pixels at +-D/2 and scale every tilt by N/(N-1))
    n = telescope.pupil.shape[0]
    x = (np.arange(n) - (n - 1) / 2) * 2 / n
    self.x_mode = np.tile(x, (x.shape[0],1)) * telescope.pupil
    self.y_mode = self.x_mode.T

    # Compute modal amplitude [m]: the modes span [-1, 1] over the pupil (D/2 in metres), so a tilt of theta [rad]
    # on sky is an OPD of theta * D/2 at the edge

    self.x_vibrations_stroke = telescope.D / 2 * (self.x_vibrations_arcsec / 206265)
    self.y_vibrations_stroke = telescope.D / 2 * (self.y_vibrations_arcsec / 206265)

def load(self, filename): 
    """
    Load a vibration temporal sequence from a H5 file.

    Parameters
    ----------
    filename : str
        Path and base filename (with extension) of the H5 file to load.

    Returns
    -------
    np.ndarray
        X-axis vibrations
    np.ndarray
        Y-axis vibrations
    float
        Sampling time of the vibration sequence

    """
    self.logger.debug('Vibration::load')


    if not filename.endswith(".h5"):
        filename += ".h5"        

    with h5py.File(filename, 'r') as f:

        x_vibrations = f['x_axis']['data'][()]
        y_vibrations = f['y_axis']['data'][()]
        Ts = f['x_axis'].attrs['Ts']

        self.logger.info(f"Vibration::load - Loaded vibrations.")     

    return x_vibrations, y_vibrations, Ts

def getCurrentVibrations(self, iteration):
    """
    Return the vibrations for the iteration asked.

    Parameters
    ----------
    iteration : int
        Iteration of the AO simulation. If iteration is larger than
        the temporal sequence of the vibrations, the method wraps-around.

    Returns
    -------
    np.ndarray
        Vibration combining X-Y vibrations for the given iteration
    """        
    if ((iteration+1) > len(self.x_vibrations_stroke)) or ((iteration+1) > len(self.y_vibrations_stroke)):
        self.logger.warning('Vibration::getCurrentVibrations - The length of the vibrations array is smaller than the simulation window. Wrapping-around.')
        iteration = iteration % np.minimum(len(self.x_vibrations_stroke), len(self.y_vibrations_stroke))

    opd_vibrations = self.x_vibrations_stroke[iteration]*self.x_mode + self.y_vibrations_stroke[iteration]*self.y_mode

    return opd_vibrations

docs.title: Validation suite
docs.text: SAOS is validated by the test suite in tests/. Each test isolates one module, feeds it synthetic input and compares the result with an independent physical or mathematical reference (closed-form theory written in the tests, never SAOS code). This section documents every test: what it checks, the module it covers, the theory and assumptions behind the reference, the tolerance and the references.

docs.title: Tiers
docs.text:
Tier Marker Content Where Duration T1 fast Module physics at small scale, deterministic seeds CPU < 5 min T2 nightly More realisations, extended object, CPU vs GPU, packaging Workstation (GPU optional) < 45 min T3 heavy Reduced MCAO scenarios (planned, no tests yet) Workstation < 1 h

gpu marks tests that need CUDA (skipped when no GPU is visible).

docs.title: Running
docs.text:
ci/run_ci.sh fast                 # T1 (forces CPU)
ci/run_ci.sh nightly              # T1 + T2
ci/run_ci.sh fast -k wfs -x       # extra arguments go to pytest
python -m pytest tests -m fast    # plain pytest

Results, figures and an HTML report go to ~/simulations/results/ci/<date>_<tier>_<sha>/ (override with SAOS_CI_ROOT); see ci/README.md for the nightly timer, the git hooks and the GitHub workflow.

docs.title: Tolerance policy
docs.text: Tolerances (tests/tolerances/*.yaml) only cover the statistical uncertainty of the estimator (about 3.5 sigma, measured over several seed sets) or the numerical precision of the reference. A systematic offset is either corrected or an explicit, documented convention.

docs.title: Conventions and common theory
docs.text:
Conventions used by every test (from tests/citools.py): report.check(name, value, expected, rtol, atol, lo, hi) passes when \(|v-e| \le \mathrm{atol} + \mathrm{rtol}\,|e|\) (expected given) or \(\mathrm{lo}\le v\le \mathrm{hi}\) (bounds given), element-wise for arrays; report.assert_ok() fails the test with all out-of-tolerance metrics after every metric has been recorded. report.metric records a value with no pass/fail criterion. Statistical tolerances in the YAML files are, unless stated otherwise, \(3.5\sigma\) of the estimator measured over several seeds. Phase screens are in rad at 500 nm; OPD in m, and \(\varphi = 2\pi\,\mathrm{OPD}/500\,\mathrm{nm}\).

Analytic references (tests/theory.py, independent of SAOS) used by the atmosphere tests:

\[\Phi(f) = 0.0229\, r_0^{-5/3}\left(f^2 + L_0^{-2}\right)^{-11/6}\ \mathrm{[rad^2\,m^2]},\qquad C(0) = 0.0229\,\pi\,\tfrac{6}{5}\,r_0^{-5/3} L_0^{5/3}\approx 0.0863\,(L_0/r_0)^{5/3}\] \[C(r) = C(0)\,\frac{2^{1/6}}{\Gamma(5/6)}\,x^{5/6}K_{5/6}(x),\quad x = \frac{2\pi r}{L_0},\qquad D(r) = 2\,[C(0)-C(r)] \xrightarrow{\,r\ll L_0\,} 6.88\,(r/r_0)^{5/3}\]

docs.title: test_atmosphere.py — von Kármán screens, extrusion, layer geometry, footprints and wind (T1)
docs.text:
Source: tests/test_atmosphere.py

Covers SAOS.infinitePhaseScreen.PhaseScreenVonKarman (initial FFT screen with subharmonics, add_row/add_col extrusion, phase_covariance), SAOS.Atmosphere (initializeAtmosphere, update, getOPD, get_pupil_footprint, save/load, per-layer r0, altitude, size and pixel scale) and the pupil of SAOS.Telescope. The strategy is to compare ensemble statistics of generated screens (structure function, PSD, joint \(r_0\)/\(L_0\) least-squares fit in \(\log D\)) against closed-form von Kármán expressions written independently in tests/theory.py, and to check the deterministic geometry (layer scaling, footprint displacement on a prescribed linear phase ramp, frozen-flow shifts, seeds, save/load) by exact or integer-pixel comparisons. The whole module is fast.

docs.title: test_theory_references_self_consistent
docs.text:
• Module: none from SAOS; checks the references of tests/theory.py (vk_psd, vk_covariance, vk_structure, kolmogorov_structure).
  • Tier: fast (module-level mark).
  • What it checks: that the closed-form covariance at \(r = 0, 0.05, 0.5, 5\) m equals the numerical Hankel transform of the PSD (scipy.integrate.quad, \(r_0 = 0.10\) m, \(L_0 = 25\) m), and that \(D_{vK}/D_{Kolmogorov}\to 1\) at \(r = 1, 10\) mm for \(L_0 = 10^5\) m.
  • Theory / assumptions: isotropic 2-D field, so the covariance is the Hankel transform of the PSD:
\[C(r) = \int_0^\infty 2\pi f\,\Phi(f)\,J_0(2\pi f r)\,\mathrm{d}f .\]

For \(r\ll L_0\) the outer-scale correction to \(D\) is \(O((r/L_0)^{1/3})\). - Tolerance: atmosphere.theory.hankel = \(10^{-4}\) (quadrature accuracy); atmosphere.theory.kolmogorov_limit = 0.01 (leading correction about 0.7 %). - References: Roddier 1981 (Prog. Opt. 19); Assémat, Wilson & Gendron 2006 for the covariance form.

docs.title: test_saos_phase_covariance_matches_theory
docs.text:
• Module: PhaseScreenVonKarman.phase_covariance.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: the SAOS covariance function (documented as Assémat & Wilson eq. 5) divided by the independent \(C(r)\) for \(r = 0\) and 30 log-spaced values between 1 mm and 100 m (\(r_0 = 0.10\) m, \(L_0 = 25\) m). It also records \(C(0)/(L_0/r_0)^{5/3}\) as a metric.
  • Theory / assumptions: von Kármán covariance \(C(r)\) as above.
  • Tolerance: relative \(10^{-6}\) (hard-coded in the test; numerical agreement of two evaluations of the same closed form).
  • References: Assémat, Wilson & Gendron 2006, Opt. Express 14:988.

docs.title: test_initial_screen_structure_function
docs.text:
• Module: PhaseScreenVonKarman.initial_screen (FFT screen, subharmonics, 4x oversized grid, cropped).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: the mean structure function along \(x\) and \(y\) of 200 screens of 64 px (4 m, \(r_0 = 0.10\) m, \(L_0 = 25\) m) against \(D_{vK}\), in two ranges of lag (4 px to \(n_x/4\) and \(n_x/4\) to \(n_x/2\)); the mean \(D_x/D_y\) anisotropy over 4 to 16 px; and the recovery of \(r_0\) from a joint \(r_0\)/\(L_0\) fit and from an \(r_0\)-only fit with \(L_0\) fixed. \(L_0\) from the joint fit and the ratio at 1 px are only recorded.
  • Theory / assumptions: \(D(r) = \langle[\varphi(\mathbf{x}+\mathbf{r})-\varphi(\mathbf{x})]^2\rangle\) equals \(D_{vK}(r)\) (ergodic average over pixels and 200 realisations). The docstring notes that an FFT screen lacks power above Nyquist, so \(D(1\,\mathrm{px})\approx 0.92\,D_{vK}\); small lags are therefore not asserted. A 4 m screen does not span the \(L_0\) turnover, so \(L_0\) is weakly constrained.
  • Tolerance: atmosphere.initial_screen: D_ratio_small_r 0.05, D_ratio_large_r 0.08, anisotropy 0.12, r0_joint 0.04, r0_fixed 0.03 (absolute on ratios; about \(3.5\sigma\) over 10 seeds, 2026-10-26).
  • References: Lane, Glindemann & Dainty 1992 (subharmonic FFT screens); Johansson & Gavel 1994 (FFT screen generation).

docs.title: test_extruded_screen_structure_function
docs.text:
• Module: PhaseScreenVonKarman.add_row (Assémat–Wilson extrusion with far-row stencil).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: after a burn-in of \(n_x\) rows, the structure function of a 32 px (2 m) screen sampled every \(n_x\) rows over 4000 rows (about 124 samples) against \(D_{vK}\) for 1 px to \(n_x/2\), averaged over axes (two lag ranges) and per axis (across and along the motion), plus the same \(r_0\) fits as above. \(D_y/D_{vK}\) at \(n_x/2\) is recorded as a trend metric.
  • Theory / assumptions: the extruded rows are built from the sampled covariance, so they do not show the sub-Nyquist deficit of the FFT screen; the ensemble average replaces the stationary ensemble.
  • Tolerance: atmosphere.extruded_screen: D_ratio_small_r 0.08, D_ratio_large_r 0.15, D_ratio_axis 0.20, r0_joint 0.06, r0_fixed 0.05 (about \(3.5\sigma\) over 10 seeds; sigma 0.016 to 0.087).
  • References: Assémat, Wilson & Gendron 2006, Opt. Express 14:988.

docs.title: test_outer_scale_initial_screen
docs.text:
• Module: PhaseScreenVonKarman.initial_screen.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: with a screen that spans the turnover of the spectrum (128 px of 0.5 m = 64 m = 2.6 \(L_0\); \(r_0 = 0.5\) m, \(L_0 = 25\) m), the joint \(r_0\)/\(L_0\) fit of the mean \(D(r)\) of 40 screens (lags from 2 px to 32 m) returns the generation parameters. The ratio \(D/D_{vK}\) at 32 m is recorded.
  • Theory / assumptions: the flattening of \(D_{vK}(r)\) towards \(2C(0)\) for \(r\gtrsim L_0\) determines \(L_0\); the pixel is chosen so that pixel\(/r_0 = 1\) (resolved), and lag 1 px is excluded from the fit because it is below the sampling of a pixelated screen.
  • Tolerance: atmosphere.outer_scale_initial: L0_atol 0.075 and r0_atol 0.025 on the fitted/true ratios (\(3.5\sigma\); measured sigma 0.021 and 0.007).
  • References: Assémat, Wilson & Gendron 2006; Roddier 1981.

docs.title: test_outer_scale_extruded_screen
docs.text:
• Module: PhaseScreenVonKarman.add_row.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: the same outer-scale recovery on an extruded screen of 64 px of 1 m (\(r_0 = 1\) m, \(L_0 = 25\) m) sampled every \(n_x\) rows over 20000 rows (312 samples), fit from 2 px to \(n_x/2 = 32\) m.
  • Theory / assumptions: as in the initial-screen version.
  • Tolerance: atmosphere.outer_scale_extruded: L0_atol 0.035, r0_atol 0.014 (\(3.5\sigma\); sigma 0.010 and 0.004 over 10 seeds).
  • References: Assémat, Wilson & Gendron 2006.

docs.title: test_extruded_screen_low_frequencies
docs.text:
• Module: PhaseScreenVonKarman.add_row.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: \(D(r)\) at \(r = n_x/8, n_x/4, n_x/2\) px along (\(y\)) and across (\(x\)) the extrusion, for a 32 px (2 m) screen, averaged over 16 independent screens of 40000 rows each (sampled every \(n_x\) rows), against \(D_{vK}\). Per-lag standard errors of the mean are recorded.
  • Theory / assumptions: the ensemble (standard error about 0.009) resolves whether the extrusion truncates low frequencies.
  • Tolerance: atmosphere.extruded_lowfreq.atol = 0.031 = \(3.5\times\) the largest standard error of the mean with 16 screens (\(0.035/\sqrt{16}\) = 0.0088, \(D_x\) at \(n_x/2\)); measured means 0.999 to 1.008.
  • References: none specific.

docs.title: test_extrusion_directions_are_mirror_images
docs.text:
• Module: PhaseScreenVonKarman.add_row, add_col (both signs of motion).
  • Tier: fast. Parametrised over axis = row, col.
  • What it checks: two screens with the same seed, the second one initialised with the mirror image of the first along rows (or columns), are extruded for \(3n_x\) steps in opposite directions (+1 and -1); the first must equal the mirror of the second. This verifies that stencils and the A/B matrices are consistent in both directions. Convention-only check, no physical theory.
  • Tolerance: max absolute difference \(\le 10^{-10}\) rad (hard-coded).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_screen_psd
docs.text:
• Module: PhaseScreenVonKarman.initial_screen.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: the radially averaged periodogram of 200 initial 64 px screens (Hann window, mean removed, normalised to rad\(^2\) m\(^2\) by \(\Delta x^2/(n\sum w^2)\)) against \(\Phi(f)\) in the band \(6/L \le f \le 0.3/\Delta x\) (amplitude ratio per bin) and the log-log slope against the slope of the theoretical PSD in the same band (asymptotically \(-11/3\)).
  • Theory / assumptions: Welch-type periodogram with a window; the lowest bins are excluded because of window leakage and the upper limit stays below Nyquist to avoid aliasing.
  • Tolerance: atmosphere.psd: amplitude 0.15 (ratio), slope 0.15 (absolute).
  • References: Roddier 1981

docs.title: test_layer_r0_and_altitude_scaling
docs.text:
• Module: Atmosphere.__init__ / initializeAtmosphere layer set-up.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: for a 3-layer profile (fractions 0.5/0.3/0.2, altitudes 0/4/12 km, zenith 30 deg, 2 m telescope, 40 arcsec field): layer \(r_{0,i}\) (stored in fractionalR0) against theory, \(\sum r_{0,i}^{-5/3}\) against \((r_0\cos^{0.6}z)^{-5/3}\), layer altitude against \(h/\cos z\), layer size D_fov against \(D + 2\tan(\mathrm{fov}/2)h_i\), and that \(n_{pix}\times\) pixel exceeds the layer size by less than two pixels (symmetric whole-pixel margin). The layer-pixel to telescope-pixel deviation is recorded.
  • Theory / assumptions: Cn\(^2\) integral along a slanted path:
\[r_{0,i} = r_0\,(\cos z)^{3/5} f_i^{-3/5},\qquad \sum_i r_{0,i}^{-5/3} = \left(r_0 \cos^{3/5} z\right)^{-5/3},\qquad h_i' = h_i/\cos z .\]
  • Tolerance: relative \(10^{-12}\) for r0 and altitude; \(10^{-5}\) for the layer size (arcsec to rad conversion with 206265); margin in \([-10^{-9}, 2]\) pixels.
  • References: Roddier 1981.

docs.title: test_layer_pixel_equals_pupil_pixel
docs.text:
• Module: Atmosphere layer sampling (spatial_res, D_fov, npix).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: the layer pixel pitch equals the pupil pixel \(D/\mathrm{res}\) for four layers at 0, 3, 7.5 and 12 km (2 m, 32 px, 40 arcsec). A geometry convention (otherwise the pupil cut from the layer would not be \(D\) wide).
  • Tolerance: relative \(10^{-6}\) (hard-coded).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_pupil_area
docs.text:
• Module: Telescope.pupil.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: the pupil pixel count against the analytic area of an annulus, \(\frac{\pi}{4}N^2(1-\epsilon^2)\) with \(\epsilon = 0.3\) central obstruction, for \(N = 64\) and 128.
  • Tolerance: absolute 0.01 on the ratio (1 %, hard-coded; sampling error of the pixelated edge).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_footprint_displacement_direction
docs.text:
• Module: Atmosphere.getOPD / get_pupil_footprint (off-axis footprint on a layer).
  • Tier: fast. Parametrised over azimuth az = 0, 90, 180, 270 deg.
  • What it checks: a source at an angle giving \(h\tan\theta = 0.2\) m at a 10 km layer (\(\theta\approx 4.1\) arcsec) samples the layer 0.2 m away along its azimuth, \((\Delta_{col},\Delta_{row}) = d(\cos az,\sin az)\). Measured on a prescribed linear phase ramp \(\varphi = g\,x\) (or \(g\,y\), \(g = 0.05\) rad/m): the mean OPD difference between the off-axis and on-axis source gives the displacement independently of SAOS's pixel policy. The layer is made exactly \(2D\) wide by tuning the field of view. The displacement 0.2 m is two 0.1 m pixels, so the footprint is rounded to the nearest layer pixel.
  • Theory / assumptions: frozen layer at altitude \(h\) is seen along the line of sight displaced by \(h\tan\theta\); a linear ramp makes the OPD difference proportional to the displacement, \(\Delta\mathrm{OPD}\cdot 2\pi/\lambda_{atm} = g\,\Delta\).
  • Tolerance: atmosphere.footprint.atol_m = \(10^{-6}\) m (float precision of the OPD difference, about \(10^{-5}\) px).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_footprint_displacement_fractional
docs.text:
• Module: Atmosphere.getOPD / get_pupil_footprint.
  • Tier: fast. Parametrised over \((d, az)\) = (0.16, 0), (0.09, 90), (0.04, 37), (0.15, 215), (0.16, 127), (0.09, 300) (metres, degrees).
  • What it checks: fractional footprint offsets (0.4 to 1.6 layer pixels of 0.1 m, no component within 0.05 px of a half pixel) follow the integer-pixel model, \(\mathrm{round}(d\cos az/p)\,p\) and \(\mathrm{round}(d\sin az/p)\,p\) with \(p = 0.1\) m, exactly; and lie within half a pixel of the physical \(h\tan\theta\) (unbiased rounding). Same linear-ramp measurement as above.
  • Tolerance: atmosphere.footprint.atol_m = \(10^{-6}\) m for the model comparison; \(|\Delta-h\tan\theta|/p\le 0.5+10^{-6}\) for the physical comparison.
  • References: none (SAOS convention documented in the test).

docs.title: test_wind_motion
docs.text:
• Module: Atmosphere.update (layer shift), PhaseScreenVonKarman.add_row / add_col.
  • Tier: fast. Parametrised over (px/step, direction deg) = (0.5, 0), (0.5, 180), (0.5, 90), (0.5, 270), (0.5, 45), (2.5, 0).
  • What it checks: after 10 snapshots (every \(\max(1,\lfloor 2/v\rfloor)\) steps) the accumulated content shift, measured by least-squares integer shift between successive layer screens (citools.integer_shift, \(\pm4\) px), equals \(v\,N\,T_s/\mathrm{pixel}\) along the wind direction, in the same frame as source azimuths (0 deg to +column, 90 deg to +row).
  • Theory / assumptions: Taylor frozen flow, \(\varphi(\mathbf{x},t)=\varphi(\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{v}t,0)\), implemented with integer-pixel motion (documented 1 px/step cap in the SAOS memory); hence the comparison is within \(\pm1\) px.
  • Tolerance: absolute 1.0 px on rows and columns (hard-coded; integer-pixel motion).
  • References: none specific (Taylor hypothesis).

docs.title: test_same_seed_reproducible
docs.text:
• Module: Atmosphere.initializeAtmosphere(randomState), Atmosphere.update.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: two atmospheres with the same randomState produce identical OPD after 25 updates (single layer at 0 m, 3 m/s, 30 deg); a different seed gives a different OPD (rms of the difference over rms of OPD \(\ge 0.5\)).
  • Tolerance: difference exactly 0 for the same seed; \(\ge 0.5\) for the different seed (hard-coded).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_save_load_initial_state
docs.text:
• Module: Atmosphere.save, Atmosphere.load (HDF5).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: the layer screen of a saved atmosphere (5 km layer) and that of a fresh atmosphere that loads the file are identical.
  • Tolerance: exact (max absolute difference 0).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_save_load_continues_identically
docs.text:
• Module: Atmosphere.save, Atmosphere.load, Atmosphere.update.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: after 7 updates the state is saved and loaded into a second atmosphere; after 20 further updates both give the same OPD, so the extrusion state (random stream, stencil buffers) is preserved.
  • Tolerance: \(\mathrm{rms}(\mathrm{OPD}_1-\mathrm{OPD}_2)/\mathrm{rms}(\mathrm{OPD})\le10^{-12}\).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_save_load_many_layers_order
docs.text:
• Module: Atmosphere.save, Atmosphere.load.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: with 11 layers (0 to 10 km) every loaded layer keeps its altitude, i.e. the layer order survives the round trip (more than 9 layers exercises double-digit layer indices).
  • Tolerance: absolute \(10^{-6}\) m on the altitude difference.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_odd_resolution_and_zero_cn2_layer
docs.text:
• Module: Telescope / Atmosphere.getOPD edge cases.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: with an odd pupil sampling (31 px) an off-axis source returns a \(31\times31\) finite OPD, and a layer with zero Cn\(^2\) fraction has a screen identically 0 and does not crash.
  • Tolerance: exact (shape equality, finiteness, max \(|\varphi| = 0\)).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_random_seed_when_not_given
docs.text:
• Module: Atmosphere.initializeAtmosphere, attribute randomState.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: without randomState two atmospheres differ, and the stored randomState reproduces exactly the screen of the first one.
  • Tolerance: exact.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_chromatic_shift_is_a_common_vector
docs.text:
• Module: Atmosphere.get_pupil_footprint, Source(chromatic_shift=...).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: the chromatic shift is an on-sky vector per layer, added to the source direction: an on-axis source with shift (4", 0) on the 5 km layer has the same footprint as a source at 4" azimuth 0; a source at 4" azimuth 90 with that shift has the same footprint as one at \(4\sqrt2\)" azimuth 45. Convention check on integer footprints.
  • Tolerance: exact array equality.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_atmosphere_t2.py — atmosphere at EST scale: r0 scan, Zernike variances, frozen flow, anisoplanatism, seeing (T2)
docs.text:
Source: tests/test_atmosphere_t2.py

Covers PhaseScreenVonKarman (initial and extruded screens), Atmosphere (multi-layer OPD, footprints), Telescope, Source and ScienceCam at the EST geometry (D = 4.149 m, 216 px, 1.92 cm/px, \(L_0\) = 25 m, \(T_s\) = 1 ms). All references are written inside the test module (von Kármán formulas, Noll Zernike basis orthonormalised on the sampled pupil, exact pupil covariance, finite-aperture long-exposure OTF), independent of SAOS. Statistics are larger than in T1 and several tests use a thread pool. The whole module is nightly. Tolerances come from tests/tolerances/atmosphere_t2.yaml (calibrated 2026-10-27 over 6 seed sets, each \(3.5\times\) the per-run sd, scaled by \(1/\sqrt n\) when \(n\) differs from the calibration run; none is derived from a SAOS-vs-theory offset).

docs.title: test_r0_scan_pupil_scale
docs.text:
• Module: PhaseScreenVonKarman.initial_screen and add_row.
  • Tier: nightly. Parametrised over source = initial, extruded.
  • What it checks: for \(r_0\) = 0.05, 0.08, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.30, 1.0 m, the mean structure function of 16 screens of 216 px (initial FFT screens, or one extruded screen sampled every \(2n_x\) rows after a burn-in of \(n_x\) rows; the YAML gives n_maps = 16, the docstring still says 32) is fitted (lags 1 px to \(n_x/2\)) for \(r_0\) jointly with \(L_0\) and with \(L_0\) fixed. Fitted/true \(r_0\) must be 1 and the joint \(L_0\) ratio must lie in \([e^{-t}, e^{t}]\).
  • Theory / assumptions: \(D_{vK}(r; r_0, L_0)\) above; a pupil-sized screen (\(\approx 0.16\,L_0\)) only weakly constrains \(L_0\), hence a tolerance on \(\log L_0\).
  • Tolerance: atmosphere_t2.r0_scan.{initial,extruded}: r0_joint, r0_fixed (per \(r_0\); initial 0.032 / 0.116, extruded 0.077 / 0.123) and logL0 (0.95 initial, 1.6 extruded), all \(3.5\sigma\) over seeds.
  • References: Assémat, Wilson & Gendron 2006; Roddier 1981.

docs.title: test_outer_scale_recovery
docs.text:
• Module: PhaseScreenVonKarman.initial_screen.
  • Tier: nightly. Parametrised over L0_true = 5, 12, 25 m.
  • What it checks: screens of 38.4 m (256 px of 15 cm, \(r_0\) = 0.3 m) that span the turnover; joint \(r_0\)/\(L_0\) fit of the mean \(D(r)\) of 24 initial screens (lags 0.45 m to 19 m) recovers \(L_0\) (within \(e^{\pm t}\)) and \(r_0\).
  • Theory / assumptions: as for the T1 outer-scale tests.
  • Tolerance: atmosphere_t2.outer_scale.L0_{5,12,25}: r0 0.011 / 0.028 / 0.032 and logL0 0.021 / 0.084 / 0.112 (\(3.5\sigma\) over seeds).
  • References: Assémat, Wilson & Gendron 2006.

docs.title: test_zernike_variances_initial_screen
docs.text:
• Module: PhaseScreenVonKarman.initial_screen.
  • Tier: nightly.
  • What it checks: the variances of the Z2 to Z11 coefficients of 1000 initial 216 px screens (\(r_0\) = 0.10 m, \(L_0\) = 25 m; the docstring still says 600) on the circular pupil against the exact von Kármán projection computed on the sampled pupil; the mean of the ratios over Z2 to Z11; and the largest off-diagonal element of the whitened covariance (Cholesky of the theory), which must be near zero.
  • Theory / assumptions: the coefficients are \(a_j = \frac{1}{N}\sum_{\mathrm{pupil}}\varphi Z_j\) with Noll-normalised Zernikes orthonormalised on the sampled pupil; their covariance is \(G = B^{T}CB\), the sampled covariance \(C\) projected on the basis (computed by FFT convolution of the sampled \(C(r)\) with each basis vector). Gaussian variance estimator: relative sd \(\sqrt{2/n}\).
  • Tolerance: atmosphere_t2.zernike.initial: mode 0.27, mean 0.085, offdiag 0.18, with \(n\) = 1000 (\(3.5\,\mathrm{sd}_{200}/\sqrt5\); off-diagonal limit adds \(3.5\times0.06/\sqrt5\) to the expected \(0.20/\sqrt5\)).
  • References: Noll 1976, JOSA 66:207.

docs.title: test_zernike_variances_atmosphere
docs.text:
• Module: Atmosphere (3 layers at 0/5/12 km, 60/30/10 % Cn\(^2\), total \(r_0\) = 0.12 m, winds 0/90/0 deg), Atmosphere.updateLayer, getOPD.
  • Tier: nightly.
  • What it checks: the same Z2 to Z11 variance ratios and whitened covariance as above for the on-axis OPD, after burn-in, with 1000 samples from 4 independent atmospheres spaced 1000 rows (19 m, decorrelated beyond \(L_0\)).
  • Theory / assumptions: a sum of independent layers with \(\sum r_{0,i}^{-5/3} = r_0^{-5/3}\) and a common \(L_0\) has the von Kármán covariance of \(r_0\). The measured mean ratio is about 0.96 (Z4 about 0.78, Z10 about 0.88), so the tolerances are set from the observed spread.
  • Tolerance: atmosphere_t2.zernike.atmosphere: mode 0.16, mean 0.033, offdiag 0.14, \(n\) = 1000.
  • References: Noll 1976, JOSA 66:207.

docs.title: test_taylor_frozen_flow
docs.text:
• Module: Atmosphere.update, Atmosphere.getOPD (single layer).
  • Tier: nightly. Parametrised over (k px/step, direction deg) = (1, 0), (1, 90), (2, 0).
  • What it checks: the temporal structure function of the on-axis OPD of one layer, averaged over the 216 x 216 px and 2000 steps after a burn-in of \(2n_x\) steps, at delays \(\tau\) = 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, 34, 54, 80, 108 steps (limited to \(k\tau\le108\) px), against the spatial \(D_{vK}\) at \(r = k\tau\,\mathrm{px}\). The effective speed ratio (mean ratio on \(r\le n_x/4\) to the power 0.6) is recorded.
  • Theory / assumptions: Taylor frozen flow,
\[D_\varphi(\tau) = \langle[\varphi(t+\tau)-\varphi(t)]^2\rangle = D_{vK}(v\tau T_s),\qquad D\propto v^{5/3}\ (r\ll L_0),\]

independent of the direction of motion; integer pixels per step. - Tolerance: atmosphere_t2.frozen_flow: per-delay absolute tolerance on the ratio, small_r = [0.12, 0.16, 0.19, 0.23, 0.29, 0.34, 0.40, 0.48, 0.61] and large_r = [0.80, 1.01]; \(3.5\times\) the largest sd of the (1,0) and (1,90) cases, indexed by delay and therefore conservative for \(k>1\). The tolerances are wide at large \(\tau\) because few independent samples cover the screen. - References: Taylor frozen-flow hypothesis (Conan 1995 discusses temporal statistics; the test uses the structure function, not spectra).

docs.title: test_anisoplanatism
docs.text:
• Module: Atmosphere.getOPD for off-axis Source, footprint model.
  • Tier: nightly.
  • What it checks: the mean over the pupil and over 96 samples of \((\mathrm{OPD}(\theta)-\mathrm{OPD}(0))^2\) for \(\theta\) = 5, 10, 15, 20 arcsec (4 layers, \(r_0\) = 0.12 m, fractions 0.5/0.2/0.2/0.1, altitudes 0, about 1.6, 4, 8 km tuned to integer-pixel offsets), both pointwise and after removing the pupil mean (piston), against theory.
  • Theory / assumptions: independent layers, each with \(r_{0,i} = r_0 f_i^{-3/5}\) and shift \(s_i = h_i\tan\theta\):
\[\langle\Delta\varphi^2\rangle_{pw} = \sum_i D_i(s_i) = \sum_i 2\,[C_i(0)-C_i(s_i)],\]

and with piston removed the variance is reduced by \(\frac{1}{N^2}\sum_{\mathbf{p},\mathbf{q}}\sum_i\left[2C_i(\mathbf{d})-C_i(\mathbf{d}+\mathbf{s}_i)-C_i(\mathbf{d}-\mathbf{s}_i)\right]\) (\(\mathbf d=\mathbf p-\mathbf q\)), computed with the autocorrelation of the sampled circular pupil. Altitudes are chosen so the footprint offsets are \(n+0.02\) px, to decouple rounding of the integer-pixel footprint from the physics. - Tolerance: atmosphere_t2.aniso: rel = 0.15 on the SAOS/theory ratio with \(n\) = 96 (\(3.5\,\mathrm{sd}_{32}/\sqrt3\); worst sd\(_{32}\) = 0.073). - References: none specific; the pupil-covariance computation is the test's own.

docs.title: test_seeing_limited_fwhm
docs.text:
• Module: Atmosphere + ScienceCam.get_frame (no AO).
  • Tier: nightly. Parametrised over \(r_0\) = 0.10, 0.15, 0.25 m.
  • What it checks: the FWHM of the long exposure of 480 ScienceCam frames (6 atmospheres x 80 frames spaced 16 m along the motion; one layer, \(L_0\) = 25 m, 500 nm, 1.5 px per \(\lambda/D\), 3.6 arcsec field) against the exact expected long exposure of the finite aperture, and first that the Tokovinin formula agrees with that reference. FWHM is measured on the azimuthal mean about the optical axis (quadratic peak fit, linear half-maximum crossing), with the same estimator on reference and SAOS.
  • Theory / assumptions: long-exposure OTF \(T(\rho)=T_{tel}(\rho)\exp[-D_{vK}(\rho)/2]\) (finite aperture) evaluated by FFT on the camera grid, and the seeing FWHM
\[\mathrm{FWHM} \approx 0.976\,\frac{\lambda}{r_0}\sqrt{1-2.183\,(r_0/L_0)^{0.356}},\]

valid for \(r_0\ll L_0\). - Tolerance: atmosphere_t2.seeing: formula_accuracy 0.03 (Tokovinin vs finite-aperture reference; measured 1.3 to 2.4 %, deterministic) and rel 0.084 (SAOS vs reference; \(3.5\times\) worst sd 0.024 at \(r_0\) = 0.25). FWHM SAOS/Tokovinin is only recorded. - References: Tokovinin 2002 (PASP 114:1156); Roddier 1981.

docs.title: test_corrsh.py — Correlating Shack-Hartmann (solar, extended scene)
docs.text:
Source: tests/test_corrsh.py

Covers SAOS.CorrelatingShackHartmann with SAOS.ExtendedSource in three layers: spot optics (get_psf), image formation (compute_images) and the end-to-end correlation measurement (wfs_measure, initialize_wfs). Configuration: \(6\times6\) subapertures of \(d=0.1\) m over a 48 px pupil, V band (500 nm), plate scale 0.4"/px (\(\lambda/d=2.58\) px), 10" field, ExtendedSource with \(3\times3\) sub-directions (sun patches of 58 px per subaperture), use_brightest=5 unless stated. Independent references written in the test file (no SAOS code): (i) the far field of a subaperture as a direct Fourier sum of the continuous amplitude (ref_spot), sampled at angle \((k-n_{sun}//2)\,\mathrm{plate\_scale}\), the contract of get_psf (PSF centred at pixel \(n_{sun}//2\), unit energy in the window); (ii) a direct circular convolution of an object built in the test; (iii) the true image shift \(\theta/\mathrm{plate\_scale}\) of a global tilt, plus an independent least-squares image registration (register_shift). A global tilt of \(\theta\) arcsec moves the image by \(\theta/\mathrm{plate\_scale}\) px, so a phase gradient of \(K_G=2\pi p\,\mathrm{ps}/\lambda\) rad/px moves it by one pixel. All tests are marked fast. Tolerances come from tolerances/corrsh.yaml (calibrated 2026-10-27, CPU float32; policy: numerical precision of the reference or estimator statistics, never absorbing a measured SAOS discrepancy).

Image formation model used by the convolution tests: the subaperture image is the object convolved with the subaperture PSF (circular convolution on the patch),

\[ I_k(\mathbf r)=\sum_{\mathbf a}\mathrm{PSF}_k(\mathbf a)\,O(\mathbf r-\mathbf a). \]

docs.title: test_spot_tilt_displacement
docs.text:
• Module: CorrelatingShackHartmann.get_psf.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: for global tilts of 0.05, 0.3, 1 and 2 px, both signs and both axes, each subaperture spot moves by exactly the tilt along its axis and not along the other. Compared against ref_spot: centroid on the direct and cross axis, spread of the centroid across subapertures, the whole spot image, and the sinc\(^2\) fit of the cut through the peak against the true shift (independent of window truncation).
  • Theory / assumptions: square aperture far field \(\mathrm{sinc}^2\); a linear phase \(2\pi(\theta/(\lambda/d))\,\xi\) displaces the spot by \(\theta\). Centroid relative to pixel \(n_{sun}//2\); window truncation belongs to the reference. Fitted shape \(A\,\mathrm{sinc}^2((k-k_0)/\mathrm{samp})\).
  • Tolerance: tilt keys: cog_atol = 0.002 px (measured 4.3e-4), image_atol = 0.002 of the reference peak (measured 3.6e-4), peak_atol = \(10^{-3}\) px (measured 3e-6).
  • References: Goodman, "Introduction to Fourier Optics".

docs.title: test_flat_spot_centred
docs.text:
• Module: CorrelatingShackHartmann.get_psf.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: with flat phase every spot peaks at pixel \(n_{sun}//2\), is mirror symmetric (\(I[k]=I[n-k]\)), has the same centroid as the reference window (which is slightly non-zero because the window extent \(-n//2\ldots n-n//2-1\) is asymmetric), and has unit energy in the window.
  • Theory / assumptions: the far field of a square aperture is real and even.
  • Tolerance: centring: mirror_atol = \(10^{-5}\) of the peak (measured 2e-10), cog_atol = \(5\times10^{-4}\) px (measured 9e-5), energy_atol = \(10^{-5}\).
  • References: none specific.

docs.title: test_spot_second_moment
docs.text:
• Module: CorrelatingShackHartmann.get_psf.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: parametrised over phase = flat, defocus. The second central moment \(M_2\) (x and y) of the spot on the \(n_{sun}\) window, a quantity that sets correlation width and centroid noise, equals that of the continuous-aperture Fourier sum on the same window. Defocus case: \(\phi=c(x^2+y^2)\), \(c=0.01\) rad/px\(^2\), evaluated per subaperture at its own centre; flat case checks one subaperture (identical).
  • Theory / assumptions: \(M_2=\sum (k-\bar k)^2 I_k/\sum I_k\). The pupil sampling of get_psf has a design bias of about \(1.22(u/n)^2\) with \(u\) the patch half-width in \(\lambda/d\) and \(n\) the pupil samples per subaperture (about 0.94 % here).
  • Tolerance: m2.rel_atol = 0.01 on \(M_2/M_{2,ref}-1\) (measured +0.77 % flat, +0.66 % defocus).
  • References: none specific.

docs.title: test_partial_subaperture_energy_and_shape
docs.text:
• Module: CorrelatingShackHartmann validity map and get_psf for partially lit subapertures.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: circular pupil with 20 % obstruction (48 px binary mask), flat phase: (1) valid iff at least 50 % of pixels lie in the pupil; (2) window energy equals the transmitted fraction (mean of the mask block), and invalid subapertures have zero energy; (3) the spot shape equals the far field of the binary mask block (amplitude 1 on its pixels), normalised to unit sum, for all partially lit valid subapertures.
  • Theory / assumptions: same aperture contract as in test_wfs.py: the binary mask is a piecewise-constant amplitude; energy proportional to illuminated area.
  • Tolerance: partial.energy_atol = \(10^{-5}\) (measured 1.3e-7), partial.shape_atol = \(10^{-4}\) of peak (measured 2e-6; mask cells align exactly with pupil samples, 16 per pixel).
  • References: none specific.

docs.title: test_defocus_mirror_antisymmetry
docs.text:
• Module: CorrelatingShackHartmann.get_psf.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: defocus \(\phi=c(x^2+y^2)\), \(c=0.013\) rad/px\(^2\) (spot motion up to about 2 px): the x displacement of subaperture \((i,j)\) is minus that of its mirror \((i,N-1-j)\) and independent of the row (and likewise for y across rows); displacements also equal the per-subaperture reference. The reference uses the piecewise-linear continuation of the pixel map of the quadratic (the input is a pixel map), and the antisymmetry bound includes the reference's own residual caused by the asymmetric window extent.
  • Theory / assumptions: mean gradient over subaperture \(j\) is \(2c\,x_j\), odd about the pupil centre; window extent asymmetry gives a small reference residual (0.0097 px per the yaml).
  • Tolerance: defocus.asym_atol = \(10^{-3}\) px added to the reference's own antisymmetry residual; defocus.cog_atol = \(10^{-3}\) px against the pixel-sampled reference (measured 3.8e-4).
  • References: none specific.

docs.title: test_convolution_delta_not_shifted
docs.text:
• Module: CorrelatingShackHartmann.compute_images.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: parametrised over margin = 8.0 (npix_sun_even) and 8.4 (npix_sun_odd). The image of a one-pixel object is the PSF placed at that pixel: a delta at the PSF origin \(n_{sun}//2\) returns the PSF unshifted for even and odd \(n_{sun}\), and a delta at offsets (0,0), (-9,6), (13,-4) returns the PSF circularly shifted by that offset. Compared as whole images and as centroids, with the PSF carrying a tilt of (0.7, -0.4) px.
  • Theory / assumptions: convolution with a delta is a shift; circular (FFT) convolution.
  • Tolerance: conv.image_atol = \(10^{-5}\) of the peak (measured 1.5e-7 to 2.7e-8), conv.cog_atol = \(10^{-4}\) px (measured 4e-6).
  • References: none specific.

docs.title: test_convolution_matches_direct_and_conserves_flux
docs.text:
• Module: CorrelatingShackHartmann.compute_images.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: a random smooth positive object per sub-direction (58 px) convolved with spots of the obstructed pupil under flat and tilted phases: (1) selected images equal the direct circular convolution of the object with the PSF (shape at unit sum); (2) the image flux equals the object flux times the transmitted energy of the subaperture, with the same constant for all subapertures and sub-directions.
  • Theory / assumptions: a unit-sum PSF conserves flux; direct convolution by summing rolled copies, \(\mathrm{out}=\sum_{ab}\mathrm{PSF}[a,b]\,\mathrm{roll}(O,(a-n//2,b-n//2))\).
  • Tolerance: conv.image_atol = \(10^{-5}\); conv.flux_atol = \(10^{-5}\) on std/mean of the flux ratio (measured 1e-7).
  • References: none specific.

docs.title: test_global_tilt_linearity_and_cross_coupling
docs.text:
• Module: CorrelatingShackHartmann.wfs_measure (correlation estimator with pseudo-reference, use_brightest = 9).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: a fixed high-order residual phase (0.3 rad rms) makes the subaperture images differ so the pseudo-reference (subaperture pseudoref_index) is a genuinely different image; that subaperture is excluded. A global tilt scans 41 shifts over \([-R,R]\), \(R=4"/0.4=10\) px (80 % of the half window), along x and then y. Linearity: RMS of the mean slopes about a fitted line \(gs+b\), relative to \(R\). Cross coupling: maximum over shifts of the RMS over subapertures of the other-axis slopes, relative to \(R\). The gain, offset and worst-subaperture errors are recorded as information. An independent least-squares registration of the images (shifts up to 3 px) is also recorded to separate image from estimator errors.
  • Theory / assumptions: ideal response is the unit-gain line \(s=\text{shift}\); the gain is absorbed by the interaction matrix so only departure from a line is penalised. Correlation-peak estimator (Michau, Rousset & Fontanella 1993; Löfdahl 2010) on extended scenes.
  • Tolerance: linearity.lin_frac = 0.02 and linearity.cross_frac = 0.03 of full scale, the specified linearity and cross-coupling bounds (cross coupling is only exceeded at the window-edge point of 4.25").
  • References: Michau, Rousset & Fontanella 1993; Löfdahl 2010, A&A 524:A90.

docs.title: test_reference_averaged
docs.text:
• Module: CorrelatingShackHartmann.initialize_wfs (pseudo-reference and reference slopes with noiseFlag=True).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: the pseudo-reference is the average of n_reference_frames images and the reference slopes the average of \(n\) further correlated frames. With \(\sigma_1\) the single-frame slope noise (30 frames), \(\sqrt n\,\mathrm{rms}(\text{ref}_{noisy}-\text{ref}_{clean})/\sigma_1\) lies in \([1,\sqrt2]\) widened by the statistics band, excluding the pseudo-reference subaperture. Uses photon noise only.
  • Theory / assumptions: the reference retains the noise of the \(n\) averaged frames, variance \(\sigma_1^2/n\), plus the effect of the residual noise of the averaged pseudo-reference, between 0 and \(\sigma_1^2/n\) (linear propagation, symmetric in the two images).
  • Tolerance: reference.n_sigma = 3.5: band widened by \(3.5/\sqrt{2M}\), \(M\) the number of slopes (\(n\) = 100).
  • References: none specific.

docs.title: test_tilt_axes_isotropy_and_sign
docs.text:
• Module: CorrelatingShackHartmann.wfs_measure, compared with ShackHartmann.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: (1) sign convention: a tilt towards +x (+y) gives positive x (y) slopes, with the sign agreeing with ShackHartmann for the same phase, plate scale and telescope; (2) isotropy: with the sun patches and sub-directions transposed (rows and columns exchanged), the y response equals the original x response, and the cross responses match (0.5 px shift).
  • Theory / assumptions: convention and symmetry only.
  • Tolerance: isotropy.atol = \(2\times10^{-4}\) px (same code path for rows and columns; measured 4e-5); signs exact.
  • References: none specific.

docs.title: test_unit_in_rad_constructs
docs.text:
• Module: CorrelatingShackHartmann.__init__ (unit_in_rad, slopes_units).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: unit_in_rad=True constructs and gives a finite positive px/rad conversion slopes_units.
  • Theory / assumptions: none (construction/convention).
  • Tolerance: boolean check.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_unit_in_rad_reference_slopes
docs.text:
• Module: CorrelatingShackHartmann.initialize_wfs, wfs_measure with unit_in_rad=True.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: the reference slopes are in rad like the measurements: a null phase gives zero slopes (below \(10^{-9}\) rad), and a 0.5 px tilt gives slope\(_{rad}\times\)slopes_units equal to the slope in px of the unit_in_rad=False sensor.
  • Theory / assumptions: unit conversion only.
  • Tolerance: null slope \(\le10^{-9}\), ratio 1 with rtol = \(10^{-6}\) (hard-coded).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_photons_scale_with_fov_squared
docs.text:
• Module: CorrelatingShackHartmann.wfs_measure (photon budget).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: with an exact-count detector (no shot noise, QE 1, no readout or dark noise, 1 e-/DN) the frame electrons equal flux \(\times D^2\times t\times(\mathrm{FoV}/\mathrm{src.fov})^2\) for FoV 6" and 10", and the ratio of the two frames is 0.36.
  • Theory / assumptions: photons collected scale with sky area observed and with the pupil area and integration time (1 ms); lightRatio = 1.
  • Tolerance: photons.rtol = \(10^{-3}\) (per-pixel rounding of the photon frame, about \(4\times10^{11}\) photons).
  • References: none specific.

docs.title: test_data.py — data directory and download of the solar images (T1)
docs.text:
Source: tests/test_data.py

Covers SAOS.data. The download is exercised against a local file:// record holding one random file, with a registry entry built from its size and MD5, so no network is used. Whole module fast.

docs.title: test_data_dir_from_environment
docs.text:
• Module: SAOS.data.data_dir.
  • What it checks: the data directory is $SAOS_DATA_DIR when set (and is created), and $XDG_CACHE_HOME/SAOS otherwise.
  • Tolerance: exact.

docs.title: test_registry_matches_the_zenodo_record
docs.text:
• Module: SAOS.data.REGISTRY.
  • What it checks: the registry lists cont_500nm.h5 and cont_680nm.h5, each with a 32-digit hexadecimal MD5.
  • Tolerance: exact.

docs.title: test_download_verifies_and_reuses
docs.text:
• Module: SAOS.data.get_data_file.
  • What it checks: a missing file is downloaded into the data directory with the bytes of the record and no partial file left; a second call returns the same path without downloading.
  • Tolerance: exact (byte equality).

docs.title: test_checksum_mismatch_raises_and_leaves_nothing
docs.text:
• Module: SAOS.data.get_data_file.
  • What it checks: a download whose MD5 differs from the registry raises IOError and leaves the data directory empty; an unknown file name raises KeyError.
  • Tolerance: exact.

docs.title: test_truncated_file_is_downloaded_again
docs.text:
• Module: SAOS.data.get_data_file.
  • What it checks: a file whose size differs from the registry is replaced by the record.
  • Tolerance: exact (byte equality).

docs.title: test_detector.py — Detector noise statistics, quantisation, saturation, reproducibility (T1)
docs.text:
Source: tests/test_detector.py

Covers SAOS.Detector (integrate(frame, photons, stream), register_stream): the frame is normalised to unit sum and scaled to photons, converted to electrons with quantum efficiency (Poisson\((\mathrm{QE}\,N)\) for shot noise), plus Poisson dark current and Gaussian readout noise, clipped to the full well and quantised to DN. Statistics are checked on uniform frames where each pixel is an independent sample (4 frames x 128 x 128 px = 65536 pixels), using sample mean and variance against the closed-form moments of the Poisson and Gaussian laws (Janesick 2001 for the detector model). One tolerance policy applies to the whole file: \(3.5\sigma\) of the estimator, with \(\sigma\) measured over 30 seeds (tests/tolerances/detector.yaml); no tolerance absorbs a measured SAOS discrepancy. Whole module fast.

docs.title: test_shot_noise_statistics
docs.text:
• Module: Detector.integrate (QE and shot noise).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: on a uniform frame of \(N\) = 400 photons/px with QE = 0.6 (1 e-/DN, no other noise) the mean and the variance of the counts both equal \(\mathrm{QE}\,N = 240\) e-.
  • Theory / assumptions: Poisson statistics, \(\mathrm{E}[n]=\mathrm{Var}[n]=\mathrm{QE}\,N\); independent pixels; large enough count that rounding to DN is negligible.
  • Tolerance: detector.shot_noise: mean_rtol \(7.3\times10^{-4}\) (measured \(\sigma\) of mean/(QE N) = \(2.1\times10^{-4}\); theory \(1/\sqrt{\mathrm{QE}N n_{px}}\)), var_rtol 0.020 (\(\sigma\) = \(5.6\times10^{-3}\); theory \(\sqrt{2/n_{px}}\) for a near-Gaussian variance estimate). Applied as absolute tolerance on the ratio to 1.
  • References: Janesick 2001 (Scientific CCDs, SPIE Press).

docs.title: test_dark_current_statistics
docs.text:
• Module: Detector.integrate (dark current).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: no signal, dark current 2000 e-/s/px over 10 ms: mean and variance both 20 e-.
  • Theory / assumptions: Poisson\((\mathrm{dark}\cdot t_{int})\).
  • Tolerance: detector.dark_current: mean_rtol \(2.9\times10^{-3}\) (\(\sigma = 8.4\times10^{-4}\), theory \(1/\sqrt{20\,n_{px}}\)), var_rtol 0.017 (\(\sigma = 4.8\times10^{-3}\)).
  • References: Janesick 2001.

docs.title: test_readout_noise_on_signal
docs.text:
• Module: Detector.integrate (readout noise and quantisation).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: on a bright uniform frame (1000 photons/px, so no clipping at 0) with \(\sigma_{RON}\) = 5 e- and \(q\) = 1 e-/DN, the variance is \(\sigma_{RON}^2 + q^2/12 = 25+1/12\).
  • Theory / assumptions: Gaussian read noise adds in variance; quantisation of a dithered signal adds the uniform-error variance \(q^2/12\) (Sheppard's correction). Shot noise is off, so the signal is deterministic.
  • Tolerance: detector.readout_noise.var_rtol = 0.0175 (\(\sigma = 5.0\times10^{-3}\); theory \(\sqrt{2/n_{px}}\)).
  • References: Janesick 2001.

docs.title: test_readout_noise_dark_frame
docs.text:
• Module: Detector.integrate (readout noise, clipping at 0).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: with no signal, \(\sigma_{RON}\) = 5 e- and quantisation 0.01 e-/DN (fine, so that quantisation is negligible), the frame follows a zero-mean Gaussian clipped at 0: mean \(\sigma/\sqrt{2\pi}\) and variance \(\sigma^2(1/2-1/(2\pi))\). Records the SAOS convention: no bias pedestal and unsigned output, so negative excursions are clipped.
  • Theory / assumptions: for \(x=\max(0,\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2))\):
\[\mathrm{E}[x] = \frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{2\pi}},\qquad \mathrm{Var}[x] = \sigma^2\left(\frac12-\frac1{2\pi}\right).\]
  • Tolerance: detector.readout_noise: dark_mean_atol 0.020 on mean\(/(\sigma/\sqrt{2\pi})-1\) (sd \(=\sqrt{(1/2-1/2\pi)/n_{px}}/0.399 = 5.7\times10^{-3}\), times 3.5) and var_rtol 0.0175 on the variance ratio.
  • References: Janesick 2001 (for read noise); clipped-Gaussian moments are standard.

docs.title: test_quantisation_unbiased
docs.text:
• Module: Detector.integrate (ADC quantisation).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: 1000 e- per pixel with \(q\) = 10 e-/DN and readout noise of 10 e- (which dithers the ADC): the mean output is 100 DN, i.e. rounding is unbiased; truncation would give 99.5 DN.
  • Theory / assumptions: rounding of a dithered signal has zero mean error; truncation has a mean error of \(-1/2\) DN.
  • Tolerance: detector.quantisation.bias_atol_dn = 0.0146 DN (\(\sigma(\mathrm{mean}) = 4.2\times10^{-3}\) DN; theory \(\sqrt{1+1/12}/\sqrt{n_{px}}\)).
  • References: Janesick 2001.

docs.title: test_dark_calibration_no_wrap
docs.text:
• Module: Detector dark calibration (darkCalibration = 20 frames) and its output dtype.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: with readout noise 10 e-, 12 bits, 1 e-/DN, full well 60000 and no signal, the calibrated output stays within \([0, 2^{12}-1]\): negative residuals are clipped at 0 (SAOS convention) and not wrapped to values near 65535 by an unsigned cast. The mean DN is recorded.
  • Tolerance: hard bounds \(0\le \mathrm{DN}\le 4095\). The yaml key dark_calibration.mean_atol_dn (0.20 DN) exists but this test does not use it.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_full_well_saturation
docs.text:
• Module: Detector.integrate (full-well clipping).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: 5000 e- per pixel on a 3000 e- full well reads exactly \(\mathrm{FWC}/q\) = 3000 DN everywhere (\(q\) = 1).
  • Tolerance: exact (absolute 0).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_infinite_full_well_scale
docs.text:
• Module: Detector.integrate with infinite full well and automatic quantisation (\(q\) = 0, 16 bits).
  • Tier: fast. Parametrised over fwc = np.inf and float('inf').
  • What it checks: the output keeps the absolute signal scale: a frame with twice the photons gives twice the mean counts (ratio 2) and not zero.
  • Tolerance: relative \(10^{-3}\) on the ratio (hard-coded).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_seeded_reproducibility
docs.text:
• Module: Detector random generator (randomState).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: with QE 0.7, shot noise, readout noise 3 e- and dark current 1000 e-/s, two detectors with the same seed give bit-identical frames; a different seed gives frames that differ (fraction of equal pixels at most 0.5).
  • Tolerance: exact for the same seed; fraction of equal pixels \(\le 0.5\) otherwise (hard-coded).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_noise_flag_off_is_identity
docs.text:
• Module: Detector.integrate with noiseFlag=False.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: the input frame is returned unchanged for a random 128x128 input, even with shot noise and readout noise configured.
  • Tolerance: exact.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_noise_streams_independent_and_reproducible
docs.text:
• Module: Detector.register_stream, Detector.integrate(frame, photons, stream).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: streams are numbered 0, 1, ... in connection order; the same stream of an identical detector (same seed) reproduces its noise exactly regardless of the order in which streams are drawn; and two streams give uncorrelated noise (correlation of the noise of a flat 64x64 frame).
  • Theory / assumptions: the correlation coefficient of two independent noise fields of \(n\) pixels has standard deviation \(1/\sqrt n\).
  • Tolerance: correlation within \(4/\sqrt{n_{px}}\) (hard-coded, 4 sigma); other criteria exact.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_dm.py — DeformableMirror: influence functions, fitting, altitude footprints, geometry, dynamics, misregistration (T1)
docs.text:
Source: tests/test_dm.py

Covers SAOS.DeformableMirror (updateDMShape, get_dm_opd, buildLayer, applyDynamics, set_actuator_misregistration, print_properties), with SAOS.LightPath and SAOS.MisRegistration where noted. The reference is an independent re-implementation of the documented actuator model (function model_opd), which never touches dm.coordinates, dm.high_res_coords, dm.influence_functions or SAOS-generated OPD: an \(n\times n\) actuator grid spanning the metapupil \(D_{fov}\) with pitch \(p=D_{fov}/(n-1)\), valid actuators \(r\le D_{fov}/2+\mathrm{thresh}\cdot p\), Gaussian influence functions and a partition of unity,

\[g_k(\mathbf x)=\exp\!\big(\ln c\;|\mathbf x-\mathbf x_k|^2/p^2\big),\qquad W(\mathbf x)=\frac{\sum_k a_k\,g_k(\mathbf x)}{\sum_k g_k(\mathbf x)},\]

with \(c\) the mechanical coupling (0.6 by default; \(g=c\) at one pitch), sampled on the pupil pixel grid \((i-(N-1)/2)\,D/N\) (\(N\) = 64, \(D\) = 4 m, 11x11 actuators). Conventions verified: the DM is transmissive (OPD = IF \(\times\) command, no factor 2) and adds to the atmospheric OPD; source azimuth 0 deg moves the altitude footprint along +x (columns), 90 deg along +y (rows). Tests that compare SAOS with its own alternative code path are named test_regression_* and are not physics checks. All tests are deterministic with numerical tolerances (tests/tolerances/dm.yaml, measured 2026-10-26). Whole module fast.

docs.title: test_piston_gives_flat_opd
docs.text:
• Module: DeformableMirror.updateDMShape (influence functions).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: an equal command \(a=1\,\mu\)m on every valid actuator gives OPD \(=a\) across the pupil: peak-to-valley over \(a\) is zero and the mean over \(a\) is 1.
  • Theory / assumptions: partition of unity, \(\sum_k a\,g_k/\sum_k g_k = a\).
  • Tolerance: dm.linearity.rel = \(10^{-10}\) (float64 linear algebra; measured \(\le10^{-13}\)).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_poke_matches_independent_actuator_model
docs.text:
• Module: DeformableMirror.updateDMShape.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: the OPD of a random command (rms 0.1 um) over the whole pupil grid equals the independent Gaussian/partition-of-unity model, as \(\max|\mathrm{OPD}-\mathrm{model}|/\max|\mathrm{model}|\) (absolute amplitude in metres).
  • Tolerance: dm.model.rel = \(10^{-10}\) (SAOS adds \(10^{-12}\) to the normalisation).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_single_actuator_surface_central_and_edge
docs.text:
• Module: DeformableMirror.updateDMShape on a 61 px pupil (odd, so that the central actuator falls on a sample).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: for pokes of a central actuator, an edge actuator on the +x border and an inner-ring actuator, SAOS equals the model on every sample; for the central actuator the value at the actuator is the infinite-lattice peak, and the model values at one and two pitches (axis) and the diagonal neighbour are \(c^{1},c^{4},c^{2}\) times that value; for the edge actuator the model value at the actuator is \(1/\sum_k c^{(d_k/p)^2}\).
  • Theory / assumptions: for an interior actuator of an infinite lattice poked with a unit command, the surface value at the actuator is
\[\frac{1}{\left(\sum_{i}c^{\,i^2}\right)^2}\approx0.1626\ \ (c=0.6),\]

and the value at the \(n\)-th neighbour on an axis is \(c^{n^2}\) times it (mechanical coupling = neighbour/actuator ratio). The pupil grid does not sample the other actuators, so only the central one is read from SAOS; the others come from the model, which SAOS equals on every sample. - Tolerance: dm.model.rel \(10^{-10}\) for the model comparisons; relative \(10^{-3}\) for the lattice-peak and neighbour ratios; relative \(10^{-9}\) for the edge value (all hard-coded except the first). - References: none.

docs.title: test_regression_poke_superposition_and_scaling
docs.text:
• Module: DeformableMirror.updateDMShape, influence_functions.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: internal consistency (not a physics check): OPD\((c_1+c_2)\) = OPD\((c_1)\) + OPD\((c_2)\); OPD\((3c)\) = 3 OPD\((c)\); a full \(n_{act}^2\) command equals the same command restricted to the valid actuators; a single poke equals the stored influence-function column times the command.
  • Tolerance: dm.linearity.rel = \(10^{-10}\).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_dm_opd_enters_lightpath_with_positive_sign
docs.text:
• Module: LightPath.propagate (wfs_opd) with a DM and a stand-in atmosphere.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: the WFS-path OPD is \((\mathrm{OPD}_{atm}+W)\,P\), with \(W\) the independent actuator model and \(P\) the pupil, i.e. the DM adds with a positive sign and no factor 2 for reflection (transmissive convention).
  • Tolerance: dm.model.rel = \(10^{-10}\) on the maximum relative difference.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_tilt_and_defocus_fitting
docs.text:
• Module: DeformableMirror.updateDMShape.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: with commands sampled on the actuators for a tilt (\(c=a\,x_{act}\)) and defocus (\(c=a\,r_{act}^2\)): (1) SAOS equals the independent actuator model over the whole pupil (maximum difference over the rms of the model); (2) the relative rms residual with respect to the target \(a x\) or \(a r^2\) (piston removed; residual and signal over the same region), computed in the inner region \(r<0.7R\) and the edge annulus \(0.7R\le r\le R\), equals the model's own value to numerical precision. The fit quality itself is a property of the finite Gaussian actuator model (reported as a metric; edge-annulus error 6.5 % for tilt); SAOS must reproduce it.
  • Tolerance: dm.model.rel \(10^{-10}\) for the first criterion; dm.fitting.ratio_atol = \(10^{-8}\) on SAOS minus model residual ratio (mechanical coupling 0.6, 11x11 actuators over 4 m).
  • References: Hardy 1998 (DM fitting, generic).

docs.title: test_altitude_dm_footprint_physical_displacement
docs.text:
• Module: DeformableMirror.get_dm_opd for an altitude DM (15x15 actuators at 10 km, 60 arcsec field, metapupil \(D_{fov}=D+2h\tan(\mathrm{fov}/2)\)).
  • Tier: fast. Parametrised over (azimuth deg, displacement in grid steps) = (0, 0.7), (0, 1.6), (90, 2.3), (180, 1.3), (270, 0.8).
  • What it checks: a source at field angle \(\theta\) and azimuth \(az\) sees the DM through the pupil displaced by \(\delta=h\tan\theta\,(\cos az,\sin az)\). For the ramp command \(c=g(x_{act}+0.7\,y_{act})\) the change of the OPD relative to the on-axis one equals \(W(\mathbf x_p+\boldsymbol\delta_r)-W(\mathbf x_p)\) from the independent model, where \(\boldsymbol\delta_r\) is \(\delta\) rounded to the nearest grid step \(D/N\) (integer-pixel model, the same as the atmosphere footprint). Fractional displacements 0.7 to 2.3 steps are chosen away from 0.5 so rounding is unambiguous. Criterion: relative \(L_2\) error of the change over the pupil.
  • Theory / assumptions: small field, line of sight at altitude \(h\) displaced by \(h\tan\theta\); azimuth 0 along +columns, 90 along +rows.
  • Tolerance: dm.footprint.rel = 0.01 (relative \(L_2\) error against the rounded model; an ideal fractional-shift implementation would give \(7\times10^{-4}\)).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_altitude_dm_metapupil_diameter
docs.text:
• Module: DeformableMirror.buildLayer (called on a stand-in object, no influence functions built).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: \(D_{fov}=D+2h\tan(\mathrm{fov}/2)\) for the EST telescope (4.149 m, 60 arcsec, \(h\) = 20 km).
  • Tolerance: dm.geometry.metapupil_rel = \(10^{-6}\) (relative, on \(D_{fov}/\mathrm{expected}-1\)).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_altitude_dm_grid_step_matches_ground
docs.text:
• Module: DeformableMirror.buildLayer (pixel_size, D_px, D_fov).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: for EST at \(h\) = 0, 5 and 20 km the DM grid step equals the pupil pixel \(D/N\); the grid covers the metapupil with a symmetric whole-pixel margin, \(0\le D_{px}\,p-D_{fov}<2p\); and \(D_{px}-N\) is even.
  • Tolerance: dm.geometry.grid_step_rel = \(10^{-3}\) for the step; margin in \([-10^{-9},2-10^{-9}]\) pixels; parity exact.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_misregistration_pixel_size_matches_dm_grid
docs.text:
• Module: DeformableMirror.misReg (MisRegistration.spatialSampling), high_res_coords.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: the metre-to-pixel conversion used by MisRegistration equals the DM grid step measured on high_res_coords.
  • Tolerance: dm.geometry.grid_step_rel = \(10^{-3}\) (relative).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_dynamics_matches_dlsim
docs.text:
• Module: DeformableMirror.applyDynamics, updateDMShape with dynamicModel (HDF5 state-space).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: a 7x7 DM with a second-order model (800 Hz, damping 0.3, zero-order hold at the loop rate \(T_s=0.5\) ms) responds to a 60-step command sequence (a step then random) exactly as scipy.signal.dlsim, actuator by actuator; and the OPD after the sequence is the independent actuator model applied to the dlsim output.
  • Theory / assumptions: discrete model from ZOH discretisation of
\[\dot{\mathbf x}=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-\omega^2&-2\zeta\omega\end{pmatrix}\mathbf x+\begin{pmatrix}0\\\omega^2\end{pmatrix}u,\quad y=(1\ 0)\,\mathbf x,\quad \omega=2\pi\cdot800\ \mathrm{Hz},\ \zeta=0.3,\]

with unit DC gain. - Tolerance: dm.dynamics.rel = \(10^{-12}\) (torch float64 vs scipy) for the dynamic output; dm.model.rel \(10^{-10}\) for the OPD. - References: none (standard discrete-time state-space simulation).

docs.title: test_actuator_misregistration_matches_independent_model
docs.text:
• Module: DeformableMirror.set_actuator_misregistration(shift_x, shift_y, rotation, magnification).
  • Tier: fast. Parametrised over shift 0.3 pitch (0.12, -0.08 m, no rotation), magnification 0.95, rotation 7 deg, combined (0.03, -0.02 m, 7 deg, 1.02).
  • What it checks: the DM shape equals the independent model with actuators moved to \(\mathbf x'=s\,R\,\mathbf x+\mathbf d\) (\(R\) a clockwise rotation for a positive angle, x right / y up; Gaussian width scaled by \(s\), so that \(g=c\) at one scaled pitch; partition of unity over the moved actuators), as documented; resetting to \((0,0,0,1)\) restores the original shape. Errors are relative to the rms of the unmisregistered surface.
  • Tolerance: dm.misregistration.exact = \(10^{-10}\).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_actuator_misregistration_moves_a_poke_as_specified
docs.text:
• Module: DeformableMirror.set_actuator_misregistration.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: the sense of each parameter on a single poked actuator at (+2 pitch, 0): a shift \((0.2p,-0.1p)\) moves the surface centroid by that vector, a +90 deg rotation (clockwise) takes it to \((0,-2p)\), a -90 deg rotation to \((0,+2p)\), and a magnification 1.1 to \((2.2p,0)\). Centroid is that of the region above half the maximum.
  • Tolerance: dm.misregistration.centroid_m = 8 mm (2 % of the pitch; bias of the half-maximum-region centroid estimator, up to 6.4 mm on the independent model).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_regression_actuator_vs_map_misregistration_convention
docs.text:
• Module: DeformableMirror.set_actuator_misregistration vs MisRegistration.apply_misreg.
  • Tier: fast. Parametrised over shift +1 px x, shift +2 px y, rotation +90 deg, rotation -90 deg (shifts in DM grid pixels).
  • What it checks: equal-path consistency (not a physics check; the physical sense is covered by the previous test): the actuator-level misregistration has the same sense as the OPD-map misregistration where the map interpolation is exact (integer-pixel shifts and \(\pm90\) deg), interior difference below tolerance (relative to the rms); the opposite transformation differs by more than ten times that difference.
  • Tolerance: dm.misregistration.convention = \(10^{-9}\) of the rms; opposite-sense ratio at least 10 (hard-coded).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_print_properties_runs
docs.text:
• Module: DeformableMirror.print_properties.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: logging runs without error and a record containing "Controlled Actuators" is emitted. Smoke test, no physics.
  • Tolerance: assertion on the presence of the message.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_extended_source.py — Extended (solar) source with ScienceCam and Atmosphere
docs.text:
Source: tests/test_extended_source.py

Covers SAOS.ExtendedSource (sub-direction patches, blending filters, flux), as used through LightPath with ScienceCam and Atmosphere. The scenario reproduces an asterism workflow: an h5 image of delta-function "stars" at 0.0128"/px (image[x_px, y_px]: first axis = image row) observed by an EST-like telescope (D 4.149 m, obstruction 1.3 m, 450 px resolution, \(3\times3\) sub-directions, FoV 9.975", padding 5", margin 4"), with a ScienceCam at 0.0128"/px. Besides the 17 stars of the asterism, a marker star at \((x,y)=(+3.0",-1.2")\) breaks the D4 symmetry so transposition or mirroring is detected. The same 18 directions are also observed as point sources (NGS) for reference. Every expectation is computed independently of SAOS: own geometry, own FFT of an analytic annular pupil with \(4\times4\) sub-pixel occupancy and bilinear phase (RefPSF, \(N=1024\), pixel scale exactly \(\lambda/(\mathrm{ps}\,N\,dx)\)), own sampling of the atmosphere screen (cubic sub-pixel windows), own convolution. The telescope resolution (450 px, about 2 per camera pupil sample) keeps the ScienceCam resampling error below 0.2 % of the PSF peak. Metrics are windows of 79 px (1.0" half-width) normalised to unit sum, compared as \(\max|{\rm window}-{\rm ref}|/\max({\rm ref})\). Frames are [row, col], with row = sky y in the SAOS atmosphere/DM frame (an NGS observing the star written at image[x_px, y_px] is placed at azimuth \(90^\circ-\varphi\)). All tests are marked nightly (module-level); fixtures are module-scoped and use the GPU when available. Tolerances: tolerances/extended_source.yaml (calibrated 2026-10-26 on develop, GPU, 8 seeds where stated, typically mean + 3.5 sd).

Mosaic model used in the altitude-layer tests: the extended object is split into \(n\times n\) patches of size \(s=2(\mathrm{fov}+\mathrm{pad})/(n+1)\) with centres every \(s/2\) (50 % overlap) and blended with tent weights that sum to one everywhere,

\[ I(\mathbf r)=\sum_{i,j} w_i(x)\,w_j(y)\,\big[O * \mathrm{PSF}_{ij}\big](\mathbf r), \]

where \(\mathrm{PSF}_{ij}\) is the PSF of the line of sight to the centre of patch \((i,j)\), which crosses a layer at altitude \(h\) displaced by \(h\tan\theta\) (rounded to the layer pixel, the integer-pixel model).

docs.title: test_b1_no_atmosphere_stars
docs.text:
• Module: ExtendedSource + ScienceCam through LightPath.propagate.
  • Tier: nightly.
  • What it checks: with no atmosphere, each of the 18 stars appears at its input pixel (position error within 0.1 px, found by Fourier upsampling and a parabola), has the FWHM of the obstructed-pupil PSF, and its 79 px window matches the independent PSF window. NGS PSFs of the same directions are recorded for comparison only.
  • Theory / assumptions: Fraunhofer PSF of the annulus, \(\mathrm{PSF}=|\mathcal F\{P\}|^2\), computed by zero-padded FFT with \(N\,dx=\lambda/\mathrm{ps}\).
  • Tolerance: b1: pos_atol_px = 0.1 px (measured 0.025), fwhm_rtol = 0.005 (measured -0.10 %, from the 450 to 898 px resampling), psf_atol = 0.006 of the peak (measured 0.08-0.23 %, 2.6x margin).
  • References: Goodman, "Introduction to Fourier Optics".

docs.title: test_b1_production_sampling_energy
docs.text:
• Module: ScienceCam.get_frame (extended source and point source), ScienceCam.compute_psf.
  • Tier: nightly.
  • What it checks: no atmosphere, production pupil sampling (200 px over 4.149 m, so \(\lambda/\Delta x = 4.97''\) at 500 nm lies inside the 9.975″ field; B1 uses 450 px, where it does not). The fraction of the extended-source frame outside the 18 star windows (1.0″ half-width) must not exceed \(1 - EE_{ref}\), and every point-source frame must keep \(EE_{ref}\) of its energy in the window, with \(EE_{ref}\) the encircled energy of the independent annular-pupil PSF (own FFT) in the same window.
  • Theory / assumptions: energy conservation of the image: the unit-sum windows of B1 cannot detect energy lost from the core of every star (for instance to PSF replicas). Stars near the field edge lose part of their halo out of the field, so the measured outside fraction can only be smaller than \(1 - EE_{ref}\).
  • Tolerance: extended_source.b1_production: bg_atol 0.005 (measured 0.0109 vs bound 0.0114), ee_atol 0.005 (measured 0.9869 vs 0.9886).
  • References: Goodman, Introduction to Fourier Optics.

docs.title: test_b2_image_not_transposed_or_mirrored
docs.text:
• Module: ExtendedSource / ScienceCam image orientation.
  • Tier: nightly.
  • What it checks: the number of peaks in the noise-free frame is 18, all stars are found at the input pixels (identity) and for every other element of the dihedral group (transposition, row/column mirrors, rotations by 90, 180, 270 degrees and anti-transposition) fewer than all 18 stars match (the marker breaks the symmetry).
  • Theory / assumptions: pure geometry/convention test, first image axis maps to frame rows.
  • Tolerance: match radius 0.7 px; counts exact.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_b2_subdirection_footprint_orientation
docs.text:
• Module: Atmosphere.getOPD for the extended source (sub-direction footprint on a layer).
  • Tier: nightly.
  • What it checks: one frozen layer at 15 km. The footprint offset of each of the 9 sub-directions relative to the central one is measured by cross-correlating whitened OPD maps (parabolic sub-pixel peak) and compared with \(h\tan(\theta)\) (sky x on rows) and with the transposed-axes version. For all off-diagonal sub-directions (\(a\ne b\)) none may be closer to the transposed offset than to the physical one.
  • Theory / assumptions: the line of sight at sky offset \((a,b)\) crosses the layer displaced by \((h\tan a,h\tan b)\) rows/columns; whitening removes low-order content, \(a_w=a-G_8 * a\).
  • Tolerance: orientation criterion, count of misoriented sub-directions = 0 (no numerical tolerance).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_b2_subdirection_footprint_subpixel
docs.text:
• Module: Atmosphere.getOPD for the extended source.
  • Tier: nightly.
  • What it checks: same measurement, restricted to the diagonal sub-directions (0, 4, 8) where transposition makes no difference; the measured offset must equal \(h\tan\theta\) rounded to the nearest layer pixel.
  • Theory / assumptions: integer-pixel footprint model (the layer is displaced by whole layer pixels).
  • Tolerance: b2.offset_atol_px = 0.09 px: precision of the offset estimator on exact sub-pixel windows of the same screens, 8 seeds, mean 0.0557, sd 0.0095, plus 3.5 sd.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_b3_ground_layer_isoplanatic
docs.text:
• Module: ExtendedSource + Atmosphere (single layer at 0 m, \(r_0=0.6\) m, \(L_0=25\) m).
  • Tier: nightly.
  • What it checks: with a ground layer every direction sees the same phase, so each star must have the PSF of that screen (own FFT of the annulus with the screen's phase window) and equal the NGS PSF of its direction. Both comparisons are per star on 79 px windows; independent Strehl is recorded.
  • Theory / assumptions: isoplanatic ground layer: \(\mathrm{PSF}=|\mathcal F\{P\,e^{i\phi}\}|^2\) with the same \(\phi\) for all patches, so the image of the object is the object convolved with one PSF and the blending is seamless.
  • Tolerance: b3.ref_atol = 0.012 (extended vs independent: 0.0059-0.0091 over 8 seeds, plus 3.5 sd), b3.ngs_atol = 0.008 (extended vs NGS: 0.0030-0.0065, plus 3.5 sd; resampling 898 vs 779 px).
  • References: none specific.

docs.title: test_b4_altitude_layer_orientation
docs.text:
• Module: ExtendedSource + Atmosphere (layer at 15 km).
  • Tier: nightly.
  • What it checks: the expected star window \(E\) (tent-weighted per-patch PSFs of the screen with footprint offsets rounded to the layer pixel) and \(E_t\) (transposed layer axes). Among the stars for which they differ by more than max(b4.ref_atol, b4.orientation_min_sep), none may be closer to \(E_t\) than to \(E\).
  • Theory / assumptions: mosaic model above. The 5 % separation threshold is a selection of discriminating stars, not a tolerance.
  • Tolerance: b4.orientation_min_sep = 0.05 and b4.ref_atol = 0.0011 (numerical precision of the reference vs a 2048 px FFT / \(8\times8\) sub-pixels / cubic-sampled phase, 8 seeds: mean 6.8e-4, sd 1.1e-4, plus 3.5 sd); count of misoriented stars = 0.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_b4_altitude_layer_psf_vs_screen
docs.text:
• Module: ExtendedSource + Atmosphere (layer at 15 km).
  • Tier: nightly.
  • What it checks: for every star, \(\max|\mathrm{ext}-E|/\max E\) is below the tolerance.
  • Theory / assumptions: as in the orientation test; the criterion covers the extended-image model error (patch resampling and PSF blending, 0.6-0.9 % on the ground layer in b3).
  • Tolerance: b4.psf_atol = 0.02 (measured 0.13-0.45 % on one seed).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_b4_anisoplanatic_difference_grows_with_patch_distance
docs.text:
• Module: ExtendedSource + Atmosphere, comparison with NGS PSFs.
  • Tier: nightly.
  • What it checks: the extended-object star PSF sees the phase of its patch centre(s) while the NGS sees the phase of its own direction, so their difference is zero at a patch centre and grows with the distance to the patch centres. Criteria: maximum difference at patch centres below a floor; mean off-centre difference divided by mean difference at centres above a minimum; Spearman correlation between the difference and \(\sigma^2\) above a minimum. Peak ratio ext/NGS against \(e^{-\sigma^2}\) is recorded only.
  • Theory / assumptions: anisoplanatic phase variance of a star \(\sigma^2=\sum_k w_k\,S(h\,d_k)\), with \(d_k\) the angular distance to patch centre \(k\) (converted by \(h\tan d_k\)) and \(S(r)\) the mean squared phase difference at lag \(r\) measured on the actual screen (average of row and column lags, citools.structure_function).
  • Tolerance: b4_growth: floor = 0.014 (0.0045-0.0091 plus 3.5 sd), ratio_min = 3.0 (measured 6.6-17), spearman_min = 0.70 (measured 0.757-0.840, mean 0.808, sd 0.028, minus 3.5 sd), 8 seeds.
  • References: none specific.

docs.title: test_b5_uniform_object_gives_uniform_image
docs.text:
• Module: ExtendedSource + ScienceCam mosaic blending.
  • Tier: nightly.
  • What it checks: parametrised over camera plate = 0.0128 and 0.016 arcsec/px. A constant object must give a constant image regardless of the phase in each patch, with a flat phase and with the 15 km layer: no NaN, std/mean and \(\max|f/\bar f-1|\) below a float64 floor, frame energy 1.
  • Theory / assumptions: convolution of a constant with a unit-energy PSF is the same constant; the blending filters form a partition of unity, so there are no seams.
  • Tolerance: b5_uniform.floor = \(10^{-10}\) (measured 2e-16 and 2e-15); energy rtol = \(10^{-12}\) (hard-coded).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_b5_structured_object_mosaic_has_no_seams
docs.text:
• Module: ExtendedSource + ScienceCam mosaic blending.
  • Tier: nightly.
  • What it checks: a smooth random texture (\(\pm30\) % contrast, correlation length 12 px, seed texture_seed) observed through the ground layer must equal the object convolved with the PSF of the screen (own fftconvolve with a 601 px PSF) over the whole 779 px frame; maximum and rms deviation relative to the mean.
  • Theory / assumptions: all patches have the same PSF in the ground-layer case, so the frame is a single convolution; seams or offsets would appear as steps of the order of the object contrast. The reference truncates the PSF at \(\pm300\) px and the 898 px patches wrap circularly.
  • Tolerance: b5_mosaic.max_atol = 0.005 (measured 0.0021), rms_atol = 0.0015 (measured 0.0006).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_b5_filters_partition_of_unity
docs.text:
• Module: ExtendedSource.filter_2D.
  • Tier: nightly.
  • What it checks: parametrised over n_sub = 2, 3, 4, 5. With patch \((i,j)\) placed at \((i,j)\times\mathrm{round}(W/2)\) in a mosaic of size \((n-1)\,\mathrm{round}(W/2)+W\) (50 % overlap as ScienceCam places them), the sum of the SAOS filters is 1 at every pixel.
  • Theory / assumptions: \(\sum_{ij}f_{ij}(\mathbf r)=1\).
  • Tolerance: min and max of the sum equal to 1 with rtol = \(10^{-12}\) (hard-coded).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_b5_flux
docs.text:
• Module: ExtendedSource.flux, LightPath.long_exposure_frame, ScienceCam.lightRatio.
  • Tier: nightly.
  • What it checks: (a) source flux equals the independent photon flux; sub-direction fluxes sum to it; (b) the long-exposure frame holds flux \(\times T\times A_{eff}\) photons with lightRatio=1; (c) the noise-free frame equals the independent convolution of the object with the PSF over the 779 px frame (maximum difference relative to the peak) and the flux within 1" of each star matches. The lightRatio=50 case is recorded for context.
  • Theory / assumptions: photon flux in a 10 nm band, using the ASTM G173-03 direct irradiance (via pvlib) and the solar disc of radius-based solid angle (\(960''\)):
\[ N=\Delta\lambda\,E(500\,\mathrm{nm})\,\frac{\Omega_{FoV}}{\Omega_{\odot}}\,\frac{\lambda}{hc},\qquad \Omega_{FoV}=\mathrm{FoV}^2,\ \ \Omega_\odot=\pi(960'')^2 . \]
  • Tolerance: b5_flux: flux_rtol = \(10^{-9}\) (same formula and table), frame_atol = 0.006 of peak (measured 0.0025; PSF wings beyond \(\pm300\) px, resampling), star_flux_rtol = 0.002 (measured \(<10^{-4}\)).
  • References: ASTM G173-03 reference solar spectra (as named in the code).

docs.title: test_b5_default_science_photon_budget
docs.text:
• Module: ScienceCam default arguments (lightRatio), LightPath.
  • Tier: nightly.
  • What it checks: with default ScienceCam arguments the noise-free long-exposure frame holds flux \(\times T\times A_{eff}\) photons (default lightRatio = 1.0).
  • Theory / assumptions: none beyond photon budget.
  • Tolerance: rtol = \(10^{-6}\) (hard-coded).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_band_without_source_entry
docs.text:
• Module: ExtendedSource.__init__ (band table).
  • Tier: nightly.
  • What it checks: for bands 'IR', 'V', 'R' (including 'IR', absent from the Source table) the extended source constructs and its sub-direction sources carry the wavelength of the extended source.
