  • Theory / assumptions: convention (own band table; the wavelengths of the solar images are kept).
  • Tolerance: exact equality of the wavelength set.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_im_controller.py — Interaction matrix and control laws
docs.text:
Source: tests/test_im_controller.py

Covers SAOS.InteractionMatrixHandler (IM measurement, bookkeeping, save/load, modal-basis convention) and SAOS.Controller (reconstructors: pseudo-inverse, Tikhonov, joint/per-DM, tomography; control laws: leaky, forward/backward PI; POLC). Setup: 48 px square pupil, \(D=0.6\) m, \(6\times6\) Shack-Hartmann (all window pixels used so the centroid is odd and continuous), \(7\times7\) DM (Gaussian influence functions, coupling 0.6), Zernike basis, CPU, stroke \(2\times10^{-8}\) m, NM = 12 modes for the controller tests. Independent references (no SAOS code or outputs): dm_surface re-implements the documented DM (Gaussian influence functions with partition of unity); sh_slopes propagates a surface over each physical subaperture by a zero-padded Fourier transform sampled at 2 px per \(\lambda/d\) and takes the centre of gravity over the 15 px window; the reconstructor and control-law references are numpy SVD, Tikhonov normal equations and difference equations (scipy.signal.dlsim) written from the documented formulas. Tests that compare SAOS with another SAOS path are named test_regression_* and are explicitly not physics checks. The controller is driven with a linear modal plant \(s(k)=\mathrm{IM}\,[a(k)+c(k-D)]\) where \(a\) is the disturbance, \(c\) the modal command and \(D\) the total pure delay (mock light path returning the slopes), so the closed loop is the textbook loop. All tests are marked fast (module-level). Tolerances: tolerances/im_controller.yaml.

Control-law and loop model:

\[ c=C(z)\,e,\quad e=-R\,s,\quad u=a+z^{-D}c\ \Rightarrow\ \frac{u}{a}=S(z)=\frac{1}{1+C(z)\,z^{-D}}, \] \[ C_{\rm leaky}=\frac{g}{1-d\,z^{-1}},\quad C_{\rm fwdPI}=\frac{g+(k_i-g)z^{-1}}{1-z^{-1}},\quad C_{\rm bwdPI}=\frac{g+k_i-g\,z^{-1}}{1-z^{-1}} . \]

Reconstructors used as references (IM \(H\), SVD \(H=U\Sigma V^T\)): minimum-norm pseudo-inverse with singular values below \(r_{cond}\,s_{max}\) discarded, \(R=V_r\Sigma_r^{-1}U_r^T\); Tikhonov \(R=(H^TH+\alpha I)^{-1}H^T=V\,\mathrm{diag}\!\big(s/(s^2+\alpha)\big)U^T\) with \(\alpha=\beta\,s_{max}^2\); joint Tikhonov \(R=(H^TH+\mathrm{diag}(\alpha_i))^{-1}H^T\) with \(\alpha_i=\beta_i s_{max,i}^2\) of the columns of DM \(i\).

docs.title: test_im_columns_vs_independent_forward_model
docs.text:
• Module: InteractionMatrixHandler.measure (Zernike modal IM), with DeformableMirror and ShackHartmann.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: the absolute IM (px of slope per metre of mode amplitude) of the first 12 Zernike modes equals the independent forward model (documented DM surface propagated through a physical SH to the spot centroid). All \(2\times36\) slopes of every mode are compared in absolute terms, error normalised to the largest expected entry of the same mode. The least-squares gain SAOS/expected is recorded as information.
  • Theory / assumptions: DM surface \(w(\mathbf x)=\sum_k g_k(\mathbf x)c_k/\sum_k g_k(\mathbf x)\) with Gaussian \(g_k=\exp[\ln(0.6)\,r^2/p^2]\) (\(p\) = actuator pitch, valid actuators with \(r\le D/2+0.5p\)); the SH slope per subaperture is the centroid of \(|\mathcal F\{e^{2\pi i\,\mathrm{OPD}/\lambda}\}|^2\) sampled at \(k\lambda/(\mathrm{samp}\,d)\) over the window, minus the flat-wavefront value; a gradient \(g\) moves the spot by \(g\,\mathrm{samp}\,d/\lambda\) px. Linear regime (spot motion 0.02-0.05 px).
  • Tolerance: forward_model.abs_rel = \(3\times10^{-3}\) (precision of the reference: 32 samples per subaperture side differ from 64 by \(9\times10^{-4}\), error \(\propto 1/m^2\), \(4\times10^{-3}\) at 16).
  • References: none specific.

docs.title: test_im_symmetry_of_symmetric_modes
docs.text:
• Module: InteractionMatrixHandler.measure / ShackHartmann slope maps.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: parametrised over mode = 2 (defocus) and 9 (spherical). A DM shape with the sensor's symmetry (even under \(x\to-x\), \(y\to-y\), \(x\leftrightarrow y\)) must give slope maps with \(s_x(r,c)=-s_x(r,5-c)=s_x(5-r,c)=s_y(c,r)\), errors normalised to the largest slope. The independent DM surface symmetry is checked first (to \(10^{-10}\)).
  • Theory / assumptions: symmetry of the problem, independent of the sensor scale. The sensor uses a cell-centred subaperture split (see test_wfs.py::test_defocus_subaperture_geometry), so the mirror asymmetry of the slope maps is at the level of the independent reference (about \(2\times10^{-4}\)).
  • Tolerance: symmetry.rel = \(10^{-3}\) (float32 FFT round-off); DM surface symmetry \(\le10^{-10}\) (hard-coded).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_regression_im_column_equals_direct_wfs_response
docs.text:
• Module: InteractionMatrixHandler.measure vs ShackHartmann.wfs_measure (equal-path consistency).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: for the first 12 modes the IM column equals the WFS slopes for the OPD of the same DM shape applied directly, divided by the stroke.
  • Theory / assumptions: none (equal-path consistency; SAOS vs SAOS).
  • Tolerance: tilt.direct = \(10^{-3}\) relative to the largest entry.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_im_linear_in_stroke_and_push_pull
docs.text:
• Module: InteractionMatrixHandler.measure.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: IM = slopes/stroke is independent of stroke where the sensor is linear (2e-8 and 4e-8 m, spot motions 0.02-0.05 px) and push (\(+\)stroke) and pull (\(-\)stroke) matrices coincide, 12 modes.
  • Theory / assumptions: linear, odd response of the all-pixel centroid.
  • Tolerance: linearity.stroke = 0.01, linearity.push_pull = 0.01 relative to the largest entry.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_identical_dms_in_two_lightpaths_both_measured
docs.text:
• Module: InteractionMatrixHandler.initialize_im_class, .measure, interaction_matrix_warehouse.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: two light paths, each with its own DM and WFS (identical properties): two distinct scanned DMs; warehouse[i][j] holds an IM only where DM \(i\) is seen by light path \(j\) (i == j) and is None otherwise; both IMs non-zero and equal to each other.
  • Theory / assumptions: bookkeeping only, including DMs with identical properties.
  • Tolerance: nonzero_min = 1000 px/m (a poked DM gives about \(10^6\) px/m); equality to reconstructor.matrix = \(10^{-9}\).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_regression_save_load_im_round_trip
docs.text:
• Module: InteractionMatrixHandler.save_IM, .load_IM.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: saving and loading the IM into a fresh handler of the same optical configuration restores the IM bit by bit, and the modal-basis name ('zonal') is restored.
  • Theory / assumptions: I/O round trip only.
  • Tolerance: exact (hi = 0).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_save_im_refuses_existing_file_and_overwrites_atomically
docs.text:
• Module: InteractionMatrixHandler.save_IM, save_modalBasis, check_output_file.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: with a pre-existing HDF5 file holding unrelated content, check_output_file and both save methods raise FileExistsError and leave the file byte-identical; with overwrite=True the file is replaced (old content gone, basis_convention written), no temporary file is left in the folder, and the overwritten IM loads back bit by bit.
  • Theory / assumptions: none (I/O contract): an existing file is never appended to, and a replacement only happens once the new file is complete (temporary file renamed with os.replace).
  • Tolerance: exact (boolean checks; IM difference 0).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_regression_save_load_im_with_science_lightpath_first
docs.text:
• Module: InteractionMatrixHandler.save_IM, .load_IM.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: a science-only light path (no WFS) listed before the WFS light path does not break the save/load round trip.
  • Theory / assumptions: I/O and indexing only.
  • Tolerance: exact.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_load_im_identical_dms_and_light_paths
docs.text:
• Module: InteractionMatrixHandler.save_IM, .load_IM.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: with two light paths with identical DMs, after save and load each IM returns to its own (DM, light path) entry, identified by group indices; the two IMs are made different before saving (one scaled by 2) to tell them apart.
  • Theory / assumptions: indexing only.
  • Tolerance: exact.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_im_and_modal_basis_convention
docs.text:
• Module: InteractionMatrixHandler.save_IM, .save_modalBasis, .load_IM, .load_modalBasis, BASIS_CONVENTION.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: IM and modal-basis files carry the basis_convention attribute; an IM of another convention (attribute removed, convention 1: opposite sign of the sine Zernikes) cannot be loaded into a handler whose basis uses the current convention (ValueError); such an IM loads with a basis of its own convention.
  • Theory / assumptions: convention bookkeeping (Zernike sine sign) only.
  • Tolerance: exact.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_regression_per_dm_modal_basis_list
docs.text:
• Module: InteractionMatrixHandler.measure.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: measure(['zonal'], ...) for a one-DM system is accepted and equals measure('zonal', ...).
  • Theory / assumptions: none (equal-path consistency).
  • Tolerance: \(10^{-12}\) relative (hard-coded).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_controller_step_response_vs_ztransform
docs.text:
• Module: Controller.computeControlAction, reconstructor of reconstructionMethod='inversion'; control laws leaky and forwardPI/backwardPI.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: parametrised over (law, gain, decay, \(k_i\), \(D\)) = (leaky, 0.4, 0.99, 0, 2), (forwardPI, 0.1, 1.0, 0.2, 2), (backwardPI, 0.1, 1.0, 0.2, 1) (ids leaky-D2, forwardPI-D2, backwardPI-D1). (a) Open-loop feed (slopes \(\mathrm{IM}\,u\), step in mode 0 plus random sequence in the others): the modal command equals dlsim of \(C(z)\) applied to \(e=-u\). (b) Closed loop with pure delay \(D\): the residual to a unit step equals dlsim of \(S(z)=1/(1+C(z)z^{-D})\), other modes stay at zero. Also \(R\,\mathrm{IM}=I\) on the controlled modes.
  • Theory / assumptions: the loop model and transfer functions given in the section introduction; difference equation in float64; the plant is exactly linear.
  • Tolerance: controller: reconstructor = \(10^{-9}\) on \(\max|R\,\mathrm{IM}-I|\) (pinv with rcond \(10^{-3}\)), difference_eq = \(10^{-12}\), closed_step = \(10^{-12}\).
  • References: none specific (standard digital control textbook).

docs.title: test_rejection_transfer_function
docs.text:
• Module: Controller.computeControlAction (frequency response of the loop).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: parametrised over (law, gain, decay, \(k_i\), \(D\)) = (leaky, 0.4, 0.99, 0, 2), (leaky, 0.3, 0.995, 0, 3), (forwardPI, 0.1, 1.0, 0.2, 2), (backwardPI, 0.1, 1.0, 0.2, 1). A multisine of 7 injected bins (2, 5, 10, 20, 40, 64, 90 of a 256-frame window) in mode 0 is rejected by the loop; lock-in over an integer number of periods after the transient gives the measured \(S(e^{j\omega})\), which must equal the analytic one in magnitude and phase.
  • Theory / assumptions:
\[ S(e^{j\omega})=\frac{1}{1+C(e^{j\omega})\,e^{-j\omega D}},\quad \omega=2\pi b/N, \]

with stable poles (the maximum pole modulus is recorded). - Tolerance: controller.rejection_mag = \(10^{-9}\) (relative magnitude error), rejection_phase = \(10^{-9}\) rad. - References: none specific.

docs.title: test_single_dm_reconstructor_vs_independent_svd
docs.text:
• Module: Controller reconstructor construction (reconstructionMethod inversion and tikhonov, joint_reconstruction), computeControlAction.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: parametrised over method (inversion, tikhonov) x joint (joint, per-DM) x rank (full-rank, rank-deficient) = 8 cases. For a prescribed IM \(H\) (\(30\times8\); rank-deficient: last column \(=0.7\,c_0-1.3\,c_1\)) the reconstructor and the first command of a gain-1 leaky controller (command \(=R(-s)\), DM command = basis \(\times c\)) equal numpy references. For rank-deficient inversion also the row-space projector \(RH=V_rV_r^T\), the Penrose condition \(HRH=H\), and the absence of any null-space component in the command (minimum norm); rank kept 7.
  • Theory / assumptions: \(R_{inv}=V_r\Sigma_r^{-1}U_r^T\) (singular values \(>r_{cond}s_{max}\), \(r_{cond}=10^{-3}\)), \(R_{Tik}=V\,\mathrm{diag}(s/(s^2+\beta s_{max}^2))U^T\) (\(\beta=10^{-3}\)) \(=(H^TH+\alpha I)^{-1}H^T\).
  • Tolerance: reconstructor.matrix = \(10^{-9}\) (float64 SVD or normal equations of the same matrix; rank deficiency amplifies round-off to below \(10^{-12}\)).
  • References: none specific (Tikhonov regularisation).

docs.title: test_two_dm_coupled_reconstructors_vs_independent_solutions
docs.text:
• Module: Controller joint and per-DM reconstruction with several DMs and WFS.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: parametrised over method (inversion, tikhonov) x rank (full-rank, rank-deficient) = 4 cases. Two DMs (6 and 4 modes), two WFS (14 slopes each), both WFS see both DMs. Joint and per-DM reconstructors and commands equal the independent solutions on the stacked matrix; the slope-fit residual equals the independent one; joint inversion equals numpy lstsq minimum-norm.
  • Theory / assumptions: joint inversion \(=H^+\) of the stacked \(H\), split by DM rows; joint Tikhonov \(R=(H^TH+\mathrm{diag}(\beta_i s_{max,i}^2))^{-1}H^T\) (\(\beta\) = [1e-3, 3e-3]); per-DM uses only the columns of one DM.
  • Tolerance: reconstructor.matrix = \(10^{-9}\).
  • References: none specific.

docs.title: test_block_diagonal_reconstructors_vs_independent_solutions
docs.text:
• Module: Controller reconstruction with block-diagonal IM.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: parametrised over method (inversion, tikhonov). WFS \(i\) sees only DM \(i\) (blocks \(14\times6\) and \(14\times4\)): the joint reconstructor of DM \(i\) is the independent reconstructor of its block on the slopes of WFS \(i\) and exactly zero on the other WFS; the per-DM one is that block alone; commands equal the independent ones.
  • Theory / assumptions: pseudo-inverse and Tikhonov of a block-diagonal matrix are block-diagonal.
  • Tolerance: reconstructor.matrix = \(10^{-9}\).
  • References: none specific.

docs.title: test_coupled_joint_reconstruction_beats_per_dm
docs.text:
• Module: Controller (joint vs per-DM reconstruction).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: with both WFS seeing both DMs and consistent noise-free slopes \(s=Hc_{true}\) (full-rank \(H\)), the joint command recovers \(c_{true}\) exactly (relative error \(\le10^{-9}\)), while the per-DM commands have an error above 1 % because they ignore the cross-term (information, makes the comparison meaningful).
  • Theory / assumptions: \(RH=I\) for full column rank \(H\) (rcond \(10^{-6}\)); the per-DM reconstructor \(H_i^+\) is not the inverse of the coupled system.
  • Tolerance: joint error \(\le10^{-9}\); per-DM error \(\ge0.01\) (hard-coded).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_single_mode_shapes
docs.text:
• Module: Controller sizing (nModes, im_per_dm, reconstructor).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: with nModes = 1, for joint and per-DM reconstruction, im_per_dm[0] has shape (nSignal, 1) and reconstructor[0] has shape (1, nSignal).
  • Theory / assumptions: shapes only.
  • Tolerance: exact.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_joint_sizing_with_fewer_im_modes_than_basis
docs.text:
• Module: Controller sizing.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: an IM measured with 10 modes of a 37-mode basis gives a controller with 10 modes (reconstructor shape (10, nSignal)).
  • Theory / assumptions: shapes only.
  • Tolerance: exact.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_polc_reconstructs_the_open_loop_turbulence
docs.text:
• Module: Controller.computeControlAction with operationType='polc' (Tikhonov, leaky configuration, delay 1).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: POLC reconstructs from the pseudo-open-loop slopes \(s_{pol}=s-\mathrm{IM}\,c(k-D)=\mathrm{IM}\,a\) with the filter \(c(k)=(1-g)\,c(k-1)+g\,(-R\,s_{pol}(k))\) (unit DC gain; the decay of the configuration is not used), with \(g=0.3\). The command must equal that recursion applied to \(-R\,\mathrm{IM}\,a\), and must differ from the closed-loop law by more than 5 % of the command scale.
  • Theory / assumptions: pseudo-open-loop control: the controller reconstructs the open-loop turbulence by adding back the commanded correction, \(s_{pol}=s_{res}+D\,c\) (with \(D\) here the IM), so the result is independent of the loop; leaky integrator on the POL error.
  • Tolerance: polc.match = \(10^{-8}\); polc.differs = 0.05.
  • References: Ellerbroek & Vogel 2003 (POLC), as cited in the docstring.

docs.title: test_polc_slopes_attribute_is_minus_the_turbulence
docs.text:
• Module: Controller.slopes_polc.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: after each call slopes_polc equals \(-s_{turb}=-\mathrm{IM}\,a\) (error-sign convention); the last step is compared (30 frames).
  • Theory / assumptions: sign convention of the pseudo-open-loop slopes.
  • Tolerance: polc.sign = \(10^{-8}\) relative.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_polc_per_dm_adds_every_dm_seen_by_the_wfs
docs.text:
• Module: Controller.computeControlAction (POLC with per-DM reconstructors, joint_reconstruction=False), Controller._init_polc_cross_ims.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: one WFS (14 slopes) seen by two DMs with prescribed IMs \(B_0\) (14×6) and \(B_1\) (14×4), plant \(s(k) = t(k) + B_0 c_0(k-1) + B_1 c_1(k-1)\) with a random turbulence sequence \(t\), Controller delay 1, 12 steps. The pseudo-open-loop slope vector of each DM must be \(-t(k)\).
  • Theory / assumptions: with the error sign convention \(e = -s\), the POLC slopes of the slope vector of DM \(i\) (the WFS of its mask row) must remove every DM seen by those WFS:
\[ -s_{pol,i}(k) = -s(k) + \sum_j B_{j\to i}\,c_j(k-d_j) = -t(k), \]

so removing only DM \(i\) would leave \(B_{j}\,c_{j}\) of the other DM. - Tolerance: im_controller.polc.sign (max relative error over steps and DMs; numerical precision). - References: Ellerbroek & Vogel 2003 (POLC).

docs.title: test_polc_per_dm_missing_cross_im_raises
docs.text:
• Module: Controller._init_polc_cross_ims, Controller.computeControlAction.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: DM 1 is in the optical path of the WFS used by DM 0 (light path 0) but its IM on that WFS was not measured; DM 1 has its own WFS. The controller records the missing pair (DM 0 row, DM 1, light path 0) and computeControlAction raises ValueError instead of forming incomplete pseudo-open-loop slopes.
  • Theory / assumptions: none (configuration check).
  • Tolerance: exact (boolean checks).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_tomography_law_vs_stated_equations
docs.text:
• Module: Controller with reconstructionMethod='tomography' (R_tomo_path, set_tomography_targets, joint).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: parametrised over joint (joint, per-DM). One WFS (24 slopes), two DMs (6 and 5 modes), \(R_{tomo}\) (\(18\times24\)), target IMs \(D_i\) (\(18\times n_i\)), leaky gains [0.4, 0.3] and decays [0.98, 0.95], 25 frames of random slopes. The target reconstructors equal the independent ones, and modal and DM commands equal the recursion in numpy at every frame.
  • Theory / assumptions: learn-and-apply style law: target reconstructor \(R=(D^TD+\mathrm{diag}(\beta_i s_{max}(D_i)^2))^{-1}D^T\) with \(D=[D_1\ldots D_n]\) (joint) or \(R_i=V\,\mathrm{diag}(s/(s^2+\beta_i s_{max}^2))U^T\) of \(D_i\) (per-DM); then
\[ e_i(k)=R_i\Big(R_{tomo}(-s(k))-\sum_j D_j\,c_j(k-1)\Big),\qquad c_i(k)=g_i\,e_i(k)+d_i\,c_i(k-1). \]
  • Tolerance: reconstructor.matrix = \(10^{-9}\).
  • References: Vidal, Gendron & Rousset 2010, JOSA A 27:A253 (Learn & Apply), as named in the docstring ("L&A").

docs.title: test_learn_estimator.py — Learn & Apply estimator (von Karman slope covariance, tomographic reconstructor)
docs.text:
Source: tests/test_learn_estimator.py

Covers SAOS.tomography.learnEstimator.LearnEstimator: von Karman structure-function series (vk_structure_torch), theoretical slope covariance (compute_covariance_matrix_torch), the Phase-1 atmosphere fit (learn), the slope-to-gradient gain conversion, and the static and predictive tomographic reconstructor (build_reconstructor). LearnEstimator only reads a few attributes of its light paths, so the tests use SimpleNamespace stand-ins (6x6 WFS of \(d=0.5\) m, plate scale 0.5"/px, 640 nm), and no optics are involved. Independent references (no SAOS code): von Karman covariance with scipy Bessel-K in tests/theory.py; a slope model as a difference of phase between the midpoints of the subaperture edges; synthetic FFT von Karman phase screens with 3 levels of Lane subharmonics generated in the test. Tiers are set per test (fast for analytic and algebraic checks, nightly for the statistical screen tests). Tolerances: tolerances/learn_estimator.yaml (policy: numerical precision of the independent reference, or estimator statistics of about 3.5 sigma measured over seeds; never absorbing a measured SAOS discrepancy).

Reference model. The von Karman phase covariance and structure function (rad\(^2\) at the wavelength of \(r_0\); \(x=2\pi r/L_0\)):

\[ C(r)=C(0)\,\frac{2^{1/6}}{\Gamma(5/6)}\,x^{5/6}K_{5/6}(x),\qquad C(0)=\frac{6\pi}{5}\,0.0229\,\Big(\frac{L_0}{r_0}\Big)^{5/3},\qquad D(r)=2\,[C(0)-C(r)], \]

with PSD \(\Phi(f)=0.0229\,r_0^{-5/3}(f^2+L_0^{-2})^{-11/6}\) (theory.vk_psd). The slope is modelled as the phase difference between the edge midpoints \(A_i,a_i\) of subaperture \(i\), \(s_i=[\phi(A_i)-\phi(a_i)]/d_i\), so for layers \(l\) with weights \(w_l\),

\[ \mathrm{Cov}(s_i,s_j)=\sum_l w_l\,\frac{C(A_i-B_j)-C(A_i-b_j)-C(a_i-B_j)+C(a_i-b_j)}{d_i\,d_j}. \]

The MMSE (Learn & Apply) reconstructor and the frozen-flow prediction:

\[ R=C_{ts}\,(C_{ss}+C_{nn})^{-1},\qquad \mathrm{Cov}\big(\phi(\mathbf r_a,t+\Delta t),\phi(\mathbf r_b,t)\big)=C(\mathbf r_a-\mathbf r_b-\mathbf V\Delta t). \]

docs.title: test_vk_series_exact_grid
docs.text:
• Module: LearnEstimator.vk_structure_torch, prepare_vk_constants_torch.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: the 10-term series for the von Karman structure function against the exact Bessel-K \(D(r)=2[C(0)-C(r)]\) on the EST range of separations \(r\in[1\,\mathrm{cm},8.5\,\mathrm{m}]\) (60 log-spaced points; 8.5 m = metapupil at 15 km with a 60" field), for \(L_0\in\{10,25,50\}\) m, \(r_0=0.15\) m. The value at \(r=8\) m, \(L_0=5\) m, outside the range of use, is recorded for information.
  • Theory / assumptions: series is exact in the range of use; it is invalid for \(L_0\lesssim7\) m with \(r\ge6\) m (\(x=\pi r/L_0>3\)).
  • Tolerance: vk_series.use_rtol = \(10^{-4}\) (measured \(6.1\times10^{-5}\) at \(L_0=10\) m, \(r=8.5\) m; \(\le10^{-8}\) for \(L_0\ge15\) m).
  • References: von Karman covariance as in Roddier, "Adaptive Optics in Astronomy" (chapter on atmospheric turbulence); not further specified in the code.

docs.title: test_phase1_L0_lower_bound
docs.text:
• Module: LearnEstimator.learn (Phase-1 fit), L0_min.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: learn() bounds \(L_0\) to the validity of the series, \(L_0\ge\pi r_{max}/3\) (\(r_{max}\) the largest separation of the problem, about 3.5-4.3 m for the 6x6, 3 m WFS). Starting from \(L_0=1\) m the bound is in \([\pi\cdot3/3,\pi\cdot4.5/3]\) and the fitted \(L_0\) is not below it. Uses synthetic slopes from independent screens (100 samples, 5 iterations).
  • Theory / assumptions: series validity \(x=\pi r/L_0\le3\).
  • Tolerance: bound range and sign hard-coded.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_vk_series_convergent_region
docs.text:
• Module: LearnEstimator.vk_structure_torch.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: control: where the series converges (\(x=\pi r/L_0\le1\)) it equals the exact Bessel-K \(D(r)\), for \(r\in[1\,\mathrm{cm},L_0/\pi]\) and \(L_0\in\{5,10,25,50\}\) m; also \(D(0)=0\) exactly.
  • Theory / assumptions: as above.
  • Tolerance: vk_series.rtol = \(10^{-6}\) (reference cancellation error \(C(0)-C(r)\le10^{-10}\) relative at \(r=1\) cm); \(D(0)\) exact.
  • References: none specific.

docs.title: test_css_matches_analytic
docs.text:
• Module: LearnEstimator.compute_covariance_matrix_torch (theoretical \(C_{ss}\)).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: the covariance matrix for 3 WFS (6x6, \(d=0.5\) m, directions (0",0), (30",0), (30",90)), 3 layers at 0, 4, 10 km with weights [0.5, 0.3, 0.2], \(r_0=0.12\) m, \(L_0=25\) m, equals the independent Bessel-K reference built from the WFS geometry; with per-WFS noise variance [0.5, 1, 2] added on the diagonal it equals \(C_{ref}+C_{nn}\).
  • Theory / assumptions: edge-midpoint slope covariance above; layers shifted by \(h\,\theta\) at the source direction.
  • Tolerance: matrix.rtol = \(10^{-8}\) relative to \(\max|C_{ref}|\) (float64, same formula).
  • References: Vidal, Gendron & Rousset 2010, JOSA A 27:A253 (theoretical \(C_{ss}\) of Learn & Apply).

docs.title: test_css_symmetric_positive_semidefinite
docs.text:
• Module: LearnEstimator.compute_covariance_matrix_torch.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: the noise-free \(C_{ss}\) of the same configuration is symmetric (\(|C-C^T|/|C|\)) and positive semi-definite (lowest over largest eigenvalue).
  • Theory / assumptions: a covariance matrix of real slopes.
  • Tolerance: matrix.asym_rtol = \(10^{-12}\), matrix.psd_rtol = \(10^{-9}\) (float64 eigvalsh).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_css_vs_independent_screens
docs.text:
• Module: LearnEstimator.compute_covariance_matrix_torch, compared with Monte Carlo.
  • Tier: nightly.
  • What it checks: the theoretical slope covariance against the empirical covariance of slopes from 1200 independent von Karman screens (\(N=256\), \(h=d/4\), \(r_0=0.15\) m, \(L_0=10\) m, one 6x6 WFS, one layer, FFT with Lane subharmonics generated in the test). The statistic \(Q=\sum(\hat C-C)^2/\sum\mathrm{Var}\) is compared with its expectation 1, and \(\mathrm{tr}\,\hat C/\mathrm{tr}\,C\) with 1.
  • Theory / assumptions: for \(n\) independent zero-mean Gaussian realisations the sample covariance has \(\mathrm{Var}(\hat C_{ij})=(C_{ii}C_{jj}+C_{ij}^2)/n\), hence \(E[Q]=1\). The reference has a bias of at most 1.5 % due to FFT grid truncation above Nyquist. Subaperture-averaged slopes would differ from the midpoint model and are not part of the criteria.
  • Tolerance: screens: q_lo = 0.67, q_hi = 1.38 (mean 1.02, sigma 0.10 over 9 seeds, band mean \(\pm3.5\sigma\)); trace_atol = 0.035 (mean 0.985, sigma 0.55 %, 1.5 % bias plus \(3.5\sigma\)).
  • References: Lane subharmonics screen generation as commonly used (not cited in the code).

docs.title: test_gain_slopes_to_phase_gradient
docs.text:
• Module: LearnEstimator.learn (gain passed to compute_measurement_covariance).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: the factor that learn() passes to compute_measurement_covariance (captured by a spy on random slopes, 1 iteration) equals \(2\pi\,\mathrm{ps}/(206265\times500\,\mathrm{nm})\), independent of the WFS wavelength (640 nm here) and the subaperture size.
  • Theory / assumptions: a slope of \(s\) px moves the spot by \(s\,\mathrm{ps}/206265\) rad, i.e. an OPD gradient (achromatic); the von Karman model is the phase structure function of \(r_0\) at 500 nm (Atmosphere convention), so the conversion to a phase gradient in rad/m uses \(2\pi/500\) nm.
  • Tolerance: gain.rtol = \(10^{-9}\).
  • References: none specific.

docs.title: test_phase1_recovers_r0
docs.text:
• Module: LearnEstimator.learn (Phase 1: gradient-based fit of \(r_0\), \(L_0\), noise variance).
  • Tier: nightly.
  • What it checks: slopes from independent von Karman screens (\(r_0=0.15\) m, \(L_0=10\) m, one layer, 1000 samples, noise-free) with the fit started at \(1.3\,r_0\); the gain is replaced by the correct one so the test is independent of the gain test. \(|r_{0,fit}/r_0-1|\) must be within the tolerance.
  • Theory / assumptions: maximum-likelihood style fit of the theoretical \(C_{ss}\) to the measured slope covariance; L0 and noise couple to \(r_0\) in the joint fit (+0.9 % mean bias).
  • Tolerance: phase1.r0_rtol = 0.03 (mean +0.9 %, sigma 0.5 % over 9 seeds; mean plus \(3.5\sigma\)).
  • References: Vidal, Gendron & Rousset 2010 (Learn & Apply); Martin et al. 2016 (on-sky L&A) is not cited in the test.

docs.title: test_phase1_recovers_r0_end_to_end
docs.text:
• Module: LearnEstimator.learn.
  • Tier: nightly.
  • What it checks: the same as test_phase1_recovers_r0 with the unmodified gain of learn(): \(r_0\) must be recovered from slopes in pixels.
  • Theory / assumptions: as above.
  • Tolerance: phase1.r0_rtol = 0.03.
  • References: as above.

docs.title: test_reconstructor_static
docs.text:
• Module: LearnEstimator.build_reconstructor (static, \(\Delta t=0\)).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: parametrised over permute = False, True. The non-predictive reconstructor \(R=C_{ts}(C_{ss}+C_{nn})^{-1}\) (3 WFS sensed, 2 target directions, 3 layers, noise [0.3, 0.6, 0.9], regularisation \(10^{-9}\)) equals the independent Bessel-K reference, both in the natural order [X of all WFS, Y of all WFS] and with permute_for_controller ([WFS0_X, WFS0_Y, WFS1_X, ...]).
  • Theory / assumptions: MMSE (Bayesian) reconstructor, \(R=C_{ts}(C_{ss}+C_{nn})^{-1}\).
  • Tolerance: reconstructor.rtol = \(10^{-7}\) (float64, same regularisation; Cholesky solve conditioning).
  • References: Vidal, Gendron & Rousset 2010 (Learn & Apply).

docs.title: test_reconstructor_predicts_future
docs.text:
• Module: LearnEstimator.build_reconstructor (predictive with winds and \(\Delta t\)).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: with frozen flow, winds (10, 3), (-6, 8), (0, 0) m/s and \(\Delta t=20\) ms, the covariance between the target at \(t+\Delta t\) and the sensed slopes at \(t\) is \(C(\mathbf r_t-\mathbf r_s-\mathbf V\Delta t)\). Two criteria: the exact error variance \(\mathrm{tr}\,E[(Rs-t)(Rs-t)^T]\) of \(R_{saos}\) equals that of the optimal reference built with \(-V\Delta t\); and \(R_{saos}\) itself matches that reference. The retrodiction reconstructor (\(+V\Delta t\)) error is recorded for information.
  • Theory / assumptions: Taylor frozen flow, \(\phi(\mathbf r,t)=\phi_0(\mathbf r-\mathbf V t)\); error trace \(=\mathrm{tr}\,[C_{tt}-RC_{ts}^T-C_{ts}R^T+R\,C_{ss}R^T]\) with exact covariances.
  • Tolerance: reconstructor.err_ratio_atol = \(10^{-6}\) on \(\mathrm{tr}E[R_{saos}]/\mathrm{tr}E[R_{opt}]-1\); reconstructor.rtol = \(10^{-7}\).
  • References: Vidal, Gendron & Rousset 2010; predictive extension as described by Martin et al. 2016 is not cited in the code.

docs.title: test_reconstructor_zero_wind_ignores_dt
docs.text:
• Module: LearnEstimator.build_reconstructor.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: control: with zero winds the shift is zero, so any \(\Delta t\) gives the static reconstructor (also equal to the reference).
  • Theory / assumptions: shift \(=V\Delta t=0\).
  • Tolerance: reconstructor.rtol = \(10^{-7}\).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_default_dt_is_delay_plus_one
docs.text:
• Module: LearnEstimator.build_reconstructor (dt=None default).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: a light path with delay \(d\) frames has a total pure delay \((d+1)T_s\) (SAOS convention, tests/test_timing.py), so with dt=None the reconstructor predicts \((d+1)T_s\) ahead and equals the one with explicit \(\Delta t=(d+1)T_s\) (\(d=2\), \(T_s=5\) ms). The result with \(dT_s\) is recorded to show the test discriminates.
  • Theory / assumptions: timing convention only.
  • Tolerance: reconstructor.dt_rtol = \(10^{-9}\) (same code path).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_frozen_flow_cross_covariance_sign
docs.text:
• Module: none from SAOS (reference check of the sign used by the predictive tests; uses only theory.py and the test's screens).
  • Tier: nightly.
  • What it checks: with a layer moving at \(V=+x\), \(V\Delta t=1\) m (8 px of \(h=0.125\) m), \(\phi(x,t+\Delta t)=\phi_0(x-V\Delta t)\): the empirical covariance between the slopes of the same 6x6 WFS at \(t+\Delta t\) (rows) and at \(t\) (columns), from 1500 independent screens, agrees with the theory with shift \(-V\Delta t\) and not with \(+V\Delta t\) (relative Frobenius norm).
  • Theory / assumptions: frozen flow, \(\mathrm{Cov}(\phi(\mathbf r_a,t+\Delta t),\phi(\mathbf r_b,t))=C(\mathbf r_a-\mathbf r_b-\mathbf V\Delta t)\).
  • Tolerance: frozen_flow.err_hi = 0.18 for the right sign (mean 0.160, sigma 0.006 over 9 seeds); frozen_flow.wrong_sign_lo = 1.0 for the wrong sign (measured 1.40, more than 6 times the right-sign error).
  • References: none specific.

docs.title: test_modal_basis.py — modal bases for DM commands and interaction matrices (T1)
docs.text:
Source: tests/test_modal_basis.py

Covers SAOS.modalBasis.zonalModes.generate_zonal_modes, discHarmonicModes.generate_dh_modes, karhunenLoeveModes.generate_kl_modes, hadamardModes.generate_hadamard_modes and zernikeModes.generate_zernike_modes / ZernikeNaive.R_nm_Jacobi. Bases are evaluated on the actuator coordinates of an 11x11 cartesian ground DeformableMirror (97 valid actuators, 32 px pupil, only the actuator geometry is used) or of an equivalent cartesian grid (e.g. 37x37 for the EST ASM) where only coordinates are needed; columns are modes normalised to \(\max|\cdot| = 1\). The strategy is structural (rank, orthogonality, piston content) plus comparison with independent definitions written in the test (Noll ordering and Zernike formula through Jacobi polynomials, Noll Kolmogorov covariance, Neumann eigenfunctions of the Laplacian on the disk), mostly through subspace distances. The bases are deterministic, so tolerances (tests/tolerances/modal_basis.yaml) are numerical, not statistical. Whole module fast.

Independent references defined in the file: Noll ordering \(j\to(n,m,\cos|\sin)\); Zernike polynomials

\[Z_j = N_{nm}\,R_n^{|m|}(\rho)\,\{\cos,\sin\}(m\theta),\quad N_{nm}=\sqrt{n+1}\ (m=0),\ \sqrt{2(n+1)}\ (m\neq0),\quad R_n^m(\rho) = (-1)^k\rho^m P_k^{(m,0)}(1-2\rho^2),\ k=\tfrac{n-m}{2};\]

and the Neumann eigenfunctions \(J_m(k\rho)\{\cos,\sin\}(m\theta)\) with \(J_m'(k)=0\) used for disk harmonics.

docs.title: test_basis_spans_actuator_space
docs.text:
• Module: generate_zonal_modes, generate_dh_modes, generate_kl_modes, generate_hadamard_modes.
  • Tier: fast. Parametrised over name = zonal, dh, kl, hadamard.
  • What it checks: the basis restricted to the valid actuators has rank equal to its number of modes (singular values above \(10^{-10}s_{max}\)). For the piston-free bases (dh, kl, hadamard) each mode has \(|\mathrm{mean}|/\mathrm{rms}\) below tolerance and the number of modes is at most \(n_{valid}-1\). The zonal basis is the identity on the valid actuators.
  • Tolerance: modal_basis.basis: rank_rel_sv \(10^{-10}\), piston_fraction \(10^{-10}\) (piston-free modes measure about \(10^{-16}\)).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_orthogonal_bases_have_diagonal_gram
docs.text:
• Module: generate_zonal_modes, generate_dh_modes, generate_kl_modes (QR-orthonormalised).
  • Tier: fast. Parametrised over name = zonal, dh, kl.
  • What it checks: the Gram matrix \(B^TB\) on the valid actuators is diagonal: \(\max|G_{ij}|_{i\ne j}/\max G_{ii}\).
  • Tolerance: modal_basis.basis.gram_offdiag = \(10^{-10}\) (measured about \(3\times10^{-16}\) for DH/KL).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_zernike_rank_limited_by_actuator_sampling
docs.text:
• Module: generate_zernike_modes (default nModes = number of valid actuators).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: for the 11x11 DM and a 37x37 grid (EST ASM size, threshold 0.7533 pitch) the first half of the modes is full rank and the piston fraction is below tolerance; the rank with nModes = nValidAct is only recorded. As the docstring states, high-order Zernikes alias on the actuator grid and the full basis is rank deficient, a property of the sampling and not of the polynomial evaluation, so it is recorded and not failed (IMs with the full Zernike basis contain dependent columns that only regularisation removes).
  • Tolerance: rank deficiency of the first half exactly 0 (singular values above \(10^{-10}s_{max}\), basis.rank_rel_sv); basis.piston_fraction \(10^{-10}\).
  • References: Noll 1976 (Zernike modes); sampling argument is generic.

docs.title: test_noll_covariance_reference_matches_noll_table
docs.text:
• Module: none from SAOS; sanity check of the test's own Noll covariance reference.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: the variances of \(Z_2\ldots Z_{11}\) from the implemented covariance, relative to \(Z_2\), equal \((\Delta_{j-1}-\Delta_j)/(\Delta_1-\Delta_2)\) from Noll's table of residual variances. The overall constant of the formula is 1.3 % above the table (0.4536 against 0.4479 for \(Z_2\)), irrelevant for eigenvectors; recorded.
  • Theory / assumptions: Kolmogorov covariance of Noll-normalised coefficients (Noll 1976 eq. 16), in units of \((D/r_0)^{5/3}\):
\[\langle a_j a_{j'}\rangle = K\,(-1)^{(n+n'-2m)/2}\sqrt{(n+1)(n'+1)}\;\frac{\Gamma\!\left(\frac{n+n'-5/3}{2}\right)}{\Gamma\!\left(\frac{n-n'+17/3}{2}\right)\Gamma\!\left(\frac{n'-n+17/3}{2}\right)\Gamma\!\left(\frac{n+n'+23/3}{2}\right)}\]

for \(m=m'\) and equal parity of \(j\) (or \(m=0\)), zero otherwise; \(K=\Gamma(14/3)\left[\tfrac{24}{5}\Gamma(\tfrac65)\right]^{5/6}\Gamma(\tfrac{11}{6})^2/(2\pi^2)\). - Tolerance: absolute \(10^{-3}\) on the variance ratios (covers the 4-digit rounding of the table; hard-coded). - References: Noll 1976, JOSA 66:207 (eq. 16 and table IV).

docs.title: test_kl_modes_are_the_atmospheric_eigenmodes_of_the_zernike_subspace
docs.text:
• Module: generate_kl_modes (first 20 modes of an 11x11 DM).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: (1) the KL modes lie in the span of piston-free Zernikes sampled on the valid actuators (Noll 2 to 21, radial orders 1 to 5 complete); (2) the variance of each mode, \(\mathbf a^TC\mathbf a\), equals the eigenvalue of the same rank, and variances are non-increasing; (3) each cluster of degenerate eigenvalues (relative gap \(10^{-6}\)) spans the same subspace as the independent eigenvectors; (4) the modes are orthogonal on the actuators and their amplitudes are uncorrelated (covariance diagonal).
  • Theory / assumptions: double diagonalisation. With \(Z=QR\) (QR of the independent Noll-normalised Zernikes on the actuators) and \(C\) the Noll covariance of the coefficients, the KL modes are \(QU\) where \(U\) diagonalises \(R\,C\,R^T\), ordered by decreasing variance. Kolmogorov statistics; finite sampled pupil.
  • Tolerance: modal_basis.kl: span \(10^{-8}\), eig_rel \(10^{-8}\) (variance ratio and covariance diagonality), subspace \(10^{-6}\) (spectral norm of the projector difference per cluster; also the Gram orthogonality bound).
  • References: Noll 1976 (covariance); none beyond Noll 1976; the KL construction is the test's own.

docs.title: test_dh_lowest_modes_span_the_lowest_neumann_eigenfunctions
docs.text:
• Module: generate_dh_modes.
  • Tier: fast. Parametrised over count = 2, 5.
  • What it checks: the first count DH modes (2: the \(k=1.841\) pair; 5: plus the 3.054 pair and the \(k=3.832\) axisymmetric mode; complete eigenvalue levels) span the count lowest eigenfunctions of the independent construction evaluated on the valid actuators of an 11x11 DM (disk radius is the outermost valid actuator, piston removed on the actuators), measured as the spectral norm of the difference of the projectors.
  • Theory / assumptions: disk harmonics are the eigenfunctions of the Laplacian on the disk with zero normal derivative at the edge, \(J_m(k\rho)\{\cos,\sin\}(m\theta)\) with \(J_m'(k)=0\), sorted by eigenvalue \(k\); the constant (\(m=0\), \(k=0\)) is excluded.
  • Tolerance: modal_basis.dh.subspace = \(10^{-8}\).
  • References: Milton & Lloyd-Hart 2005 (disk harmonics for adaptive optics); standard Neumann problem on the disk.

docs.title: test_dh_radial_order_shells_span_documented_functions
docs.text:
• Module: generate_dh_modes.
  • Tier: fast. Parametrised over nmax = 1, 2, 3, 4.
  • What it checks: the documented Noll-like labelling of SAOS disk harmonics: the first modes completing radial orders \(1..n_{max}\) span exactly the functions \(J_m(kr)\{\cos,\sin\}(m\theta)\) with \(k\) the \(q\)-th root of \(J_m'\), \(q=(n-|m|)/2+1\) for \(m\ne0\) and \(n/2\) for \(m=0\). The distance to the lowest-eigenvalue set (the labelling is not eigenvalue-ordered) is informational.
  • Tolerance: modal_basis.dh.subspace = \(10^{-8}\).
  • References: Milton & Lloyd-Hart 2005.

docs.title: test_zernike_low_order_shapes
docs.text:
• Module: generate_zernike_modes.
  • Tier: fast. Parametrised over Noll index 2 (tip, \(\rho\cos\theta\to x\)), 4 (defocus, \(2\rho^2-1\)), 6 (astigmatism, \(x^2-y^2\)), 11 (spherical, \(6\rho^4-6\rho^2+1\)).
  • What it checks: the SAOS mode with the given Noll index, on the valid actuators with piston removed, is positively correlated with the analytic shape (correlation above 0.999). Fixes the sign convention for even-\(j\) (cosine) and \(m=0\) modes.
  • Tolerance: modal_basis.zernike.shape_correlation = 0.999 (measured \(1-10^{-15}\) for exact polynomials).
  • References: Noll 1976.

docs.title: test_zernike_noll_sign_convention
docs.text:
• Module: generate_zernike_modes.
  • Tier: fast. Parametrised over Noll index 3 (\(2\rho\sin\theta\to y\)) and 5 (\(\sqrt6\rho^2\sin2\theta\to xy\)).
  • What it checks: the odd-\(j\) (sine) modes follow Noll's sign convention: positive correlation with \(+y\) and \(+xy\) (correlation above 0.999), with \(y\) = +row of the actuator coordinates.
  • Tolerance: modal_basis.zernike.shape_correlation = 0.999.
  • References: Noll 1976.

docs.title: test_zernike_radial_polynomial_low_orders
docs.text:
• Module: ZernikeNaive.R_nm_Jacobi.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: the SAOS radial polynomial (Jacobi form, the evaluator used to build the basis) matches the scipy-Jacobi reference for every \(n\le30\) and all allowed \(m\) on 501 points of \(\rho\in[0,1]\).
  • Tolerance: modal_basis.zernike.radial_abs_low_orders = \(10^{-5}\) (DMs up to about 22x22 actuators).
  • References: standard Jacobi representation of \(R_n^m\) (e.g. Born & Wolf).

docs.title: test_zernike_radial_jacobi_evaluator
docs.text:
• Module: ZernikeNaive.R_nm_Jacobi.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: the Jacobi evaluator is accurate up to \(n=49\) (sampled orders \(n=0,7,\ldots,49\)). The physical bound \(|R|\le1\) makes the absolute criterion meaningful.
  • Tolerance: modal_basis.zernike.radial_abs = \(10^{-6}\) (the evaluator gives about \(10^{-13}\) at \(n=49\)).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_zernike_radial_polynomial_est_orders
docs.text:
• Module: generate_zernike_modes for an EST-size DM (37x37, Zernike up to \(n\approx49\)).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: the basis generated by SAOS equals, column by column, the same basis rebuilt with R_nm_Jacobi temporarily replaced by the module's independent radial reference (patched in a try/finally); the number of columns differing by more than the bound must be 0. The numerical rank ratio (singular values above \(10^{-8}s_{max}\)) is recorded as information (aliasing on the grid at the highest orders is a physical limit). A plot of the radial error against \(n=31..49\) is produced.
  • Tolerance: modal_basis.zernike.basis_column_abs = 0.01 on the maximum column difference (modes are normalised to \(\max|Z|=1\)); radial_abs \(10^{-6}\) is the reference line of the plot.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_packaging.py — wheel contents and declared dependencies (nightly)
docs.text:
Source: tests/test_packaging.py

Covers the packaging of SAOS (setup.cfg / build metadata) rather than any physics class. A wheel is built from the repository (pip wheel --no-deps --no-build-isolation, module-scoped fixture) and inspected as a zip file. The check is independent of the packaging metadata: source packages are found by walking SAOS/, and third-party imports are read from the source with ast (excluding sys.stdlib_module_names and SAOS), with the import-name to distribution mapping cv2 to opencv-contrib-python and zmq to pyzmq. No statistics or theory are involved. Whole module nightly (it builds a wheel).

docs.title: test_wheel_contains_every_subpackage_and_the_data_command
docs.text:
• Module: packages, package data and entry points of the SAOS distribution.
  • Tier: nightly.
  • What it checks: every directory of SAOS/ containing Python modules appears in the wheel as a package (a directory with __init__.py); the wheel contains no HDF5 file (the solar images are downloaded by SAOS.data); and the console script saos-download-data = SAOS.data:main is declared.
  • Tolerance: exact (zero missing subpackages, zero HDF5 files, entry point present).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_wheel_requirements_match_the_imports
docs.text:
• Module: wheel METADATA (Requires-Dist, Requires-Python).
  • Tier: nightly.
  • What it checks: the set of declared requirements equals the set of third-party modules imported by the package (nothing imported but undeclared, nothing declared but never imported), and Requires-Python is exactly >=3.10.
  • Tolerance: exact (zero differences in both directions; exact string for the Python requirement).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_parallel_gpu.py — Parallel (threads) and GPU execution
docs.text:
Source: tests/test_parallel_gpu.py

Covers the execution-mode independence of SAOS: joblib threaded LightPath.propagate (sharing Atmosphere, Telescope, DeformableMirror, ShackHartmann, ScienceCam), CPU versus CUDA execution of ShackHartmann, ScienceCam, DeformableMirror, InteractionMatrixHandler and Controller, thread counts and the VRAM peak. By documented policy these are the only tests whose reference is SAOS itself ("equivalence tests"): the result of a configuration must not depend on how it is executed. There is no theory; numerical agreement is set by the arithmetic precision of each computation (float64 for DM, ScienceCam, Controller; float32 inside the ShackHartmann field cube and centroid). Controller and InteractionMatrixHandler hard-code "cuda if available", so the CPU version is built with torch.cuda.is_available patched to False during construction. Module-level marker is nightly; tests that need CUDA additionally carry gpu (skipped when no GPU is visible). Tolerances: tolerances/parallel_gpu.yaml (provisional, calibrated 2026-10-26, GTX 1660).

The Multi fixture builds a telescope (48 px, \(D=0.6\) m), a 3-layer atmosphere (winds 8/15/25 m/s, directions 0/70/200 deg, altitudes 0/4/11 km), a shared ground DM (\(7\times7\)) and \(n\) light paths (one source direction, one WFS and one ScienceCam each), rebuilt with identical seeds for each execution mode.

docs.title: test_threads_bit_identical_to_sequential_noise_off
docs.text:
• Module: LightPath.propagate under joblib.Parallel(prefer='threads').
  • Tier: nightly (no gpu marker; runs on CPU).
  • What it checks: six light paths sharing atmosphere, telescope and one DM, each with its own WFS and science camera, are propagated for 3 steps with n_jobs = 1, 2, 8 (noise off). OPD, slopes, WFS frames and science frames are bit-identical to the sequential run.
  • Theory / assumptions: the same computation, only the scheduling differs; shared objects must be thread-safe.
  • Tolerance: threads.exact = 0.0 (bit equality). The maximum slope magnitude is recorded to show a signal is present.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_threads_reproducible_with_per_object_seeds_and_noise
docs.text:
• Module: LightPath.propagate with Detector noise (ShackHartmann(noiseFlag=True, randomState)).
  • Tier: nightly.
  • What it checks: with detector noise on and a distinct seed per WFS (seed = 100 + path index), results for n_jobs = 1 and 8 are bit-identical, and two runs with n_jobs = 8 coincide.
  • Theory / assumptions: the noise stream of a detector does not depend on scheduling when each detector is used by one light path (a shared RNG would break this; see the next test).
  • Tolerance: threads.exact = 0.0.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_threads_reproducible_with_shared_detector
docs.text:
• Module: LightPath.propagate with one WFS (one Detector, one seed) shared by four light paths.
  • Tier: nightly.
  • What it checks: four light paths sharing one WFS are propagated with n_jobs = 1 and 8; a reproducible simulator should give the same noisy slopes for the same path regardless of scheduling, and two runs with n_jobs = 8 should coincide. The maximum slope difference is recorded.
  • Theory / assumptions: reproducibility with a shared random state; the test fails if the order of noise draws from the shared Detector random state depends on thread scheduling.
  • Tolerance: threads.exact = 0.0.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_thread_count_inside_threaded_lightpaths_within_cpu_count
docs.text:
• Module: Atmosphere.getOPD for an extended (sun-like) source with nine point directions, called from 8 joblib threads.
  • Tier: nightly.
  • What it checks: resource criterion. Eight concurrent getOPD calls, each parallelising its 9 directions, are repeated 3 times after a warm-up; the worker threads created (peak minus baseline of threading.active_count() and, if psutil is available, of OS threads) must not exceed os.cpu_count().
  • Theory / assumptions: none (no oversubscription of threads).
  • Tolerance: threads_count.max_threads = 0, meaning os.cpu_count() is used as limit.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_gpu_matches_cpu_shackhartmann
docs.text:
• Module: ShackHartmann.wfs_measure (device='cpu' vs 'cuda').
  • Tier: nightly + gpu.
  • What it checks: the same Kolmogorov-like phase (1 rad rms, masked by the pupil) through a CPU and a CUDA ShackHartmann (6x6, 48 px, noise off) gives the same slopes (absolute, px) and the same frame (relative to its peak).
  • Theory / assumptions: the cube of subaperture fields is complex64 and the centroid float32, so agreement is at float32 precision.
  • Tolerance: cpu_gpu.shackhartmann_slope_px = \(10^{-5}\) px (measured 1.9e-6), cpu_gpu.shackhartmann_frame_rel = \(10^{-6}\) of the peak (measured 2e-7).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_gpu_matches_cpu_sciencecam
docs.text:
• Module: ScienceCam.get_frame (device='cpu' vs 'cuda').
  • Tier: nightly + gpu.
  • What it checks: a 2 rad rms smooth phase on a 64 px pupil gives the same science frame on CPU and GPU, relative to the peak.
  • Theory / assumptions: complex128 FFT on both devices; differences only from the order of floating-point operations.
  • Tolerance: cpu_gpu.sciencecam_rel = \(10^{-10}\) of the peak.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_gpu_matches_cpu_deformablemirror
docs.text:
• Module: DeformableMirror.updateDMShape, get_dm_opd (device='cpu' vs 'cuda').
  • Tier: nightly + gpu.
  • What it checks: the OPD of a random command (\(10^{-7}\) m scale, \(9\times9\) DM) for a ground layer and a 4 km layer (footprint shift for a source at 15", 30 deg) agrees between CPU and GPU, relative to the maximum.
  • Theory / assumptions: float64 influence-matrix product; only summation ordering differs.
  • Tolerance: cpu_gpu.dm_rel = \(10^{-12}\) relative to the maximum.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_gpu_matches_cpu_interaction_matrix_and_controller
docs.text:
• Module: InteractionMatrixHandler.measure, Controller.computeControlAction (CPU vs CUDA).
  • Tier: nightly + gpu.
  • What it checks: (i) zernike IMs measured on a CPU-built system (with torch.cuda.is_available patched to False) and on a GPU system agree: the slope-level difference \(\max|\mathrm{IM}_{cpu}-\mathrm{IM}_{gpu}|\times\mathrm{stroke}\) stays within float32 precision. (ii) Controllers (inversion, leaky gain 0.4 decay 0.99, 12 modes) built on the same IM, one per device and verified to be on cpu and cuda, give identical modal and DM commands over 10 random slope vectors.
  • Theory / assumptions: WFS slopes are float32 (hence the IM tolerance); the controller is float64 (matrix products, Cholesky/SVD).
  • Tolerance: cpu_gpu.im_slope_px = \(10^{-5}\) px (measured 4.3e-6), cpu_gpu.controller_rel = \(10^{-10}\) relative to the maximum.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_vram_peak_within_budget
docs.text:
• Module: whole GPU path (ShackHartmann, ScienceCam, DeformableMirror, Atmosphere, LightPath) on CUDA.
  • Tier: nightly + gpu.
  • What it checks: for a fixed small configuration (64 px pupil, \(8\times8\) SH with 2x oversampled 16 px windows, \(9\times9\) DM, 64 px science camera, 5 steps) the peak torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated above the baseline is (i) at least the analytic size of the dominant tensor, the complex64 field cube of the SH, and (ii) below the recorded budget times a headroom (guard against a leak or per-step copy). The final allocated memory is recorded.
  • Theory / assumptions: analytic size of the SH field cube,
\[ V_{cube}=n_{subap}^2\,n_{FFT}^2\times 8\ \text{B},\qquad n_{FFT}=\mathrm{round}\!\Big(\frac{\lambda\cdot206265}{d\cdot\mathrm{plate\_scale}}\,n_{lenslet}\Big), \]

(8 bytes per complex64 element); the peak must be at least this. - Tolerance: vram.budget_mib = 8.7 MiB (measured peak 8.62 MiB, GTX 1660) times vram.headroom = 1.25. - References: none.

docs.title: test_perturbations.py — Vibration, LocalSeeing, spider arms, NCPA, logging at exit (T2)
docs.text:
Source: tests/test_perturbations.py

Covers SAOS.Vibration, SAOS.LocalSeeing, Telescope.apply_spiders, SAOS.NCPA, SAOS.LightPath (how the perturbations enter the WFS and science paths), SAOS.ScienceCam, SAOS.ShackHartmann (only as a witness that NCPA does not reach it), SAOS.LoggingHelper, and the Source constructor for laser guide stars. Expectations are independent of SAOS: a sky tilt \(\theta\) moves a diffraction-limited image by \(\theta/\mathrm{plate\_scale}\) pixels; injected OPD equals the file; the area removed by spiders equals an exact strip-annulus integral; spider diffraction spikes are perpendicular to the arms, checked against an FFT of an independently built mask; logging is checked in subprocesses. Whole module nightly. Tolerances: tests/tolerances/perturbations.yaml (provisional, calibrated 2026-10-26).

Helper estimator used for image shifts: sub-pixel peak position by 16x (or 8x) Fourier upsampling plus parabolic refinement, valid for band-limited PSFs.

docs.title: test_vibration_one_step_tilt_moves_image_by_file_angle
docs.text:
• Module: Vibration.getCurrentVibrations through LightPath.propagate(temporal_tick=True) and ScienceCam.
  • Tier: nightly.
  • What it checks: with no atmosphere and no AO, iteration \(k\) injects \((x_k, y_k)\) arcsec from an HDF5 file; the ScienceCam peak (64 px, 4 px per \(\lambda/D\), 1 m telescope, R band) moves, relative to the zero-vibration frame, by \(x_k/\mathrm{plate\_scale}\) px towards +col and \(y_k/\mathrm{plate\_scale}\) towards +row. The fitted slope measured/file is recorded and must be 1.00.
  • Theory / assumptions: a small tilt \(\theta\) of the wavefront displaces the PSF by \(\theta/p\) pixels (\(p\) = plate scale), shift-invariance of the diffraction-limited image.
  • Tolerance: perturbations.vibration: shift_rtol 0.005 and shift_atol_px 0.01 px (absolute floor, as zero shift is exactly zero), set by the accuracy of the peak estimator on 1 to 2 px shifts.
  • References: none specific.

docs.title: test_vibration_wraps_with_different_length_series
docs.text:
• Module: Vibration.getCurrentVibrations (indexing).
  • Tier: nightly. Parametrised over \((L_x, L_y)\) = (5, 8) x_shorter, (8, 5) y_shorter, (6, 6) equal.
  • What it checks: with series of different length iteration \(k\) must give \((x[k \bmod L], y[k \bmod L])\) with \(L=\min(L_x,L_y)\) and never raise. The tilts fitted by least squares to the injected OPD over the pupil coordinates are compared with the file sample (scale calibrated at iteration 0), over \(2\max(L_x,L_y)+1\) iterations. Convention/indexing check.
  • Tolerance: perturbations.vibration.index_rtol = \(10^{-9}\) on the maximum error relative to the largest file value (float64 arithmetic).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_vibration_psd_equals_file_psd
docs.text:
• Module: Vibration + LightPath + ScienceCam.
  • Tier: nightly.
  • What it checks: a 1024-step series at 1 kHz (three tones at 37, 112, 251 Hz plus AR(1) noise, rms 0.3 px in \(x\) and 0.2 px in \(y\) delayed by 100 samples) is injected; the camera peak series (8x upsampling) has the file periodogram: band-integrated power in 8 equal bands up to 500 Hz, and rms, ratio to the file equal 1.
  • Theory / assumptions: since the image-motion to peak map is linear and exact to a factor \(1/p\), the camera series is the file series up to scale, and so is its PSD (periodogram \(|\mathrm{FFT}|^2\) with no windowing, same samples).
  • Tolerance: perturbations.vibration.psd_rtol = 0.01 (estimator error of a linear map).
  • References: none specific.

docs.title: test_localseeing_opd_equals_file_with_wraparound
docs.text:
• Module: LocalSeeing, LightPath.localSeeing_opd, LightPath.sci_opd.
  • Tier: nightly.
  • What it checks: for a random OPD cube (32x32x5 frames, rms 0.1 um), the OPD injected at iteration \(k\) is frame \(k \bmod T\) (including beyond \(T\), over \(2T+3\) iterations) both as localSeeing_opd and in the science OPD (file times pupil; no atmosphere, DM or NCPA).
  • Tolerance: perturbations.localseeing.exact = 0 (bit equality, since the OPD is copied).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_localseeing_resolution_mismatch_is_bilinear_resampling
docs.text:
• Module: LocalSeeing (resampling of a file at a different resolution).
  • Tier: nightly.
  • What it checks: a 64x64 file used with a 32 px pupil is resampled to the 2x2 block mean times the pupil: halving a grid by bilinear interpolation at pixel centres is the 2x2 mean.
  • Theory / assumptions: pixel centres of the coarse grid lie at the centre of 2x2 blocks of the fine grid, so linear interpolation averages the four neighbours with equal weights.
  • Tolerance: perturbations.localseeing.resize_rtol = \(10^{-6}\) (relative to the maximum; cv2 float32 arithmetic).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_localseeing_input_not_modified_by_interaction_matrix_propagate
docs.text:
• Module: LocalSeeing.localSeeing_input, LightPath.propagate(interaction_matrix=True).
  • Tier: nightly.
  • What it checks: the user's OPD sequence is data: after a normal step and an interaction-matrix step (which suppresses the path disturbances) the stored input is unchanged and still equals the file, and the next normal step injects file frame 0. The interaction-matrix propagate does not zero or overwrite the user's array in place.
  • Tolerance: exact (0).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_spider_removed_area
docs.text:
• Module: Telescope.apply_spiders.
  • Tier: nightly. Parametrised over arm-angle sets cardinal [0, 90, 180, 270], diagonal [45, 135, 225, 315], non_cardinal [20, 140, 260], rotated [17, 107, 197, 287], near_cardinal [357, 87, 177, 267] (deg); \(N\) = 256 px, \(D\) = 8 m, obstruction 0.3, arm width \(w\) = 0.8 m (25.6 px).
  • What it checks: the number of pixels removed from the pupil by the arms against the exact area of the half-strips inside the annulus; also records the count of an independent mask at zero offset.
  • Theory / assumptions: the area of one half-strip \(|t|<w/2\), \(s>0\) inside \(R_{co}\le r\le R\) is \(A(R)-A(R_{co})\) with
\[A(r) = \tfrac{w}{2}\sqrt{r^2-\tfrac{w^2}{4}} + r^2\arcsin\!\frac{w}{2r},\]

so \(n\) arms remove \(n[A(R)-A(R_{co})]/p^2\) pixels (\(p=D/N\)), approximately \(n\,w\,(R-R_{co})/p^2\). Arms aligned with the lattice are quantised deterministically for any implementation centred on the array. - Tolerance: absolute, the larger of \(3.5\sigma\) (perturbations.spider.sigma_mult) of the pixel count of the independent mask over 64 random sub-pixel offsets (n_lattice) and the deviation of that mask's count at zero offset from the exact area. - References: none.

docs.title: test_spider_arm_angles
docs.text:
• Module: Telescope.apply_spiders.
  • Tier: nightly. Parametrised over the same five arm-angle sets.
  • What it checks: that the number of arms found equals the requested number, and that the direction of each removed region (principal axis of its connected component, pointing away from the centre, counter-clockwise from +x with y = +row) matches the requested angles; the estimator is first validated on the independent mask.
  • Tolerance: perturbations.spider.angle_deg = 1.0 deg (the estimator measured less than 0.2 deg on the independent mask; margin for the grid).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_spider_single_arm_is_one_half_strip
docs.text:
• Module: Telescope.apply_spiders.
  • Tier: nightly. Parametrised over angle = 30, 0, 357 deg.
  • What it checks: one arm removes a single connected half-strip beyond the central obstruction (count of connected components = 1). An arm whose direction lies just below a multiple of 90 deg (357 deg) is also a single piece.
  • Tolerance: exact (one component).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_spider_psf_spikes_perpendicular_to_arms
docs.text:
• Module: Telescope.apply_spiders, ScienceCam.compute_psf.
  • Tier: nightly.
  • What it checks: for two perpendicular arms at 20 and 110 deg (\(N\) = 128, \(D\) = 4 m, obstruction 0.1, \(w\) = 0.1 m, 4 px per \(\lambda/D\)) the azimuthal profile of the SAOS PSF over the annulus 2.5 to 7 \(\lambda/D\) (normalised to unit mean, 3 deg smoothing) is compared with that of the independent FFT of an independently built mask. The rms profile difference must be within the pixelisation floor, estimated by the same comparison between lattices displaced by 32 random sub-pixel offsets. The mirrored-arm case and the spike azimuths are recorded only.
  • Theory / assumptions: by Fourier optics the PSF is \(|\mathcal F\{P\}|^2\); a thin strip of width \(w\) produces a sinc-like spike perpendicular to its length, on both sides of the centre, so the two arms give four spikes at 20, 110, 200 and 290 deg.
  • Tolerance: rms difference \(\le \overline{d}_{floor} + 3.5\,\sigma_{floor}\) (perturbations.spider.sigma_mult).
  • References: Hardy 1998 (Fourier optics of pupils with struts, generic).

docs.title: test_ncpa_load_same_shape_round_trip
docs.text:
• Module: NCPA.load, NCPA.getPhase.
  • Tier: nightly.
  • What it checks: a 32x32 OPD file with the pupil shape is returned by getPhase after load (which returns True).
  • Tolerance: perturbations.ncpa.float32_rtol = \(10^{-6}\) of the maximum (the NCPA buffer is float32).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_ncpa_load_resized_file_is_bilinear_resampling
docs.text:
• Module: NCPA.load.
  • Tier: nightly.
  • What it checks: a 64x64 file used with a 32 px pupil is resampled to the 2x2 block mean (same reasoning as for LocalSeeing).
  • Tolerance: perturbations.ncpa.resize_rtol = \(10^{-6}\) of the maximum.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_ncpa_enters_science_path_not_wfs_path
docs.text:
• Module: NCPA.setOPD, LightPath.propagate (sci_opd, wfs_opd, slopes_1D), ShackHartmann, ScienceCam.
  • Tier: nightly.
  • What it checks: a tilt NCPA of 0.05 arcsec, per the LightPath documentation \(\mathrm{wfs\_opd}=\mathrm{atm}+\mathrm{vib}+\mathrm{LS}+\mathrm{DM}\) and \(\mathrm{sci\_opd}=\mathrm{wfs\_opd}+\mathrm{NCPA}\): (i) moves the science image by \(\theta/p\) px along +col (and 0 along rows, within 0.01 px), (ii) leaves a 4x4 Shack-Hartmann slope vector bit-equal to the case without NCPA, (iii) gives \(\mathrm{sci\_opd}=(\mathrm{wfs\_opd}+\mathrm{NCPA})\cdot\mathrm{pupil}\) exactly.
  • Tolerance: perturbations.ncpa.shift_rtol = 0.005 for the shift; perturbations.ncpa.exact = 0 for the slopes and OPD identity; 0.01 px (hard-coded) for the orthogonal shift.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_exit_after_exception_with_logger_none
docs.text:
• Module: Telescope, Source, LightPath, LoggingHelper with logger=None (shared logging queue and its thread at interpreter exit).
  • Tier: nightly. Parametrised over name = telescope, lightpath_source, logginghelper.
  • What it checks: a subprocess that creates the objects and then raises RuntimeError exits by itself with status 1 and prints the traceback within the timeout (a hang is killed and counts as failure).
  • Tolerance: perturbations.logging.exit_timeout_s = 10 s.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_logger_none_prints_each_message_once
docs.text:
• Module: LoggingHelper with several objects using logger=None.
  • Tier: nightly.
  • What it checks: in a subprocess with a Telescope, Source and LightPath created with logger=None, a warning is printed exactly once, the process exits by itself with status 0, and no "Exception ignored in" message appears from __del__ at exit.
  • Tolerance: exact counts; timeout 10 s (perturbations.logging.exit_timeout_s).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_lgs_source_not_implemented
docs.text:
• Module: Source.__init__.
  • Tier: nightly. Parametrised over altitude = 90 km, Na_profile, FWHM_spot_up = 1.0, laser_coordinates = [1.0, 0.0].
  • What it checks: any laser-guide-star parameter raises NotImplementedError (message matching "Laser guide stars"), never a silent natural guide star. Laser guide stars are not implemented.
  • Tolerance: exception raised (no numerical criterion).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_savepoint.py — Saved metrics and HDF5 output
docs.text:
Source: tests/test_savepoint.py

Covers SAOS.Savepoint (compute_stats, save, add_metadata, module_metadata) and the HDF5 files it writes. Savepoint.compute_stats is fed synthetic data with a known answer: OPD maps, slope vectors, PSFs computed in the test by an independent zero-padded FFT (theory.psf_reference) and small solar-like images. The HDF5 round trip and the saving cadence use a small LightPath (32 px telescope, ScienceCam at 2 px per \(\lambda/D\) with n_pix = res, so no pupil resampling) whose atmosphere is a stub returning prescribed band-limited OPDs; files go to pytest's tmp_path. Many checks are exact comparisons (rtol \(10^{-12}\) or equality) because they verify bookkeeping and statistics, not physics. All tests are marked fast (module-level). Tolerances: tolerances/savepoint.yaml (calibrated 2026-10-26, develop a243eb4, CPU, fixed seeds).

Strehl definition used as reference in the Strehl tests: for a high-order phase without tilt the on-axis ratio equals the coherent energy of the pupil phase,

\[ S=\left|\langle e^{i\phi}\rangle_{P}\right|^2, \]

(exact for the sampled phase); the Maréchal approximation \(S\approx e^{-\sigma_\phi^2}\) is not used by the tests.

docs.title: test_opd_statistics
docs.text:
• Module: Savepoint.compute_stats with data type 'opd'.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: min, max, mean, std (piston-removed rms, the WFE) and rms of an OPD map are computed over the pupil pixels only. The test map is an asymmetric ramp plus offset plus a Gaussian bump in one quadrant with large values (1e-3) outside the pupil, so any statistic taken outside the mask is wrong.
  • Theory / assumptions: none (direct computation over the pupil mask).
  • Tolerance: ratio to direct numpy value equal to 1 with rtol = \(10^{-12}\) (hard-coded).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_slopes_1d_statistics_split_xy
docs.text:
• Module: Savepoint.compute_stats with 'slopes_1D'.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: for \(\mathrm{slopes\_1D}=[x\ (n),\ y\ (n)]\) the min, max, mean, std and rms are reported per axis as [[x, y]], equal to numpy statistics of each half (40 slopes per axis with different means 3 and -1).
  • Theory / assumptions: layout convention of the slope vector.
  • Tolerance: rtol = \(10^{-12}\).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_slopes_2d_statistics_split_xy
docs.text:
• Module: Savepoint.compute_stats with 'slopes_2D'.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: for a 2D map \([x\text{ block }(n\text{ rows});\ y\text{ block }(n\text{ rows})]\) as saved by LightPath, min and max per axis are correct (Savepoint expands 2D data to 3D).
  • Theory / assumptions: layout convention.
  • Tolerance: rtol = \(10^{-12}\).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_strehl_known_phase
docs.text:
• Module: Savepoint.compute_stats with 'sci_frame' (strehl).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: for 9 PSFs (rms 0.3, 0.6, 0.9 rad x 3 realisations, SR 0.45-0.92) of a high-order phase (PSD \(f^{-11/3}\) above 4 cycles/\(D\), no tilt), computed by independent FFT at Nyquist (2 px per \(\lambda/D\)) in a wide field (32 \(\lambda/D\)), the saved Strehl equals \(|\langle e^{i\phi}\rangle|^2\) over the pupil.
  • Theory / assumptions: exact Strehl of the sampled phase; no tilt so that the peak pixel is at the centre; the field edge plays no role.
  • Tolerance: strehl.known_phase_rtol = 0.03 (peak-pixel SR at Nyquist sampling).
  • References: none specific.

docs.title: test_strehl_subpixel_tilt
docs.text:
• Module: Savepoint.compute_stats (strehl, peak search).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: a pure tilt does not change the Strehl: a diffraction-limited PSF shifted by 0.25 and 0.5 px in both axes at Nyquist sampling scores SR = 1.
  • Theory / assumptions: tilt does not change the PSF shape; the sub-pixel peak must be found by interpolation.
  • Tolerance: strehl.tilt_rtol = 0.02.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_strehl_in_field_convention
docs.text:
• Module: Savepoint.compute_stats (strehl).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: documents the convention that the saved Strehl is the measured SR in the camera field. For a 1 rad rms high-order phase and fields of 32 \(\lambda/D\) and 6 \(\lambda/D\) the saved value must equal \(SR_{peak}\,f_0/f\). Independent terms: \(SR_{peak}\) is the maximum of the aberrated PSF sampled 16x finer (unit ideal peak); \(f/f_0\) from the independent frames' sums. The exact \(|\langle e^{i\phi}\rangle|^2\) is recorded.
  • Theory / assumptions:
\[ SR=\frac{I_{peak}/E_{field}}{I^{ideal}_{peak}/E^{ideal}_{field}}=SR_{peak}\,\frac{f_0}{f}, \]

with \(f\) and \(f_0\) the fractions of the total energy inside the field for the aberrated and ideal PSF. Frames carry unit energy in the field, hence the explicit ratio of sums. - Tolerance: strehl.convention_rtol = 0.002 (1/32 px interpolation grid of the sub-pixel peak vs the 16x oversampled reference peak). - References: none.

docs.title: test_contrast_and_mfgs
docs.text:
• Module: Savepoint.compute_stats for solar frames (contrast, MFGS).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: contrast \(=\sigma/\mu\): \(1+a\sin(2\pi m x/N)\) over whole periods gives \(a/\sqrt2\); a constant image gives 0. MFGS (mean fraction of gradient similarity) of a deterministic \(12\times12\) texture (smooth waves, a hot pixel, a pseudo-random pattern at amplitudes 0, 0.05, 0.3) equals the independent loop implementation mfgs_reference, and both contrast and MFGS are invariant to image scale (scales 1, \(10^{-6}\), \(10^6\), as frames are saved in photons or DN). The median-filter border is extended symmetrically.
  • Theory / assumptions: MFGS definition as implemented in the reference: image divided by its mean; \(M\) = \(3\times3\) median filter (symmetric border); Sobel-like gradient with kernel \([[-3,0,3],[-10,0,10],[-3,0,3]]\) (Scharr) and its transpose, magnitude \(g=\sqrt{g_x^2+g_y^2}\);
\[ \mathrm{MFGS}=\Big\langle\frac{2\,g_I\,g_M+C}{g_I^2+g_M^2+C}\Big\rangle_{\rm pixels},\quad C=10^{-10}. \]
  • Tolerance: contrast \(a/\sqrt2\) and constant image: rtol = \(10^{-12}\) / atol = \(10^{-12}\); MFGS and contrast vs reference: rtol = \(10^{-9}\) (hard-coded).
  • References: none specific (no citation in the test).

docs.title: test_mfgs_constant_image
docs.text:
• Module: Savepoint.compute_stats (MFGS).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: an image without structure has no gradients, so every pixel is "similar" and MFGS = 1 (for constants 3.7 and \(10^5\)).
  • Theory / assumptions: \(C\) regularises \(0/0\) in the similarity formula.
  • Tolerance: atol = \(10^{-12}\).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_hdf5_roundtrip
docs.text:
• Module: Savepoint.save through LightPath.propagate; HDF5 groups atm_opd, sci_opd, sci_frame_shortExp.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: over 6 iterations, the saved data equal what was physically injected: atmosphere OPD per direction (the stub OPD, iteration index), science OPD (equal to the OPD on the pupil mask and zero outside), std over the pupil, 6 short-exposure frames equal to the independent FFT frame (unit energy in the field), and the saved Strehl per frame equal to the exact \(|\langle e^{2\pi i\,\mathrm{OPD}/\lambda}\rangle|^2\). The OPDs are band-limited to 4-7 cycles/\(D\) with 0.6 rad rms so the halo stays inside the \(\pm8\lambda/D\) field.
  • Theory / assumptions: exact Strehl of the sampled phase; frames from the independent Fraunhofer FFT.
  • Tolerance: OPD maps \(\le10^{-15}\) m; std rtol = \(10^{-9}\); frame_atol = \(10^{-6}\) of the peak (same computation, float precision); strehl.known_phase_rtol = 0.03.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_saved_frames_match_decimation
docs.text:
• Module: Savepoint.save, ScienceCam(decimation), LightPath.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: with the camera decimated by 3 and frames saved every 3 iterations, the 4 frames taken in 12 iterations (at iterations 2, 5, 8, 11, i.e. \((i+1)\%3==0\), the Savepoint convention) are saved with the iteration index of the OPD they come from and the content of the independent FFT frame of that OPD.
  • Theory / assumptions: cadence convention; frames from independent FFT.
  • Tolerance: frame_atol = \(10^{-6}\) of the peak; count and indices exact.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_metadata_provenance_and_config
docs.text:
• Module: Savepoint metadata (/metadata group, add_metadata, light-path group attributes).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: /metadata holds the SAOS version (equal to SAOS.__version__), provenance (Python version, host, command line, creation and last-saved times, Savepoint settings JSON), last_iteration updated at each save, user metadata from the constructor and add_metadata() (lists, strings, dicts as JSON), the telescope configuration (D, resolution, spiders 'none'), and light-path attributes (source wavelength, delay, science camera plate scale).
  • Theory / assumptions: I/O and bookkeeping only.
  • Tolerance: exact equality.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_metadata_large_values_as_datasets
docs.text:
• Module: Savepoint metadata storage.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: user metadata above the attribute size limit (a 10000-element float array, 80 kB, above the 64 kB HDF5 object-header limit) is stored as a dataset of /metadata/user without failure, and small values stay attributes.
  • Theory / assumptions: HDF5 attribute-size limit (I/O only).
  • Tolerance: exact.
  • References: HDF5 documentation (attribute size limit), implicit.

docs.title: test_metadata_of_modules
docs.text:
• Module: SAOS.Savepoint.module_metadata for Telescope, Atmosphere, DeformableMirror.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: the returned dictionaries carry the parameters the modules were created with: telescope spider angles and thickness (and 'none' after set_pupil), atmosphere \(r_0\), \(L_0\), altitudes, wind speeds, zenith in degrees, DM nActs, nValidAct, altitude and misregistration entries; the dictionary is JSON-serialisable.
  • Theory / assumptions: none (metadata round trip).
  • Tolerance: exact (zenith rtol = \(10^{-12}\)).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_sciencecam.py — Science camera PSF and long-exposure accumulation
docs.text:
Source: tests/test_sciencecam.py

Covers SAOS.ScienceCam (compute_psf, get_frame, plate scale and field resampling) and the long-exposure accumulation done by SAOS.LightPath (sci_frame, long_exposure_frame). ScienceCam is driven directly with synthetic phases (no atmosphere or DM); the long-exposure tests use a LightPath whose "atmosphere" is a stub (StubAtmosphere) returning a prescribed OPD sequence, so the accumulation is tested in isolation. The validation strategy is comparison with an independent noise-free reference: \(|{\rm FFT}|^2\) of the zero-padded pupil sampled at fw pixels per \(\lambda/D\) (theory.psf_reference), cropped to the camera field and normalised to unit energy, plus closed-form results (Airy pattern, tilt-to-shift, Strehl of a sampled phase). Conventions: frames are [row, col]; a phase ramp increasing along columns moves the image towards +col; pixel n_pix//2 is the optical axis. Tolerances are in tolerances/sciencecam.yaml, calibrated 2026-10-26 (develop a243eb4, CPU) as a few times the measured deviation. All tests are marked fast (module-level).

Far-field model used by the PSF tests (Fraunhofer, Goodman; discrete implementation as a zero-padded FFT):

\[ \mathrm{PSF}(\boldsymbol\theta)=\left|\mathcal F\{P(\mathbf x)\,e^{i\phi(\mathbf x)}\}\right|^2,\qquad \text{pixel scale}=\frac{\lambda}{N_{pad}\,dx}. \]

docs.title: test_airy_psf_unobstructed
docs.text:
• Module: ScienceCam.get_frame / compute_psf.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: flat phase, unobstructed 64 px pupil, camera field sampled exactly like the pupil (n_pix = res, 4 px per \(\lambda/D\), no resampling). The frame has unit energy, peaks on the optical axis (within 0.02 px), FWHM equal to \(1.029\lambda/D\) (theory.airy_fwhm), first dark ring at \(1.220\lambda/D\) from the azimuthal mean of an 8x Fourier-upsampled frame, and a radial profile within a tolerance of the Airy law for \(r<2\lambda/D\).
  • Theory / assumptions: unobstructed circular aperture,
\[ \frac{I(x)}{I(0)}=\left[\frac{2J_1(\pi x)}{\pi x}\right]^2,\quad x=\theta D/\lambda, \]

FWHM \(=1.029\,\lambda/D\), first zero at \(x=1.220\). The pupil is pixelated at 64 px (a small bias against the continuous Airy pattern). - Tolerance: psf: fwhm_rtol = 0.01 (measured -0.15 %), first_zero_rtol = 0.02 (0.25 px radial bins), airy_profile_atol = 0.01 of the peak; energy rtol = \(10^{-12}\) (hard-coded). - References: Goodman, "Introduction to Fourier Optics".

docs.title: test_psf_obstructed_vs_reference
docs.text:
• Module: ScienceCam.get_frame for an obstructed pupil.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: with a 0.3 central obstruction, flat phase, n_pix = res, the frame equals the independent zero-padded FFT of the same pupil mask (theory.psf_reference, normalised to unit sum); compares the FWHM ratio and \(\max|{\rm frame}-{\rm ref}|/{\rm peak}\).
  • Theory / assumptions: same Fraunhofer model; SAOS and the reference should be the same computation when no resampling is needed.
  • Tolerance: psf.fwhm_rtol = 0.01; psf.reference_profile_atol = \(10^{-6}\) of the peak.
  • References: Goodman.

docs.title: test_psf_band_limited_beyond_nyquist
docs.text:
• Module: ScienceCam.compute_psf, ScienceCam._mft_kernel (band limit).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: a 64 px pupil (obstruction 0.3), 4 px per \(\lambda/D\) and a 384 px field, which extends to \(|u| = 0.75\) cycles per pupil sample. For a flat phase and for a high-order phase (1 rad rms, PSD \(f^{-11/3}\) above 4 cycles/D): pixels outside the Nyquist band are exactly zero, the PSF energy over the band is 1, and inside the band the PSF equals an independent zero-padded FFT of the same samples (one period).
  • Theory / assumptions: the transform of a field sampled at \(\Delta x\) is periodic with period \(1/\Delta x\); the band \(|u| \le 1/2\) holds exactly one period, so Parseval gives unit energy, and outside it there is no information.
  • Tolerance: sciencecam.band_limit: energy_atol and inside_atol \(10^{-10}\) (numerical precision: same samples, same transform).
