  • References: Bracewell, The Fourier Transform and Its Applications; Goodman, Introduction to Fourier Optics.

docs.title: test_image_motion_tilt
docs.text:
• Module: ScienceCam.get_frame (image motion, sign convention).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: phase ramps along x (columns) and y (rows) of 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6 \(\lambda/D\), camera sampled like the pupil. The peak (16x Fourier upsampling plus parabola) moves by \(\theta/\mathrm{plate\_scale}=\theta\cdot fw\) px on the tilted axis (ratio 1), with no motion on the other axis and positive ramp giving a positive pixel shift.
  • Theory / assumptions: Fourier shift theorem: \(\phi=2\pi\,t\,x/D\) gives a shift of \(t\,\lambda/D\) in the focal plane, i.e. \(t\,fw\) px; the peak estimator error is about 0.01 px for shifts of 2-24 px.
  • Tolerance: motion.shift_rtol = 0.003, motion.cross_axis_atol_px = 0.02 px.
  • References: Goodman.

docs.title: test_plate_scale_with_resampled_pupil
docs.text:
• Module: ScienceCam field resampling (n_pix != res).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: for n_pix = 160 and res = 64 (the typical case, e.g. EST red 555 px vs 216) a 4 \(\lambda/D\) tilt moves the image by 4 fw px and the FWHM equals \(1.029\lambda/D\), both within 0.2 %. The align_corners scale model \(n_{pix}(res-1)/((n_{pix}-1)res)\) is recorded as a metric only.
  • Theory / assumptions: requested plate scale must be the effective plate scale.
  • Tolerance: plate_scale.rtol = 0.002.
  • References: none specific.

docs.title: test_strehl_vs_native_grid
docs.text:
• Module: ScienceCam.compute_psf (Strehl after pupil-phase resampling).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: on-axis intensity of the PSF relative to the aberration-free one, for high-order phases (PSD \(f^{-11/3}\) above 8 cycles/\(D\), rms 0.5 and 0.9 rad, 4 realisations each, camera field \(n_{pix}=2.5\,res\)), equals the exact Strehl of the sampled phase on its native grid, averaged per rms.
  • Theory / assumptions: exact Strehl of the sampled phase over the pupil support,
\[ S=\left|\langle e^{i\phi}\rangle_{P}\right|^2 , \]

which is the on-axis value ratio (not the Maréchal approximation \(S\approx e^{-\sigma^2}\), which is not used for the criterion). The ratio of the mean SAOS SR to the mean exact SR (per rms) must be 1; the phase is resampled from the 64 px pupil grid to the camera pupil grid inside compute_psf. - Tolerance: strehl.sr_rtol = 0.02. - References: none specific; Strehl definition as in Roddier (ed.), "Adaptive Optics in Astronomy".

docs.title: test_long_exposure_frame_count
docs.text:
• Module: LightPath.propagate long-exposure logic with ScienceCam(integrationTime, decimation).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: parametrised over fs = 1000, 2000, 1500, 1800 Hz. A long exposure of \(T_{int}=k\cdot\mathrm{decimation}\cdot T_s\) (written as \(k/f_s\), as a user would) must accumulate exactly \(k\) short frames, for \(k=1..12\) with decimation 1 and \(k=1..6\) with decimation 2. The non-integer \(f_s\) values (1500, 1800) are the floating-point rounding cases.
  • Theory / assumptions: frame counting only.
  • Tolerance: exact (atol = 0).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_long_exposure_non_integral_ratio
docs.text:
• Module: LightPath.propagate long-exposure logic.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: when \(T_{int}\) is not a multiple of \(T_s\) the exposure is rounded up and never shorter than \(T_{int}\): 2.4 \(T_s\) gives 3 frames; 1/56 s at 2 kHz (35.7 \(T_s\)) gives 36 frames.
  • Theory / assumptions: convention (ceiling).
  • Tolerance: exact.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_long_exposure_mean_and_energy
docs.text:
• Module: LightPath long-exposure accumulation with ScienceCam.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: with random tilts per frame from the stub atmosphere (\(k=8\) frames, 32 px pupil, lightRatio 0.9), the noise-free long exposure equals the mean of the independent unit-energy short frames, scaled to the collected photons. Two criteria: total energy against \(\mathrm{flux}\cdot T_{int}\cdot A\cdot\text{throughput}\) and \(\max|{\rm LE}/{\rm photons}-\bar I_{ref}|/\mathrm{peak}\).
  • Theory / assumptions:
\[ \mathrm{LE}=\Phi\,T_{int}\,A_{pix}\,\eta\ \frac{1}{k}\sum_{n=1}^{k}I_n,\qquad \sum I_n=1, \]

\(A_{pix}\) the pixelated pupil area \(\sum P\,(D/res)^2\), \(\eta\) = lightRatio. Expected frames come from an independent FFT with the tilt ramp. - Tolerance: long_exposure.energy_rtol = \(10^{-10}\), long_exposure.mean_rtol = \(10^{-10}\). - References: none specific.

docs.title: test_long_exposure_gaussian_tilt
docs.text:
• Module: LightPath long-exposure accumulation with ScienceCam.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: Gaussian image motion (\(\sigma=0.8\lambda/D\) per axis) via a \(30\times30\) grid of Gaussian quantiles, 900 frames. (1) LE equals the mean of independent frames of the tilts actually used; (2) LE equals the independent diffraction-limited frame convolved with a Gaussian (FWHM ratio and \(\max|{\rm LE}-{\rm ref}|/\mathrm{peak}\)). The quadrature law \(\mathrm{FWHM}_{LE}^2=\mathrm{FWHM}_{DL}^2+(2.355\sigma)^2\) is reported only (approximate for an Airy core).
  • Theory / assumptions: random image motion with distribution \(p\) blurs the long exposure into \(\mathrm{PSF}_{DL}*p\); in Fourier space the Gaussian transfer function is \(\exp[-2(\pi\sigma f)^2]\) in the code's pixel units (\(\sigma_{px}=\sigma\,fw\)). The quantile grid approximates the continuous Gaussian to under 1 % (about 0.3 % in the grid itself).
  • Tolerance: long_exposure: discrete_profile_atol = \(10^{-3}\) (exact discrete comparison; measured 2e-4 at the FoV edge), gaussian_fwhm_rtol = 0.015, gaussian_profile_atol = 0.015.
  • References: none specific.

docs.title: test_sharepoint.py — ZMQ publisher and request client
docs.text:
Source: tests/test_sharepoint.py

Covers SAOS.Sharepoint (ZMQ PUB publisher, shareData) and SAOS.ReceptionPoint (ZMQ REQ client, sendRequest). These tests concern communication and bookkeeping, not physics: there is no theory or numerical tolerance. Sharepoint is fed with documented stubs (SimpleNamespace) exposing exactly the attributes shareData reads (light-path buffers, atmosphere layers, DM command vectors) filled with random data; a real SUB socket receives everything (slow-joiner handled by a handshake on a private sync topic). Expectations are independent of the implementation: payloads must be bit-equal (shape, dtype and values) to the published arrays and every topic must appear exactly at the iterations whose \((it+1)\) is a multiple of its decimation. ReceptionPoint is tested against a REP server thread. Each test uses its own random free local port and short timeouts, and always closes its sockets and contexts. All tests are marked fast (module-level). No tolerance yaml is used (exact comparisons).

Scheduling rule checked everywhere: a topic with decimation \(k>0\) is published at iteration \(it\) iff \((it+1)\bmod k=0\); a decimation of 0 disables it. Each call of shareData ends with a topics message that lists the topics configured for the iteration.

docs.title: test_atmosphere_layers_decimation
docs.text:
• Module: Sharepoint.shareData (atmosphere layers).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: with atm=3 and two atmospheres (2 and 1 layers), one topic per atmosphere/layer (atmosphere_<i>/layer_<j>) is published exactly at iterations 2, 5, 8 of 10, with payload bit-equal to the layer screen.
  • Theory / assumptions: none (scheduling and payload identity).

  • References: none.

docs.title: test_dm_command_decimation
docs.text:

  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: with dm=2 the topic dm_<i>/1D_command (valid actuators only, cmd_1D[validAct]) is published only at iterations 1, 3, 5 of 6.

  • References: none.

docs.title: test_dm_command_does_not_hijack_atmosphere_topic
docs.text:
• Module: Sharepoint.shareData.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: topic routing: with atm=1 and dm=2, at iteration 0 only the atmosphere topic is due, so only atmosphere_1/layer_1 is published with the atmosphere screen, and the DM command is not published under an atmosphere topic.

docs.title: test_lightpath_topics_decimation
docs.text:
• Module: Sharepoint.shareData (per light path topics).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: for two light paths and decimations (atm_per_dir=2, slopes=3, wfs=4, wfs_frame=5, sci=6, sci_frame=2) over 12 iterations, the set of topics (lightPath<i>/atmosphere_opd, atmosphere_phase, slopes_1D, slopes_2D, wfs_opd, wfs_phase, wfs_frame, sci_opd, sci_phase, sci_frame), their bit-equal payloads and publication iterations match the schedule rule at every iteration; sci_frame of light path 1 appears at 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 and wfs_frame of light path 0 at 4, 9.

docs.title: test_lightpath_payload_types_and_decimation_one
docs.text:
• Module: Sharepoint.shareData.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: with decimation 1 (slopes, sci_frame) topics are published every iteration (4 iterations) and the payload follows the current buffer values (the buffers are refreshed before each call).
  • Theory / assumptions: none.
  • Tolerance: exact.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_sections_absent_in_light_path_are_not_published
docs.text:
• Module: Sharepoint.shareData.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: a light path with atm, dm, wfs, sci set to None publishes nothing for those sections even with all the decimations enabled; the catalogue is empty.
  • Theory / assumptions: none.
  • Tolerance: exact.

docs.title: test_disabled_decimations_publish_nothing
docs.text:
• Module: Sharepoint.shareData.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: with all decimations at 0 no data topic is published over 3 iterations (only the empty topics message), even with atmosphere and DM objects supplied.
  • Theory / assumptions: none.
  • Tolerance: exact.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_topics_catalogue
docs.text:
• Module: Sharepoint.shareData (final topics message).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: the topics message lists the configured topics in publication order at every iteration (5 iterations) with two light paths and an atmosphere with two layers, regardless of whether each topic is due at that iteration (decimations atm=2, slopes=3, wfs=1, sci_frame=4).
  • Theory / assumptions: catalogue lists configured, not just due, topics.
  • Tolerance: exact list equality.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_dm_per_dir_phase_topic_sends_phase
docs.text:
• Module: Sharepoint.shareData (dm_per_dir with several directions).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: with dm_per_dir=2 and 3 directions (3D DM buffers), dm_opd_<j> carries dm_opd[j] and dm_phase_<j> carries dm_phase[j] for \(j=1..3\) at the due iterations, nothing otherwise. The phase topic carries the phase buffer, not the OPD buffer.
  • Theory / assumptions: none.

docs.title: test_dm_per_dir_single_direction_phase_topic
docs.text:
• Module: Sharepoint.shareData (dm_per_dir, one direction).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: with one direction (2D buffers) and dm_per_dir=1, topics lightPath0/dm_opd and lightPath0/dm_phase are published, each carrying its own buffer.
  • Theory / assumptions: none.
  • Tolerance: exact.

docs.title: test_dm_per_dir_single_direction_decimation
docs.text:
• Module: Sharepoint.shareData (dm_per_dir, one direction).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: with dm_per_dir=3 and one direction, nothing is published at iterations 0, 1, 3, 4, and both topics at 2 and 5.
  • Theory / assumptions: none (the decimation must also apply in the single-direction branch).
  • Tolerance: exact.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_reception_actuator_cmd_roundtrip
docs.text:
• Module: ReceptionPoint.sendRequest('actuator_cmd').
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: the request sent is the pickled string 'actuator_cmd' and the 37-element answer comes back bit-equal.
  • Theory / assumptions: none.
  • Tolerance: exact.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_reception_loop_cmd_state_tracking
docs.text:
• Module: ReceptionPoint.sendRequest('loop_cmd').
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: the request payload carries buffer_type and the previous state (-1 at the first request, then the last desired state), and the result is int(desired_state); three requests answered 1, 0, 1 produce requests with actual_state -1, 1, 0.
  • Theory / assumptions: none (protocol state tracking).
  • Tolerance: exact.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_reception_unsupported_type_returns_none
docs.text:
• Module: ReceptionPoint.sendRequest.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: an unknown buffer type, or no argument, returns None and nothing is sent to the server.
  • Theory / assumptions: none.
  • Tolerance: exact.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_reception_timeout_returns_none_and_recovers
docs.text:
• Module: ReceptionPoint.sendRequest (timeout and recovery).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: parametrised over buffer_type = actuator_cmd, loop_cmd. With no server the request returns None after the timeout (300 ms, bounded time); once a REP server is started on a new port and the socket rebuilt, the next request succeeds with the expected answer.
  • Theory / assumptions: none (ZMQ REQ/REP lock-step must recover from a timeout by rebuilding the socket).
  • Tolerance: exact.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_reception_poller_only_holds_live_socket
docs.text:
• Module: ReceptionPoint (poller and socket rebuild).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: after a timeout the socket is rebuilt and the poller holds exactly the current socket and none of the closed ones.
  • Theory / assumptions: none.
  • Tolerance: exact.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_reception_second_timeout_returns_none_in_bounded_time
docs.text:
• Module: ReceptionPoint.sendRequest.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: three consecutive timeouts (200 ms each) each return None within a thread deadline of 4 s, so a hang is reported as a failure instead of blocking the suite.
  • Theory / assumptions: none.
  • Tolerance: thread deadline 4 s; results [None, None, None].
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_timing.py — loop latency: impulse response of the AO chain (T1)
docs.text:
Source: tests/test_timing.py

Covers the time structure of the closed loop built from SAOS.LightPath (delay \(d\), propagate(temporal_tick=True)), SAOS.ShackHartmann (6x6 subapertures, 48 px pupil), SAOS.InteractionMatrixHandler (zernike IM), SAOS.Controller (tikhonov reconstructor, leaky integrator, 12 modes, delay = \(d+1\)) and SAOS.DeformableMirror (7x7 actuators, updateDMShape). The atmosphere is replaced by a stand-in object whose getOPD returns a prescribed OPD. The strategy is an impulse-response experiment: a one-frame tilt is injected at frame \(k_0\) and the run with the impulse minus the run without it is examined, which removes the constant WFS offset. The test is fast.

Loop definition used as expectation (SAOS convention, from the docstring): the WFS measures frame \(k\); computeControlAction reads the measurement of frame \(k-d\); updateDMShape makes the command shape the DM seen by the WFS from frame \(k+1\) on. Hence the first change of the controller output is at call \(k_0+d\) and the first change of the DM OPD in the WFS path is at frame \(k_0+d+1\), a total pure delay of \(d+1\) frames.

docs.title: test_impulse_latency_is_delay_plus_one
docs.text:
• Module: LightPath.propagate with delay, Controller.computeControlAction (delay = d + 1), DeformableMirror.updateDMShape(dynamicResponse=False); helper chain fixture builds the IM.
  • Tier: fast. Parametrised over the light-path delay delay = 0, 1, 2 frames (\(K_0\) = 4, \(K\) = 14 frames, gain 0.5, leaky decay 0.9).
  • What it checks: with the full signed difference arrays (impulse run minus no-impulse run): slopes before frame \(k_0\), controller outputs before call \(k_0+d\) and DM OPD maps before frame \(k_0+d+1\) are exactly zero; slopes at \(k_0\), controller output at \(k_0+d\) and the DM OPD map at \(k_0+d+1\) exceed a small floor; the DM OPD map at \(k_0+d+1\) equals an independent Gaussian-actuator DM model applied to the controller output of call \(k_0+d\); and the pupil-mean \(x\)-gradient of that map equals \(-g\) times the injected gradient.
  • Theory / assumptions: independent DM model with Gaussian influence functions, mechanical coupling 0.6 at one pitch, partition of unity:
\[\mathrm{OPD}(\mathbf x) = \frac{\sum_a c_a\,g_a(\mathbf x)}{\sum_a g_a(\mathbf x)},\qquad g_a(\mathbf x) = \exp\!\left[\ln(0.6)\,\frac{|\mathbf x-\mathbf x_a|^2}{p^2}\right],\]

with \(p = D/(n_{act}-1)\) and valid actuators within \(D/2 + p/2\). For a pure tilt that the 12 modes represent and a leaky integrator of gain \(g\) at the first response frame, the correction is \(-g\) times the injected tilt gradient (OPD tilt 2 nm per px, about 0.1 px of spot shift). The slope baseline is assumed to cancel in the difference. - Tolerance: timing.latency: zero_atol 0.0 (exact zeros), signal_min \(10^{-12}\) (response must exceed it), model_rel \(10^{-9}\) (DM OPD against independent model, float64), gain_atol 0.05 (the gain statement ignores the edge droop of the Gaussian-actuator tilt, which is 6.5 % in the edge annulus fit, see test_dm; measured 0.018). - References: none specific (loop-delay convention of SAOS).

docs.title: test_wfs.py — Shack-Hartmann (point source) validation
docs.text:
Source: tests/test_wfs.py

Covers SAOS.ShackHartmann (wfs_measure, get_subaps, get_psf, subaperture validity logic, parameter validation) with a point source. The sensor has \(6\times6\) subapertures of \(d=0.1\) m over a 48 px pupil (8 phase px per subaperture), band R (640 nm), 2 px per \(\lambda/d\) unless stated, and is driven with synthetic phases; slopes are in detector pixels. The strategy is to compare against an independent reference written in the test file (propagate_cog): a direct Fourier sum of the continuous phase over the physical square subaperture (side \(d\), \(N_{ref}\) equal cells), evaluated at the detector pixel centres \(u_m=(m-(n-1)/2)/\mathrm{samp}\) in units of \(\lambda/d\), followed by the centre of gravity of the \(n\times n\) window. The reference does not use SAOS code or SAOS-measured quantities; the centroid window truncation is part of the reference, while the spot-motion scale \(k_{px}=\lambda/(2\pi p)\cdot 206265/\mathrm{plate\_scale}\) (\(p\) = phase pixel) is derived from the nominal geometry. The tolerance policy (header of tolerances/wfs.yaml) is that tolerances only cover the numerical precision of the reference or estimator statistics (about 3.5 sigma) and never absorb a measured SAOS discrepancy. All tests are marked fast (module-level pytestmark).

Common reference model. For a subaperture field \(E(\xi,\eta)=\exp[i\phi(\xi,\eta)]\) on \(\xi,\eta\in[-1/2,1/2]\), the far field sampled at window pixel \((m_x,m_y)\) is

\[ I(u_x,u_y)=\left|\frac{1}{M^2}\sum_{\xi,\eta}E(\xi,\eta)\,e^{-2\pi i(u_x\xi+u_y\eta)}\right|^2 , \]

and the ideal slope is the window centroid relative to the window centre,

\[ s_x=\frac{\sum_{m} (m-\tfrac{n-1}{2})\,I_m}{\sum_m I_m}. \]

A phase gradient \(g\) [rad/px] gives a spot shift \(k_{px}\,g\) pixels (small-angle approximation, flat-field, noise-free).

docs.title: test_tilt_axes_isotropy_cross_term
docs.text:
• Module: ShackHartmann.wfs_measure.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: a 0.3 px tilt along x on a square pupil gives positive x slopes, negligible y slopes (cross term), and the same response across all subapertures; a tilt along y gives the same response on the y slopes as x does on x (isotropy); a 30 deg tilt gives slopes whose angle is \(\arctan(\bar s_y/\bar s_x)=30^\circ\).
  • Theory / assumptions: slope = mean phase gradient converted to pixels, \(s=k_{px}\,g\); sign convention: positive phase gradient along +x gives a positive x slope. Linear regime, noise-free.
  • Tolerance: tilt_axes in wfs.yaml: cross term \(\le 10^{-3}\) (cross_max), isotropy \(10^{-4}\), uniformity (std/mean) \(10^{-3}\), angle 0.1 deg; all set by float32 FFT precision.
  • References: none specific.

docs.title: test_tilt_scale_vs_exact_geometry
docs.text:
• Module: ShackHartmann.wfs_measure (angular scale of the sensor, window sampling).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: parametrised over fov_px = 15, 30. A 0.05 px tilt gives a mean slope that must equal the ideal window centroid from tilt_cog (ratio 1). It also records \(N\) (samples across the subaperture) and \(N/(N-1)\) as metrics.
  • Theory / assumptions: ideal centroid of the Fourier-sum reference for the nominal motion \(k_{px}g\); sampled reference with \(N\) cells differs from the continuum by a few tenths of a percent.
  • Tolerance: scale_atol = 0.01 on the ratio (the reference sampled with \(N\) cells differs from the continuum by 0.7 % at \(N=15\) and 0.2 % at \(N=31\) at the largest shift, per the yaml comment).
  • References: none specific.

docs.title: test_reference_converged
docs.text:
• Module: none from SAOS; tests the reference (tilt_cog / propagate_cog).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: for shifts 0.05, 0.5, 2, 5 px, the ideal centroid computed with \(N=31\) cells differs from the continuum (\(M=1024\) cells) by less than the absolute-slope tolerance; the errors at \(N\), \(2N\), \(4N\) are recorded and plotted (expected \(\propto 1/N^2\)).
  • Theory / assumptions: midpoint-rule quadrature of the Fourier sum converges as \(1/N^2\).
  • Tolerance: absolute.rtol = \(5\times10^{-3}\) on the maximum relative error with \(N\) cells (measured \(\le 0.2\) %).
  • References: none specific.

docs.title: test_linearity_sweep
docs.text:
• Module: ShackHartmann.wfs_measure (full response curve of the centroid).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: for 18 log-spaced spot motions from 0.01 to 6 px, both signs, 31 px window, the mean x slope satisfies \(|s-s_{ref}|\le \mathrm{atol}+\mathrm{rtol}|s_{ref}|\) against the ideal window centroid for the nominal motion (no normalisation by the SAOS small-signal gain). The normalised gain curves are recorded as diagnostics only (not asserted).
  • Theory / assumptions: ideal windowed centroid, including window truncation at large shifts.
  • Tolerance: absolute.rtol = \(5\times10^{-3}\), absolute.atol = \(10^{-3}\) px (float32 FFT / centroid precision); the combined ratio must be \(\le 1\).
  • References: none specific.

docs.title: test_spot_centred_in_window
docs.text:
• Module: ShackHartmann.get_subaps, wfs_measure (window positioning).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: parametrised over fov_px = 15, 16 (odd and even windows). With a flat phase the centre of gravity of the first subaperture image sits at \((n-1)/2\) in x.
  • Theory / assumptions: an ideal sensor puts the zero-tilt spot at the window centre; this is the origin of the slope definition.
  • Tolerance: centring_atol = 0.05 px.
  • References: none specific.

docs.title: test_odd_symmetry_all_pixels
docs.text:
• Module: ShackHartmann.wfs_measure, centroid on all pixels.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: with an odd 15 px window and all pixels used, the response is odd, \(|s(+\theta)+s(-\theta)|/|s(+\theta)-s(-\theta)|\) stays below the bound for shifts 0.05, 0.5, 1.5, 3 px, and the small-signal gain at 0.002 px equals that at 0.05 px (continuity at zero).
  • Theory / assumptions: symmetric window and symmetric spot imply odd centroid response.
  • Tolerance: symmetry.asym_max = 0.005 (0.5 %); symmetry.continuity_atol = 0.002 on the gain ratio.
  • References: none specific.

docs.title: test_continuity_default_brightest
docs.text:
• Module: ShackHartmann.wfs_measure with use_brightest=50.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: the small-signal gain at \(\pm0.002\) px equals the gain at \(+0.05\) px, and the gain at \(-0.05\) px equals that at \(+0.05\) px (odd, linear). The weighted selection of the brightest pixels keeps the response continuous at zero shift for a point source.
  • Theory / assumptions: none beyond linearity and oddness.
  • Tolerance: symmetry.brightest_atol = 0.02 (2 %), larger than the all-pixel case because of the tie-break discontinuity.
  • References: none specific.

docs.title: test_defocus_astigmatism_relations
docs.text:
• Module: ShackHartmann.wfs_measure (linear response to quadratic phases).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: scale-free algebraic identities with \(c=5\times10^{-4}\) rad/px\(^2\): for defocus \(\phi=c(x^2+y^2)\) the x slopes are independent of the row and \(s_x[i,j]=s_y[j,i]\); for \(\phi=cxy\), \(s_x=s_y^{\mathrm{defocus}}/2\) and \(s_y=s_x^{\mathrm{defocus}}/2\); for \(\phi=c(x^2-y^2)\), \(s_x=s_x^{\mathrm{defocus}}\) and \(s_y=-s_y^{\mathrm{defocus}}\). Differences are normalised by the largest slope.
  • Theory / assumptions: slope proportional to the mean phase gradient over the subaperture, \(\partial_x\phi=2cx\) (defocus), \(cy\) (astigmatism). Identities hold for any common scale, so they say nothing about absolute response (tested in test_quadratic_phase_absolute_slopes). Small amplitude keeps spot motions below 0.1 px (linear range).
  • Tolerance: quadratic.rel_max = \(2\times10^{-3}\) relative to the largest slope.
  • References: none specific.

docs.title: test_quadratic_phase_absolute_slopes
docs.text:
• Module: ShackHartmann.wfs_measure.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: parametrised over mode in {defocus, astig_xy, astig_x2y2} and c in {0.002, 0.01, 0.03} rad/px\(^2\) (9 cases). The slopes of every subaperture must match quadratic_expected, which propagates each subaperture independently over the 31 px window, so the reference includes window truncation and phase curvature inside the subaperture (spot motions up to about 3.7 px).
  • Theory / assumptions: per-subaperture Fourier-sum centroid as above, phase \(a_{xx}x^2+a_{yy}y^2+a_{xy}xy\) about the pupil centre; subaperture centres are on the pupil grid (SUB_C).
  • Tolerance: \(|s-s_{ref}|\le\mathrm{atol}+\mathrm{rtol}|s_{ref}|\) with absolute.rtol = \(5\times10^{-3}\), absolute.atol = \(10^{-3}\) px.
  • References: none specific.

docs.title: test_defocus_subaperture_geometry
docs.text:
• Module: ShackHartmann subaperture grid geometry.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: for defocus with \(c=0.002\) the mean gradient over subaperture \(j\) is \(2cx_j\), so the profile of the slopes is affine in the pupil-grid centres \(x_j=n_pj+(n_p-1)/2-(\mathrm{res}-1)/2\). A line \(s_j=a x_j+b\) is fitted (scale \(a\) absorbed): the centre offset \(b/a\) and the maximum residual \(/a\) (pitch uniformity), in px of subaperture position, must be small, for both axes.
  • Theory / assumptions: \(\bar{\partial_x\phi}=2c\,x_j\), linear regime.
  • Tolerance: geometry.offset_atol = 0.05 px, geometry.pitch_atol = 0.05 px.
  • References: none specific.

docs.title: test_spot_fwhm
docs.text:
• Module: ShackHartmann.wfs_measure / get_subaps (spot shape and sampling).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: the flat-phase spot of a square subaperture, 4 px per \(\lambda/d\), 31 px window: the FWHM along x and y (band-limited upsampled cut through the peak, then half-maximum crossings) divided by \(0.8859\,\lambda/d\) equals 1.
  • Theory / assumptions: a square aperture of side \(d\) gives a \(\mathrm{sinc}^2(d\,\theta/\lambda)\) spot, with FWHM \(0.8859\,\lambda/d\) (not the \(1.03\lambda/D\) of a circular aperture).
  • Tolerance: fwhm_atol = 0.02 on the ratio.
  • References: Goodman, "Introduction to Fourier Optics" (Fraunhofer diffraction by a rectangular aperture).

docs.title: test_cog_photon_noise
docs.text:
• Module: ShackHartmann.wfs_measure with detector shot noise.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: with QE 1, 1 e-/DN, no readout or dark noise and all window pixels, the variance of the slopes over 120 frames (all valid subapertures, x and y) equals \(M_2/N_e\) for three flux levels (magnitude 2, 1, 0). \(M_2\) is the second central moment of the ideal spot computed in the test; \(N_e\) is the electron count measured in the noisy frames themselves, so photometric calibration is not involved.
  • Theory / assumptions: photon-noise-limited centre of gravity, \(\sigma_s^2=M_2/N_e\) with \(M_2=\sum(x-x_c)^2I/\sum I\). Valid for negligible per-pixel rounding at these fluxes.
  • Tolerance: photon_noise.ratio_atol = 0.053 on the ratio (8640 samples give \(\sigma(\mathrm{var})/\mathrm{var}=\sqrt{2/8640}=1.5\) %; band is 3.5 sigma).
  • References: none specific (standard photon-noise CoG variance, e.g. Rousset 1999 in Roddier, "Adaptive Optics in Astronomy").

docs.title: test_reference_slopes_averaged
docs.text:
• Module: ShackHartmann reference-slope computation (reference_slopes_maps, n_reference_frames).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: with noiseFlag=True the reference slopes are averaged over n_reference_frames (100) noisy frames, so \(\mathrm{rms}(\text{ref}_{noisy}-\text{ref}_{clean})=\sigma_1/\sqrt n\), where \(\sigma_1\) is the single-frame noise rms measured over 30 extra frames; checked as \(\sqrt n\cdot\mathrm{ratio}=1\).
  • Theory / assumptions: independent frame noise, so averaging reduces rms by \(\sqrt n\).
  • Tolerance: reference.n_sigma = 3.5: band \(1\pm 3.5/\sqrt{2M}\), \(M\) the number of valid slopes (estimator statistics).
  • References: none specific.

docs.title: test_partial_subaperture_energy
docs.text:
• Module: ShackHartmann validity of partial subapertures (valid_subapertures, get_psf).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: parametrised over pupil resolution 48, 96, 192 (ids res48, res96, res192; 8, 16, 32 px per subaperture). For a circular pupil with 20 % central obstruction and flat phase, the valid-subaperture map equals (fraction of pixels in the pupil \(\ge 0.5\)), and the energy of each valid subaperture image, relative to a fully illuminated one, equals the energy transmitted by the binary mask through that subaperture computed by an exact Fourier sum (partial_energy_discrepancy).
  • Theory / assumptions: the aperture contract: the pupil is a piecewise-constant binary mask, each pixel a uniform cell transmitted with unit amplitude; window energy = \(\sum|E_{far}|^2\) over the window. The reference uses at least 256 Fourier cells per subaperture to avoid aliasing (about 1 % error otherwise).
  • Tolerance: energy_atol = \(2\times10^{-3}\) (float32 FFT and exact Fourier-sum reference); the valid map must match exactly.
  • References: none specific.

docs.title: test_partial_energy_converges
docs.text:
• Module: same as above.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: the rms (over valid subapertures) of energy ratio \(-1\) is below the tolerance at each of the three pupil resolutions, i.e. the energy is a property of the aperture, not its sampling.
  • Theory / assumptions: as above.
  • Tolerance: energy_atol = \(2\times10^{-3}\).
  • References: none specific.

docs.title: test_undersampled_spot_rejected
docs.text:
• Module: ShackHartmann.__init__ parameter validation.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: a plate scale coarser than \(\lambda/d\) (samp=0.8, spot below 1 px) raises ValueError at construction.
  • Theory / assumptions: convention/validation only.
  • Tolerance: exception raised.
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_use_brightest_validated
docs.text:
• Module: ShackHartmann.__init__ / centroid selection (use_brightest).
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: parametrised with n = 0 (zero) and \(15^2+1\) (more_than_window). Out-of-range use_brightest must either raise ValueError at construction, or behave as all pixels: 0.3 px tilt slopes equal those of use_brightest = npix^2.
  • Theory / assumptions: validation only.
  • Tolerance: max slope difference \(\le 10^{-6}\) px (hard-coded).
  • References: none.

docs.title: test_unknown_kwarg_reported
docs.text:
• Module: ShackHartmann.__init__ keyword handling.
  • Tier: fast.
  • What it checks: a misspelt option (validSubapTreshold) must raise TypeError or log a warning that names it.
  • Theory / assumptions: validation only.
  • Tolerance: exception or warning present.
  • References: none.

docs.text:
